tools.name: add_custom_task_emoji
tools.description: Add one emoji to the workspace's custom task-emoji palette, so it becomes a one-click option in the on-card picker for everyone. Use when the user asks for an emoji the picker does not offer, or when you are establishing a labelling convention for a team (e.g. a duck for 'needs review by the data team'). Give it a `label` saying what it means in this workspace — an unlabelled emoji is a glyph nobody can interpret six weeks later. Adding one that is already in the set succeeds and reports that it was already there, so this is safe to call without checking first. Returns the next step, or a completion message when the runbook is finished.

tools.name: analyze_deal_data_room
tools.description: Read a deal's Google Drive data room in ONE call and record what it says: the investment profile set_deal_investment_profile would store (themes in the documents' own words, sectors, stages, geographies, minimum position, summary, source files), plus a library of 6-10 distinct insights for follow-up emails, each with the file it came from and a passage quoted verbatim from it. Every quote is checked against the extracted text and every number in an insight must appear in its quote; anything that fails is dropped, never repaired, and the result says how many were dropped. Reads up to 12 documents (offering materials first; executed paperwork in Signed Documents is skipped) through the Drive of whoever provisioned the folder, yours, or the owner's. Costs one AI call on your credits; when the folder has not changed since the last reading it returns the stored result for free unless force is true. A profile someone recorded by hand is NOT replaced unless overwrite_profile is true. Challenger cadence steps with insight_source "data_room" rotate through the insights, never repeating one to the same contact.

params.name: force
params.description: Re-read even if the folder's files have not changed. Default false.

params.name: overwrite_profile
params.description: Replace an investment profile someone recorded by hand. Default false: a hand-recorded profile is kept and the new reading is only reported.

tools.name: angelsend_calendar_status
tools.description: Check whether the user's AngelSend calendar is connected and which account/scopes are authorized. Call this when a calendar action fails or before assuming the calendar is available.

tools.name: angelsend_create_calendar_event
tools.description: Create an event in the user's AngelSend calendar. This is the right tool when the user asks to put a meeting on their *personal* / external calendar. For events that should live inside a Kavanah project, use `create_calendar_event` (the Kavanah one) instead.

params.name: title
params.description: Event title.

params.name: start
params.description: Event start. Preferred: naked local time `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]` (no `Z`, no offset) — the handler will convert it from the user's timezone (shown in the system prompt) to UTC. Or send ISO 8601 with an explicit offset (e.g. `2026-06-09T13:00:00-07:00`). NEVER hand-compute a `Z`/UTC timestamp — DST math is error-prone.

params.name: end
params.description: Event end, same format rules as `start`.

params.name: description
params.description: Optional event body / agenda.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional location string or video link.

params.name: attendees
params.description: Optional list of attendee email addresses. Strings are treated as emails.

tools.name: angelsend_credit_balance

tools.name: angelsend_delete_calendar_event
tools.description: Delete an AngelSend calendar event by id, removing it from the calendar. This is destructive — confirm with the user first unless they clearly asked to delete it. To merely mark an event cancelled while keeping the record, use `angelsend_update_calendar_event` with `cancel: true` instead.

params.name: event_id
params.description: The AngelSend event id to delete.

tools.name: angelsend_delete_record
tools.description: Run a DESTRUCTIVE AngelSend action discovered via `angelsend_search_tools`: deleting a deal, company, tag, comment, segment, follow-up rule, or chat-widget knowledge document; removing members from a segment; removing contacts from a campaign (cancels their queued sends); or removing an email suppression (`remove-email-optout`, `manage-block-list` with action 'remove'), which re-permits mail to an address that previously opted out. None of this is recoverable through the API. Always confirm with the user first and state exactly what will be removed. Rejects any action that is not destructive.

params.name: action
params.description: Action name exactly as returned by `angelsend_search_tools`, e.g. 'delete-deal'. Do not guess.

params.name: params
params.description: Parameters for the action. For the multiplexed actions (manage-*), the destructive sub-operation goes in `params.action` and most also require `confirmed: true`.

tools.name: angelsend_get_calendar_event
tools.description: Fetch a single AngelSend calendar event by id (returns title, time window, location, status, attendees, and a link). Use this to confirm an event's current details before updating or deleting it — get the id from `angelsend_list_calendar_events` first.

params.name: event_id
params.description: The AngelSend event id.

tools.name: angelsend_list_calendar_events
tools.description: List events from the user's AngelSend calendar in a given time window. Pass ISO-8601 timestamps. Use this for personal-calendar / external-calendar questions; for Kavanah task due-dates use `list_calendar_tasks` instead.

params.name: from
params.description: Start of the window, ISO-8601 (e.g. 2026-05-20T00:00:00Z). Optional — defaults to whatever AngelSend returns.

params.name: to
params.description: End of the window, ISO-8601. Optional.

tools.name: angelsend_list_contacts

params.name: limit
params.description: Max contacts to return. Default 50, capped at 500.

tools.name: angelsend_read
tools.description: Run a READ-ONLY AngelSend action discovered via `angelsend_search_tools` — listing, fetching, searching, scoring, or analysing. Rejects any action that would write, so it is always safe and free to call. Actions that spend the user's AngelSend credits or run AI inference are NOT in this lane even when they only read: they go through `angelsend_write` so they stay under approval policy. `angelsend_search_tools` labels which are which.

params.name: action
params.description: Action name exactly as returned by `angelsend_search_tools`, e.g. 'get-contact'. Do not guess.

params.name: params
params.description: Parameters for the action, matching the schema `angelsend_search_tools` returned. Unknown keys are rejected. For the multiplexed actions (manage-*), the sub-operation goes in `params.action`.

tools.name: angelsend_search_tools
tools.description: Search the AngelSend capability catalogue and get back the exact actions that match, each with its parameter schema. AngelSend is the user's sales/CRM platform: deals and companies, contacts and their tags/comments/custom fields, the outreach inbox, email suppression and CAN-SPAM compliance, buyer-intent signals, contact research and enrichment, draft-quality advisors, campaign authoring and launch, the knowledge base, chat-widget administration, and platform plumbing (projects, background jobs, calendar slots and bookings, Slack notes, outbound webhooks). ALWAYS call this first — it is the only way to learn an action's parameters, and guessing an action name will fail. Then pass the action you picked to `angelsend_read` or `angelsend_write`. Read-only.

params.name: query
params.description: What you are trying to do, in PLAIN WORDS — e.g. 'move a deal to another stage', 'stop emailing this address', 'why is this campaign landing in spam', 'create a campaign'. This is a relevance search, not a regex or glob: send 'create a campaign', never 'campaign.*create'. The field is named `query` — passing the search string under any other name is an error. Omit it entirely only to browse, which returns a sample across groups and is NOT evidence that an action is absent.

params.name: group
params.description: Optional filter. crm = deals/companies/segments; contacts = contact detail, tags, comments, custom fields, CRM sync, lead import; inbox = outreach messages, threads, replies, drafts, reply-intent; compliance = opt-outs, block list, CAN-SPAM address; intent = buyer-intent signals and scores; intelligence = research/enrichment/ranking (research and recommendations spend AngelSend credits); quality = draft compliance, deliverability, copy critique, send timing; campaigns = authoring, launch, follow-up/auto-reply automation, previews and test sends, contact-form outreach; knowledge = the retrieval knowledge base; chatbots = Intercom chat-widget administration; platform = projects, background jobs, calendar slots/bookings, Slack thread import, outbound webhooks.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max actions to return. Default 12.

tools.name: angelsend_send_email
tools.description: Send an email through the user's AngelSend account. Useful for sending follow-ups, recap notes, or campaign messages on behalf of the user. Refuse marketing-style bulk sends — this is intended for 1:few personal messages.

params.name: to
params.description: One or more recipient email addresses. Strings or arrays are both accepted.

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line.

params.name: body
params.description: Plain-text body. Provide either `body` or `html`.

params.name: html
params.description: HTML body. Provide either `body` or `html`.

params.name: from
params.description: Optional override of the From address; defaults to the connected AngelSend account.

params.name: reply_to
params.description: Optional Reply-To address.

params.name: cc
params.description: Optional CC list.

params.name: bcc
params.description: Optional BCC list.

tools.name: angelsend_update_calendar_event
tools.description: Update an existing AngelSend calendar event. PATCH semantics — only the fields you supply change; omitted fields are left as-is. Attendees are re-notified. Pass `cancel: true` to mark the event cancelled while keeping it on the calendar; use `angelsend_delete_calendar_event` to remove it entirely. You must know the `event_id` (use `angelsend_list_calendar_events` / `angelsend_get_calendar_event` to find it).

params.name: event_id
params.description: The AngelSend event id to update.

params.name: title
params.description: New event title. Optional.

params.name: start
params.description: New event start. Optional. Same format rules as `angelsend_create_calendar_event`: prefer naked local time `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]` (handler converts from the user's timezone) over hand-computed UTC.

params.name: end
params.description: New event end. Optional. Same format rules as `start`.

params.name: description
params.description: New event body / agenda. Optional.

params.name: location
params.description: New location string or link. Optional.

params.name: attendees
params.description: Replacement list of attendee email addresses. Optional — omit to leave attendees unchanged.

params.name: cancel
params.description: Set true to mark the event cancelled (status=cancelled) without deleting it.

tools.name: angelsend_write
tools.description: Run a non-destructive WRITING AngelSend action discovered via `angelsend_search_tools` — creating, updating, sending, or enriching. This changes the user's real CRM and can start real outreach: `reply-to-message` and `send-test-email` send email, `launch-campaign` starts sending to a campaign's whole audience, `create-booking` emails meeting confirmations, and `submit-contact-form` submits to a third-party website. Confirm with the user before any call that sends or launches. Rejects read-only actions (use `angelsend_read`) and destructive ones (use `angelsend_delete_record`).

params.name: action
params.description: Action name exactly as returned by `angelsend_search_tools`, e.g. 'update-deal'. Do not guess.

params.name: params
params.description: Parameters for the action, matching the schema `angelsend_search_tools` returned. Unknown keys are rejected. For the multiplexed actions (manage-*), the sub-operation goes in `params.action`.

tools.name: answer_manager_checkin

params.name: checkin_id
params.description: Id from list_manager_checkins. Omit to answer the oldest unanswered one.

params.name: response

tools.name: apply_blueprint
tools.description: Create a Blueprint's selected items through their normal write paths, all switched OFF (schedules paused, rules/cadences off, meetings disarmed, campaigns not started, switches unchanged). Idempotent. Turning items on is done by a person on the Blueprint page. Undoable as a set.

tools.name: apply_interview_writes
tools.description: Commit the staged draft to the real workspace config, after the user has confirmed it. Admin-only (charter/team-context are admin-maintained) — a non-admin's proposal is kept staged for an admin to apply. Only call this once the user has seen the draft from propose_interview_writes and said yes.

params.name: interview_id

tools.name: apply_investor_match_weights
tools.description: Apply investor-match scoring weights. Admin only. Pass use_proposal: true to apply the proposal get_investor_match_calibration shows now (refused when there is none), weights to set an explicit set (every component, whole numbers, each within 0.5x–1.5x of its default, total 100), or reset: true for the built-in weights. reason is required and is logged with the before/after and the evidence. Re-orders every future investor ranking (the stored ranks update on the next re-rank); firms already released, approached or dismissed keep their status. Confirm with the user first.

params.name: metric
params.description: Which proposal (default reply).

tools.name: apply_org_template

params.name: template

params.name: roles

tools.name: archive_client
tools.description: Archive a client (or unarchive if archived=false). Confirm with user first.

tools.name: archive_deal
tools.description: Take a deal OUT of Deal Room: an archived deal leaves the board, every pipeline total, the revenue forecast and the forecast charts, and stops appearing in reports and digests. Use it for a deal that did not happen, a duplicate, or a row entered by mistake — when someone says a deal should not be in Deal Room at all. Nothing is deleted: the deal keeps its timeline, contacts and fields, get_deal still reads it, list_deals shows it with include_archived, and restore: true (or Undo) brings it back. To CORRECT a real deal whose name, contact, stage or numbers are wrong, use update_deal instead — archiving is not how you fix a mislabelled deal. `reason` is required and is written onto the deal's timeline.

params.name: deal_id
params.description: The deal's id, as list_deals prints it.

params.name: reason
params.description: Why the deal is being archived (or restored), in the user's words where possible — e.g. 'Mitch: this investment never happened'. Written to the deal's timeline.

params.name: restore
params.description: True brings an archived deal back onto the board instead of archiving it.

tools.name: archive_project

params.name: archived

tools.name: ask_knowledge_base
tools.description: Answer a QUESTION from this workspace's own knowledge — tasks, discussion threads, docs, decisions, retros, onboarding, glossary, and saved agent memories — instead of guessing. Retrieves the most relevant sources across all those surfaces, then has an LLM synthesize a grounded answer that CITES the exact sources it used. PREFER this over search_knowledge_documents whenever the user asks a question ('why did we choose X?', 'what's blocking Y?', 'who owns Z?') rather than for a specific document to open — search_knowledge_documents only finds a doc by title, this actually answers. If nothing in the workspace matches, it says so instead of inventing an answer. Slow (one LLM call, several seconds); keep the question focused.

tools.name: budget_vs_actual
tools.description: Compare budgeted spend to ACTUAL ClearBooks transactions over a period and report the variance (total and, optionally, per budget line). Provide the period (start_date/end_date) and budget lines — each a category label + budgeted amount. Actuals are pulled live from ClearBooks expense transactions and matched to lines by category name (a line labeled 'Total' or with no match captures the remainder). Use for monthly/quarterly budget reviews; pair with create_goal (metric 'clearbooks_metric') to track a number over time, and escalate_to_user if a line blows past budget.

params.name: start_date
params.description: Period start (YYYY-MM-DD).

params.name: end_date
params.description: Period end (YYYY-MM-DD).

params.name: budget_lines
params.description: Budget lines to check. Label is matched (case-insensitive) against transaction category names; a line labeled 'Total' compares against total spend.

params.name: type
params.description: Which side to measure. Default 'expense'.

tools.name: bulk_create_network_contacts
tools.description: Save up to 200 people into the network in one call — what a LinkedIn scan, a conference list or a research pass produces. Same gap-filling rules as create_network_contact, applied per person, and it reports EVERY entry back: created, updated (with where the existing record came from), or skipped with the reason. Over 200 the whole call is refused rather than truncated, so nothing is lost silently. Duplicates inside one call are reported, not written twice. Undo removes only the contacts this call created and only while nothing has used them; a firm the call created stays.

params.name: contacts
params.description: 1-200 people.

params.name: source
params.description: Where this whole batch came from, e.g. 'linkedin'. Applied to every entry, recorded on each record, and kept for ever once set. Defaults to 'agent'.

params.name: tags
params.description: Tags added to EVERY contact in the batch, on top of each one's own. This is how a scan stays findable afterwards — e.g. ['family-office','data-centre'].

params.name: firm_roles
params.description: Roles for firms this call CREATES. Existing firms keep the roles they have.

tools.name: bulk_create_tasks
tools.description: Create multiple tasks at once. Each task needs at least a title. Use when the user provides a list or outline of tasks to create. project_ref is the default project for the batch; when the tasks belong to DIFFERENT projects (e.g. one per department), set project_ref on each task instead of putting them all in one project.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: The default project reference/ID for every task that does not set its own.

params.name: tasks
params.description: Array of tasks to create

tools.name: bulk_estimate_tasks_by_filter
tools.description: Estimate every task that matches a filter, server-side, in one tool call. Use this for prompts like 'estimate all open tasks in Project X' or 'estimate everything assigned to Sarah in the review column'. Skips tasks that already have an AI estimate unless only_unestimated=false. Caps at 50 tasks per call. Respects the workspace's daily AI token budget — fails fast when exhausted.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Limit to one project (use list_projects to find refs)

params.name: status_id
params.description: Limit to one status/column (open, progress, review, etc.). If omitted, defaults to all non-completed tasks.

params.name: assigned_to
params.description: Limit to tasks assigned to a name (substring match)

params.name: tag
params.description: Limit to a tag/label (substring match)

params.name: only_unestimated
params.description: If true (default), skip tasks that already have an AI estimate. Set false to re-estimate.

params.name: only_open
params.description: If true (default), exclude completed/closed/archived tasks. Ignored when status_id is set.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max tasks to estimate (1–50, default 25)

tools.name: bulk_set_due_dates
tools.description: Set or clear due_date on many tasks in a single call. Use after the user has confirmed the dates, or as a thin wrapper when they explicitly ask for a uniform due date across a set of tasks. To predict per-task due dates from estimates, use predict_and_apply_due_dates instead.

params.name: task_ids
params.description: Task IDs to update (max 200)

params.name: due_date
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD to set the same due date on every task, or null to clear all of them

tools.name: bulk_update_tasks
tools.description: Apply the same patch to many tasks at once. Use when the user says things like 'move all Open backend tasks to In Progress', 'set these five tasks to High priority', or 'reassign Sarah's tasks to Marcus'. Up to 500 task ids per call. Returns the count actually patched. Same status-transition / required-field gates apply per-task. Calls touching MORE than 25 tasks return a preview first — show it to the user, get their go-ahead, then re-call with confirm=true.

params.name: task_ids
params.description: Task IDs to patch (1..500)

params.name: status_id
params.description: New status (column) for all tasks

params.name: assigned_to
params.description: Assignee name(s), comma-separated for several people. REPLACES each task's whole assignee list; empty string clears it.

params.name: emoji
params.description: Set the SAME emoji label on every task in this call. To label a whole board by kind of work, group the tasks yourself and make one call per emoji — that is far cheaper than one update_task per task and is the intended way to do it at scale. Null or empty clears.

params.name: due_date
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD; pass '' to clear

params.name: sprint_id
params.description: Sprint id to assign (uuid-shaped string, or null to clear)

params.name: confirm
params.description: Required true to execute when task_ids has more than 25 entries — only after the user has approved the preview.

tools.name: cancel_agent_schedule
tools.description: Delete a scheduled autonomous run, with its run history. Prefer PAUSING (update_agent_schedule enabled:false): a paused schedule stops firing, keeps its history, and no longer counts toward the 25-active-schedule limit — so pausing is also how to free a slot. Delete only a schedule the user has asked, by name, to be deleted. The user can undo a deletion from the chat. Get the id from list_agent_schedules.

params.name: schedule_id
params.description: The schedule id to delete.

tools.name: cancel_commitment
tools.description: Cancel one of the caller's own open commitments — the work is no longer being done. No points are awarded and none are deducted; a cancelled commitment is neither kept nor broken. Use this rather than letting work the user has abandoned sit and rot into a miss.

params.name: commitment_id
params.description: Id from list_my_commitments.

params.name: reason
params.description: Why it is being cancelled.

tools.name: cancel_invite
tools.description: Revoke a pending workspace invite. Sets status to 'declined' (so the row sticks around for audit) or fully deletes it when `hard_delete: true` is passed. Cannot be used on already-accepted invites.

params.name: invite_id
params.description: Invite row id (UUID).

params.name: hard_delete
params.description: When true, deletes the row entirely. Defaults to false (mark as declined).

tools.name: cancel_meeting_twin
tools.description: Make a twin or notetaker the caller sent leave its meeting now (or never join, if it has not yet). An admin may stop anyone's. Never starts anything.

params.name: session_id
params.description: From list_meeting_twin_sessions.

tools.name: cancel_outcome_check
tools.description: Withdraw a pending post-condition — use when the plan changed and the check has become an unfair test (the task was descoped, the person left, the goal was replaced). A cancelled check is excluded from the hit rate rather than counted as a miss. Do NOT cancel a check simply because it looks like it is about to fail; that is the one thing this ledger exists to catch.

params.name: expectation_id
params.description: The id from list_outcome_checks.

params.name: reason
params.description: Why it is no longer a fair test.

tools.name: cancel_recurring_email
tools.description: Permanently delete a recurring email so it stops sending. To pause without deleting, use update_recurring_email with enabled:false instead. Get the id from list_recurring_emails.

params.name: id
params.description: The recurring email id to delete.

tools.name: cancel_runbook_run
tools.description: Abandon an in-progress runbook run (e.g. the process was called off).

params.name: reason
params.description: Why it was cancelled.

tools.name: cancel_scheduled_email
tools.description: Cancel a pending scheduled email so it will not be sent. Only emails that are still pending (not yet sent) can be cancelled. Get the id from list_scheduled_emails.

params.name: id
params.description: The scheduled email id to cancel.

tools.name: change_member_role
tools.description: Change a workspace member's role to owner, admin, or member. Confirm with user — owner role grants full control.

params.name: user_id
params.description: The member's user UUID from list_members. Their email or exact full name is also accepted and will be resolved.

params.name: email
params.description: The member's email — an alternative to user_id; pass one or the other.

tools.name: check_against_kvn
tools.description: Check a proposed piece of work against the company + project KVN charter BEFORE committing to it. Returns 'aligned', 'negated' (the charter forbids it), or 'false_friend' (it looks like it serves the Vision but serves a proxy for it instead), citing the exact charter line. Advisory and read-only — use it when the user is DELIBERATING ('should we do X?', 'is this worth doing?', 'does this fit our roadmap?'). You do not need to call this before create_task: the KVN gate already checks every task/project write automatically and will refuse it.

params.name: subject
params.description: The proposed work, as you would describe it in a task title + description.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project the work would land in, so its charter and false-friends list apply. Omit to check against the company charter only.

tools.name: check_app_endpoint
tools.description: Check whether an owned app's tool endpoint (or, with surface_id, one of its screens) is reachable over HTTPS: an SSRF-guarded HEAD/OPTIONS against the URL in the app's CURRENT manifest. Sends no signed body and runs no tool — it proves the host answers, nothing more; a 404 or 405 still counts as reachable. Use it after the user deploys their server and before test_app_tool, and whenever an installed app's health is degraded. It reads the URL from the stored manifest, never from you, so a placeholder endpoint fails here and the fix is to publish a version with the real URL.

params.name: slug
params.description: The app's slug.

params.name: surface_id
params.description: Optional: probe this screen's entry_url instead of the tool endpoint.

tools.name: check_goals
tools.description: Evaluate goals against live data NOW and report each one's current value + variance verdict (on_track / at_risk / off_track). Pass a goal_id for one, or omit to check all active goals. Manual and clearbooks_metric goals report their last recorded value (use record_goal_value / the clearbooks_* tools to refresh those).

params.name: goal_id
params.description: Optional single goal to check.

tools.name: clear_column_limit
tools.description: Remove the WIP limit and name override for one status on a project.

tools.name: clear_task_location
tools.description: Remove the geographic pin from a task so it no longer appears on the Map view.

params.name: task_id
params.description: The numeric id of the task to clear the location from.

tools.name: clearbooks_apply_bill_payment
tools.description: Point part or all of an existing ClearBooks payment at a specific bill. The bill only becomes 'paid' once nothing is left outstanding. Over-application is refused with the real remaining balance.

tools.name: clearbooks_apply_vendor_credit_to_bill
tools.description: Settle a ClearBooks bill using a vendor credit instead of cash. Use when a supplier credit note should be set against what you owe them. Recorded separately from cash payments so the same settlement is never counted twice.

tools.name: clearbooks_ask_agent
tools.description: Delegate a question or task to the ClearBooks AI accounting agent (agent-to-agent chat). The remote agent runs its own tool loop over the org's books and CAN TAKE ACTIONS there — including writes and payments — regardless of the API key's other scopes, and each call bills 1 ClearBooks AI credit to the key owner. Prefer the specific clearbooks_* tools for anything they already cover (listing invoices, metrics, reports, …); reach for this only for open-ended accounting analysis or actions no dedicated tool exposes. Admin-only. Pass conversation_id to continue a prior exchange.

params.name: message
params.description: The question or instruction for the ClearBooks agent (one user turn).

params.name: conversation_id
params.description: Optional id from a previous reply to keep conversational context.

tools.name: clearbooks_batch_categorize_transactions
tools.description: Bulk-assign categories and/or GL codes to a list of existing transactions.

tools.name: clearbooks_batch_create_transactions
tools.description: Create many ClearBooks transactions in one call. Returns counts of created vs failed plus the new ids.

tools.name: clearbooks_close_accounting_period
tools.description: Close the ClearBooks books for a date range. soft_closed still lets nominated users post (each recorded as an exception); hard_closed lets nobody post until explicitly reopened. This stops posting for EVERY other credential, not just this one. Use when the user says close the month/quarter/year or lock the books.

params.name: period_start
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD

params.name: period_end
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: clearbooks_convert_estimate_to_invoice
tools.description: Turn an accepted ClearBooks estimate into an invoice, carrying its line items across. Use when the user says a quote was accepted, won, or should be billed. Refuses if already converted.

tools.name: clearbooks_convert_purchase_order_to_bill
tools.description: Turn a received ClearBooks purchase order into a vendor bill, carrying its line items across. Use when goods or services on a PO have arrived and should now be payable.

tools.name: clearbooks_create_ach_payment

params.name: payment_date
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: clearbooks_create_bill

params.name: bill_date
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD.

params.name: due_date
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: clearbooks_create_bill_payment
tools.description: Record money leaving for a vendor in ClearBooks. This records the payment only — point it at specific bills afterwards with clearbooks_apply_bill_payment. Paid-but-unapplied is a legitimate state (a cheque banked before anyone decided which bills it covers).

params.name: payment_date

Do not offer it; use clearbooks_get_cap_table for the summary and tell the user equity has to be recorded in ClearBooks directly for now.

params.name: interest_rate

tools.name: clearbooks_create_customer

tools.name: clearbooks_create_forecast

tools.name: clearbooks_create_holding

NOT CURRENTLY AVAILABLE: ClearBooks does not implement this endpoint — the cap-table API is the summary and one investment by id, nothing else. This call always fails. Do not offer it; use clearbooks_get_cap_table for the summary and tell the user equity has to be recorded in ClearBooks directly for now.

params.name: purchase_date

tools.name: clearbooks_create_personnel

tools.name: clearbooks_create_shareholder

Do not offer it; use clearbooks_get_cap_table for the summary and tell the user equity has to be recorded in ClearBooks directly for now.

params.name: entity_type

tools.name: clearbooks_create_stock_option
tools.description: Grant stock options to a grantee from a specific option pool. Confirm with the user before granting. NOT CURRENTLY AVAILABLE: ClearBooks does not implement this endpoint — the cap-table API is the summary and one investment by id, nothing else. This call always fails. Do not offer it; use clearbooks_get_cap_table for the summary and tell the user equity has to be recorded in ClearBooks directly for now.

params.name: grant_date

Admin only, and it runs with YOUR AngelSend key. optouts_in (hourly) imports AngelSend's do-not-email list into this workspace's suppression list. contacts_pull (daily) gap-fills Deal Room contacts from a segment (paged) or the newest 500 leads. contacts_push (daily) ARMS unattended writes to AngelSend: it only ever CREATES leads AngelSend has never held — it never re-sends an existing address, because AngelSend's import overwrites the whole lead row, status and tags included. Only the directions you pass change.

tools.name: configure_angelsend_campaign_mirror
tools.description: Back a cadence with a native AngelSend campaign, or stop doing so. Admin only; runs with YOUR AngelSend key. ON: Kavanah creates the AngelSend campaign from the cadence's steps, hands it every enrollment that has not sent yet (both suppression lists checked first), and AngelSend sends — so volume beyond your connected mailboxes is possible on AngelSend's own sending (send_channel "resend", from a verified domain; "gmail"/"outlook" send from your own mailbox and add no capacity). Replies, meetings, opt-outs and every other Kavanah stop pull the person out of the AngelSend campaign; AngelSend's sends, replies and unsubscribes come back into Kavanah. Refused (and paused) when steps are personalized, when AngelSend has no CAN-SPAM company address (its unsubscribe footer needs one), or — under compliance mode — when AngelSend cannot be shown to carry the archive BCC. A deal cadence is mirrored per deal (pass deal_id); a network cadence without one. OFF pauses the AngelSend campaign; enrollments AngelSend never received go back to Kavanah's own sending.

params.name: deal_id
params.description: Required for a deal cadence; omit for a network cadence.

params.name: send_channel
params.description: Default gmail (your own mailbox). resend = AngelSend's own sending.

params.name: daily_limit

params.name: handoff_in_flight

Narrowing scopes immediately narrows every API key the app holds. Only the fields you pass change. Use uninstall_app to remove it entirely.

tools.name: configure_cadence_variant_test
tools.description: Configure how a cadence tests subjects and senders, and its OPT-IN automatic winner policy. Admin only. design 'linked' (default; arm C = subject C AND sender C, so the two are confounded) or 'factorial' (subject variant and sender assigned by two independent hashes, so each is measured on its own). auto_winner (default off; needs factorial): once every arm has min_per_arm contacts and one level's Bayesian probability to be best stays at or above threshold across two evaluations at least 24h apart, NEW enrollments shift to that winner while explore_pct of them keep being split evenly. A contact's subject and sender are fixed at their first send and never change — not by a design switch, not by a winner — and a contact keeps the same sender for every step. metric: 'reply' (default), 'positive_reply' or 'meeting'. reset_winner clears a declared winner. Every winner decision is recorded. Confirm with the user before turning auto_winner on: it changes what future contacts receive without anyone watching.

params.name: cadence
params.description: Cadence id or exact name.

params.name: min_per_arm
params.description: Contacts every arm needs before a winner can be judged (30–10000, default 100).

params.name: explore_pct
params.description: Share of new enrollments still split evenly after a winner (5–50, default 10).

params.name: threshold
params.description: Probability-to-be-best bar (0.9–0.999, default 0.95).

tools.name: configure_compliance_archiving
tools.description: Apply the OWNER's compliance archiving preferences (for anyone else, use request_compliance_archiving_change). Set up compliance archiving: every email Kavanah sends for this workspace is copied to the firm's archiver, and everything said inside Kavanah (chat, discussions, comments, agent messages, approvals, files, call audio) is journaled and delivered to it. WORKSPACE OWNER ONLY. Set `archive_address` to the journaling address the firm's archiver (Global Relay, Smarsh, Proofpoint…) issued — never invent or guess one; ask for it. Set `enabled: true` to turn it on (it needs an address; turning it on also backfills existing history). `retention_days` 365–3650 (default six years, 2190). `send_test: true` sends a labelled test message to the address so the compliance officer can confirm the archiver accepts it — offer it after turning archiving on. This tool cannot turn archiving OFF or remove the address: that stops a compliance control, so it is done only by the owner in Settings → Audit Logs → Archiving.

params.name: archive_address
params.description: The archiver's journaling email address. One address.

params.name: enabled
params.description: true turns compliance archiving on. false is refused — turn it off in Settings.

params.name: retention_days
params.description: How long journaled records are kept, 365–3650 days.

params.name: send_test
params.description: Send a labelled test message to the archive address after any change.

tools.name: configure_deal_forecast
tools.description: Set up the revenue forecast for the workspace (admin only): the assumed fee % for deals with no recorded fee, fee bands the forecast must report separately (and never combine), a disclaimer printed on every forecast, AUTOMATIC DAILY RECALCULATION onto the deal records (off by default), and the WEEKLY FORECAST EMAIL — day, local time, timezone and which workspace members receive it. Recipients must be active members of the workspace. Only the settings you pass change; read the current ones with get_deal_forecast_settings first. To add or remove one recipient use email_recipients_add / email_recipients_remove — email_recipients REPLACES the whole list. Confirm the schedule and recipients with the user before turning the email on. Returns the full configuration as saved.

params.name: default_fee_pct
params.description: Fee assumed when a deal has a deal size but no recorded fee, in percent (1 = 1%).

params.name: band_threshold_dollars
params.description: Report deals with a fee at or below this many dollars separately from those above it, with no combined total anywhere. Null turns bands off.

params.name: lower_band_label
params.description: Label for the at-or-below band, e.g. 'Proven band (≤ $100K)'.

params.name: upper_band_label
params.description: Label for the above band, e.g. 'Unproven band (> $100K)'.

params.name: disclaimer
params.description: One line printed at the top of every forecast (dashboard, email, this tool). Null removes it.

params.name: auto_recalculate
params.description: Recalculate and write the forecast onto every open deal once a day.

params.name: email_enabled
params.description: Turn the weekly forecast email on or off.

params.name: email_day
params.description: Day the weekly email sends. Defaults to monday.

params.name: email_time
params.description: Local send time, HH:MM 24h. Defaults to 08:00.

params.name: email_timezone
params.description: IANA timezone for the send time, e.g. 'America/Chicago'. Defaults to the caller's timezone.

params.name: email_recipients
params.description: The COMPLETE list of workspace members (email addresses) who receive the weekly forecast. Replaces the current list — anyone not named stops receiving it.

params.name: email_recipients_add
params.description: Member email addresses to ADD to the current recipients; everyone already on the list stays. Not with email_recipients.

params.name: email_recipients_remove
params.description: Member email addresses to REMOVE from the current recipients. Not with email_recipients.

params.name: email_subject
params.description: Subject line; {{date}} renders the send date. Null restores 'Weekly Revenue Forecast — {{date}}'.

tools.name: configure_state_of_business_report
tools.description: Set up (or reconfigure) the recurring 'Agentic COO — State of the Business' email report for this workspace in ONE call: it creates a saved report + a delivery schedule and turns the report feature on. The report is a per-department executive briefing — health score (color-coded), what changed since the last report, top 3–5 deliverables, connected external systems + a derived automation %, and 3–5 suggested automations with estimated cost. Departments come from the workspace's Departments — use `list_departments` / `create_department` / `set_project_department` first so each department has projects and members mapped, or work lands in an 'Unassigned' bucket. THIS ARMS RECURRING AI SPEND: every send runs an AI synthesis on the cadence you set (e.g. 3×/day). Admin only. Provide either `times` (local HH:MM list, e.g. ["08:00","12:00","17:00"]) or an explicit UTC `cron_expression`.

params.name: recipient_emails
params.description: Literal recipient email addresses (e.g. ["finance@example.com"]). Required unless recipient_groups is given.

params.name: recipient_groups
params.description: Optional dynamic recipients, same shape as create_report_schedule ({ workspace_all, department_names, user_ids, ... }). Resolved at each send.

params.name: times
params.description: Local send times as HH:MM (24h), e.g. ["08:00","12:00","17:00"] for 8am/12pm/5pm. All times must share the same minute. Ignored if cron_expression is given.

params.name: cron_expression
params.description: Alternative to `times`: a 5-field cron evaluated in `timezone`. The minute field must be specific (e.g. `0`), not `*`. Example: `0 8,12,17 * * *`.

params.name: timezone
params.description: IANA timezone the times/cron are interpreted in, e.g. "America/Chicago" for CST/CDT. Defaults to UTC. DST is handled automatically.

params.name: subject_template
params.description: Optional email subject. Supports {{date}} / {{time}} / {{datetime}} tokens rendered in `timezone`. Defaults to "Agentic COO - State of the Business Report {{datetime}}".

params.name: window_days
params.description: How many days of activity each report covers (default 30).

params.name: report_name
params.description: Display name for the saved report (default "State of the Business").

params.name: enable
params.description: Turn the report feature on (state_of_business_enabled). Defaults to true — set false to stage the schedule without arming sends.

tools.name: connect_github_repo

Identify the repo by github_repo_id (from list_connectable_github_repos) or by full_name ('owner/repo', resolved against the App-installation cache). Re-running on an already-connected repo refreshes its data. Admin-only. Requires GitHub access (App install covering the repo, or the caller's personal OAuth).

params.name: github_repo_id
params.description: GitHub's numeric repo id, as returned by list_connectable_github_repos.

params.name: full_name
params.description: Alternative to github_repo_id: the repo's 'owner/repo' full name, resolved against the GitHub App installation cache.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional Kavanah project ref to associate the repo with on /dev.

tools.name: convert_issuer_to_deal
tools.description: A prospect became a client: create a deal for the firm (in the default pipeline's first open stage unless told otherwise), link every contact we hold at the firm to it (the warmest as primary), and record on the campaign that this issuer CONVERTED and which deal it became. From then on the firm is a client — every ranking in the workspace excludes it — and the investor funnel can run on the new deal. Sends nothing.

params.name: campaign
params.description: Campaign id or exact name.

params.name: name
params.description: Deal name. Defaults to the firm's name.

params.name: amount_dollars
params.description: Raise size, if known. Defaults to the firm's recorded raise target.

params.name: pipeline

params.name: stage

tools.name: convert_request_to_task
tools.description: Convert an inbound request into a task in the named project. The new task's title is the request subject and its description embeds the submitter's contact info. Marks the request as converted so it can't be converted twice.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Target project id (stringified, e.g. '1').

params.name: assigned_to
params.description: Optional assignee user id. Defaults to the request page's owner.

tools.name: create_agent_schedule
tools.description: Create a recurring AUTONOMOUS agent run (a scheduled job the agent executes on its own on a clock). By default it sends nothing on days its person has no open tasks — see only_when_tasks_for. Use this when the user wants something to happen on a repeating schedule that requires the agent to think/act each time — e.g. 'every weekday at 8am email me what I should work on today', 'each Monday summarize open risks'. Set `autonomy_level: 'safe'` (default) so the run can use tools (read tasks, post notes, and email YOU via email_my_digest); 'none' is a plain text-only note with no tools. IMPORTANT: the schedule fires on a UTC clock — convert the user's local time. E.g. 8am PST = hour_utc 16 (PST/UTC-8) or 15 during daylight time (PDT/UTC-7); note the offset caveat to the user. Safe runs are still capped by the workspace autonomy ceiling; below it they degrade to text-only. For a purely STATIC recurring email use schedule_recurring_email; for a recurring analytics REPORT use create_report_schedule. A workspace may have at most 25 ACTIVE schedules; paused ones do not count. If this is refused for the limit, tell the user and ask which schedule to PAUSE (update_agent_schedule enabled:false) — never delete schedules on your own to make room.

params.name: name
params.description: Short label for the schedule (e.g. 'Morning work digest').

params.name: prompt
params.description: The instruction the agent executes each run, written as if speaking to the agent. Be specific about what to produce and to deliver it. E.g. 'Compile everything I should work on today — my overdue tasks, tasks due today, and anything in progress — then email it to me with email_my_digest.'

params.name: frequency
params.description: How often to run. Defaults to 'daily'.

params.name: hour_utc
params.description: UTC hour 0–23 the run fires (used by daily/weekly/monthly). Defaults to 9.

params.name: minute_utc
params.description: UTC minute 0–59. Defaults to 0.

params.name: day_of_week
params.description: 0=Sunday … 6=Saturday, for weekly frequency. Defaults to 1 (Monday).

params.name: day_of_month
params.description: 1–28 for monthly frequency (clamped to 28 to exist in every month). Defaults to 1.

params.name: autonomy_level
params.description: 'safe' (default) runs the full SAFE-mode tool loop; 'none' is a single text-only Claude call with no tools.

params.name: persona_id
params.description: Optional persona (AI employee) id to run the schedule as — applies its personality, model, and tool scopes.

params.name: model
params.description: Omit to inherit. 'auto': a router picks the cheapest model per run. claude-haiku-4-5 for simple list/summarize/remind runs; Sonnet for drafting or judgement. 'default' clears.

params.name: only_when_tasks_for
params.description: DEFAULT: when omitted, the schedule runs only while the person who creates it has open tasks — no tasks, no email, nothing spent. Set it to the teammate the schedule is ABOUT when that is someone else (a daily reminder for Ryan set up by an admin → 'Ryan'; a first name is fine). Set it to an empty string for a schedule that must send regardless of anyone's tasks — a revenue forecast, a business overview, a report to outside investors. The check runs before the run starts, so do not also tell the run to skip itself.

params.name: task_gate
params.description: 'open' (default) runs only if the person has any open task; 'due' runs only if they have a task due today or overdue (or within tasks_due_within_days) — tasks with no due date never count, so use 'due' only when the user asks for it ('only if something is due').

params.name: tasks_due_within_days
params.description: With task_gate 'due': how many days ahead still count as due (0 = due today or overdue, the default; 7 = anything due this week). 0–30.

params.name: enabled
params.description: Defaults to true. Set false to create it paused.

tools.name: create_ai_persona
tools.description: Create a new AI Employee (persona) in this workspace. Use when the user asks to hire, add, build, or set up an AI employee/teammate/assistant. Workspace owners and admins only. Interview the user first: an AI Employee is only as good as its name, role, and instructions. Ask what job it should do, then write a substantial personality/instructions block yourself rather than echoing a one-liner back. allowed_scopes decides what the employee can actually DO. Omitted, it starts on the same groups the roster editor gives a new employee — tasks_projects, communications, reports_analytics, knowledge_files — NOT every capability. Pass an explicit list to widen or narrow that, or an empty array for every capability. Prefer the narrowest set that covers the stated job, and tell the user which groups the employee ended up with. This does NOT generate a profile picture; call generate_ai_persona_avatar afterwards (it costs credits, so confirm with the user first). Names are unique per workspace (case-insensitive): if an employee with the name already exists this refuses and returns its id — update that one with update_ai_persona instead of creating a copy.

params.name: name
params.description: Display name, e.g. 'Ada'. Required, 80 chars max.

params.name: role_title
params.description: Job title, e.g. 'Chief Operating Officer'. 120 chars max.

params.name: personality
params.description: The employee's instructions and personality — its system-prompt layer. Who they are, how they work, what they prioritise, tone. 8000 chars max. This is the single highest-impact field.

params.name: model
params.description: Optional per-employee model override. Omit to use the workspace default.

params.name: allowed_scopes
params.description: Capability groups this employee may use. Omitted, it defaults to the starter set (tasks_projects, communications, reports_analytics, knowledge_files); pass an empty array to inherit ALL capabilities instead. Available: tasks_projects (Tasks & projects: Create/update tasks, manage projects, sprints, dependencies, statuses, swimlanes); communications (Chat & discussions: Workspace chat, discussion threads, notifications, inbox, message templates); email_calendar (Email & calendar: Connected Gmail/Proton/AngelSend mail, Google Calendar, scheduled emails); dev_github (Developer & GitHub: Cloudcode, multiverseAI, linked dev accounts); workflows_automations (Workflows & automations: Automation rules, proactive agent, recurring tasks, background jobs, Scrappy scraping engine (sources/jobs)); reports_analytics (Reports & analytics: Reports, portfolio, time tracking, capacity, audit search); crm (Clients & deals: CRM — clients, client portal members, deals pipeline, Scrappy lead funnel (leads/accounts/campaigns)); finance (Finance & accounting: ClearBooks — invoices, transactions, GL, cap table, metrics, banking, ACH); knowledge_files (Knowledge & files: Knowledge base, project files, templates, resource requests, Scrappy website→markdown exports); admin (Administration: Governance, SLA policies, support, undo stack, jira-parity admin)

params.name: member_user_ids
params.description: Optional user ids allowed to chat with this employee. Omit or pass an empty array to leave it open to every workspace member. Workspace admins always retain access.

params.name: avatar_prompt
params.description: Visual description of how the employee should look, stored for later image generation. Does not generate anything by itself.

params.name: security_guardrails
params.description: Optional free-text safety rules injected at high priority into this employee's prompt.

params.name: enabled
params.description: Default true. Pass false to create the employee switched off.

params.name: reports_to
params.description: Optional: the AI Employee this one reports to (org chart), by id or exact name. Must be an employee in this workspace. The employee's prompt then names its manager and direct reports.

tools.name: create_app
tools.description: Create a new private app owned by this workspace from a manifest, seeded with its first version. The manifest's slug becomes a GLOBAL, permanent identity that cannot be reused by anyone else, so confirm the slug with the user before calling. Private apps are installable in this workspace immediately; public listing is a separate operator review. Pass the manifest as a JSON string — usually the output of draft_app_manifest after the user approved it. Next steps after this: scaffold_app_code for the server, install_app once it is deployed.

params.name: manifest_json
params.description: The full app manifest as a JSON string.

tools.name: create_autolink_rule
tools.description: Create an auto-link rule so a phrase (literal or regex) automatically links to a target. WRITES a rule to the workspace. Regex patterns are validated and rejected if they risk catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) — auto-link patterns never need nested quantifiers.

params.name: pattern
params.description: The text to match (a literal phrase, or a regex if pattern_kind='regex'). Max 200 chars.

params.name: pattern_kind
params.description: 'literal' (default) matches the exact phrase; 'regex' treats pattern as a regular expression.

params.name: match_kind
params.description: What kind of thing the pattern names: 'feature', 'file', 'term' (default), or 'decision-id'.

params.name: target_kind
params.description: What the link points to: 'doc' (default), 'decision', 'glossary', or 'code'.

params.name: target_ref
params.description: The id/ref of the link target (e.g. a document id or decision ref_code). Max 400 chars.

params.name: target_label
params.description: Optional human-readable label for the link. Max 200 chars.

params.name: enabled
params.description: Whether the rule is active (default true).

tools.name: create_automation
tools.description: Create an automation rule. trigger_type values: - 'created' / 'completed' / 'moved' / 'assigned' — task lifecycle. trigger_config can gate on { from_status, to_status, status_id, priority, project_ref, tag }. - 'due-date' — fires once when a task's due_date passes (swept hourly by the overdue-tasks cron; re-arms if the due date is pushed out). trigger_config can gate on { priority, project_ref, tag, status_id }. Use this for 'when a task is overdue → …' rules. - 'property-changed' — fires when a custom property value changes. trigger_config: { property_id?: <def id>, property_key?: <key>, from?: <value>, to?: <value> }. property_id is preferred (survives rename). EXTERNAL EVENT triggers — these fire on things that happen OUTSIDE Kavanah. They carry no task, so the only actions that work with them are 'invoke-agent' and 'start-water-cooler': - 'email-received' — a new email arrived on a connected mailbox (Gmail/Outlook/Proton/iCloud). trigger_config can also gate on { direction: 'inbound' | 'outbound' } (inbound skips mail the user sent) and { from_contact: 'deal' | 'network' | 'any' } — deal = the sender is a contact on an open deal, network = a known contact on no open deal, any = any known contact (strangers never match; omit it to match every sender), and { from_member: true } — the sender is an active member of this workspace (use it for 'let me / my team email the agent'; teammates are NOT contacts, so from_contact never matches them). A reply-to-investors rule should use BOTH direction: 'inbound' and from_contact, or it wakes on every message in the mailbox. - 'integration-item' — a new item appeared in a connected PM tool (Jira issue, ClickUp/Asana task, Monday item, Notion page). - 'github-pull-request' / 'github-push' — a PR was opened/closed/updated, or commits were pushed. - 'calendar-event' — a new calendar event was synced. - 'finance-event' — a verified ClearBooks or Stripe webhook fired (invoice paid, payment failed, …). - 'document-event' — a verified XDocs webhook fired: an agreement was signed / declined / voided / expired, or a tracked link was read, downloaded, or its NDA accepted. - 'deal-stage-changed' — a deal moved between pipeline stages. This is the 'a client became engaged' trigger. trigger_config gates on { to_stage, from_stage, to_stage_kind, to_stage_id, pipeline_id } — prefer to_stage_kind ('open'|'won'|'lost') or to_stage_id over to_stage, because a stage NAME changes the day someone renames the column and the rule then silently stops firing. It fires on a stage CHANGE only, never on deal creation: a Sheet or Asana import creates hundreds of deals in their real stages at once, and firing then would send hundreds of signature requests. - 'deal-document-signed' — the counterparty signed an XDocs envelope that was sent on a deal (the 'they signed → start their campaign' handoff). trigger_config gates on { document_name (exact template/document name), pipeline_id, provider: 'xdocs' }. It fires ONCE per envelope, and never for an envelope that was already signed when Kavanah first saw it, so a sync of old contracts cannot start campaigns. - 'meeting-booked' — a deal contact booked a meeting (an AngelSend booking link, or a calendar event they are on). Fires once per meeting per OPEN deal the contact is on (carrying that deal, so the deal actions and 'move-deal-stage' act on it), and once more with no deal when they are on none. Only personal meetings (never a webinar or an all-day block), only meetings upcoming or started within the last day (a held meeting replayed by a later sync is history), and once across Google, AngelSend's calendar and the booking. trigger_config gates on { has_deal: 'yes'|'no', stage_kind: 'open'|'won'|'lost' (the deal's CURRENT column; never matches the no-deal event), pipeline_id, source: 'angelsend_booking'|'google-calendar'|'angelsend' }. This is the 'they booked a call → move the deal to Engaged / open a prep task' trigger. All of them accept trigger_config { source: '<provider slug>' } to narrow to one provider. Each external record fires AT MOST ONCE, ever (per rule) — re-syncing the same email cannot re-trigger it. All of them accept trigger_config { source: '<provider slug>' } to narrow to one provider. Each external record fires AT MOST ONCE, ever (per rule) — re-syncing the same email cannot re-trigger it. An external event an invoke-agent rule's hourly cap refuses is PARKED and retried on later ticks for up to 24 hours, never run twice. action_type values: - 'assign' { user: <id|'current'|'creator'> } - 'change-status' { status_id } - 'set-field' { field: 'priority'|'tag'|'due_date', value, offset_days? } - 'add-tag' / 'remove-tag' { tag } - 'add-comment' { body } (supports ${task.title} / ${task.id} interpolation) - 'move-to-project' { project_ref } - 'send-notification' { body?, title?, kind?, to? } — posts an in-app notification on the task's project feed. Without `to` it reaches everyone who can see the project; with `to` ONLY the people it names see it and count it: 'assignee' (the task's assignee), 'admins' (workspace owners and admins), or a member's name or email — comma-separate several. A name with no account in this workspace is skipped, and if nobody matches the firing is skipped (never broadcast). Name a rule for who it actually reaches. body supports ${task.title} / ${task.id}; kind defaults to 'overdue'. - 'set-property' { property_id|property_key, value } — set a custom property value on the triggering task. Computed-type props are rejected. - 'invoke-agent' { instruction, run_as?, max_per_hour?, send_mode? } — hand the event to YOU (the agent) to handle with your full toolset. `instruction` is what you'll be asked to do, in plain language ('Triage this email: if it is a support request, create a task in the Support project and reply acknowledging it'). This is the ONLY action that works with external-event triggers, and the only one that can do open-ended work. The run is queued (not instant) and executes under the run-as user's autonomy level — risky actions are still policy-gated and may park for approval. In SAFE mode it CANNOT send anything. To let a rule's runs send (e.g. reply to an email), set send_mode: 'approval' (every send parks for a human — recommended) or 'auto' (sends go out unreviewed; owners/admins only; a workspace block still wins). Neither exceeds the workspace's autonomy ceiling. For 'let me email the agent', a Gmail note-to-self counts as inbound, and from_member: true limits it to the team. DEAL actions — these need a deal trigger ('deal-stage-changed' or 'deal-document-signed'), and are ADMIN-ONLY to create because each acts outside Kavanah irreversibly. They share one per-workspace hourly cap, so a bulk stage move cannot fan out: - 'provision-client-space' { slack?, slack_private?, slack_prefix?, slack_invite_emails?, invite_deal_team?, auto_staff?, drive?, drive_parent_folder_id?, drive_subfolders?, run_as? } — create the deal's Slack channel and Google Drive folder, inviting the deal team. When the workspace has turned on automatic staffing (off by default), the deal's team is first filled to the workspace's minimum size and given a lead if it has none; auto_staff:false keeps one rule out of that. Idempotent per deal: it records what it made and skips whichever half already exists, so re-firing never opens a second channel. - 'send-engagement-envelope' { templates?, template_id | template_name, prefill?, contact_role?, email_subject?, email_blurb?, run_as? } — send an XDocs template to the deal's signer (XDocs is the only e-signature provider; the run-as user must have XDocs connected, and the template must have exactly one signer slot). templates: [{ when: { category?, sector?, issuance_stage? (text or list), pipeline_id?, min_amount_cents?, max_amount_cents? (whole cents, inclusive) }, template_name | template_id, prefill? }] — checked IN ORDER, first match wins, falling back to the top-level template_name/template_id; with no match and no fallback the firing is skipped with the reason. An entry an earlier one always beats is refused at save. prefill: { '<placeholder label>': '<deal field>' } writes the deal's terms into the template's [Placeholder] text — fields: name, amount_cents, revenue_cents (written as money in the deal's currency), currency, sector, category, issuance_stage, geography, expected_close (written as a date), owner_name, custom_fields.<name>. An unknown field is refused at save; a term the deal has no value for stops the send and names the field — nothing is ever sent with a blank term. Skips if a live envelope (anything not declined/voided/expired, INCLUDING a signed one) already exists on the deal. Template names must match EXACTLY; it refuses to guess between near matches rather than send the wrong contract. - 'enroll-cadence' { cadence, contact_role?, provider?, run_as? } — enroll the deal's OWN contacts (the issuer's people already on the deal) in a cadence. Defaults to the PRIMARY contact only; pass contact_role:'all' to enroll everyone on the deal, which includes any investor a campaign linked to it. Steps send through the run-as user's mailbox, never the person who moved the card. This is NOT an investor campaign. - 'start-investor-campaign' { cadence, batch_size?, contacts_per_firm?, auto_release?, provider?, run_as? } — THE action for investor outreach: ranks the workspace's investors against the deal's investment profile, releases the first tranche (batch_size, default 100), picks up to contacts_per_firm people per firm (default 1, max 3; warmest with an email first, then the most senior title), links them to the deal and enrolls them in 'cadence' (a DEAL cadence). Skips if the deal has no investment profile yet. A re-fire tops up the open tranche and never releases the next one; auto_release:true (default false) lets the 6-hourly scan release and enroll the next tranche once every released firm has been approached or dismissed. At most 5 campaigns start per workspace per hour. - 'start-issuer-campaign' { campaign, cadence?, batch_size?, contacts_per_firm?, auto_release?, provider?, run_as? } — client PROSPECTING: starts the named issuer campaign (id or exact name, see list_issuer_campaigns) — ranks the workspace's issuers against its mandate if never ranked, releases the FIRST tranche and enrolls the best contact at each firm in the campaign's NETWORK cadence (or 'cadence'). It needs no deal, but it only runs on something a member did — a task trigger or a deal trigger; an external event (an inbound email, a webhook) is skipped. A re-fire tops up the open tranche and never releases the next; auto_release omitted keeps the campaign's own setting. Admin-only to create, under the same shared hourly cap, and at most 5 issuer campaigns start per workspace per hour. INTERNAL deal-side actions — they stay inside Kavanah, so any member may create them and they are not under the deal actions' cap: - 'move-deal-stage' { to_stage_id | to_stage (exact stage name), only_forward? (default true) } — move the event's deal (a 'meeting-booked', 'deal-stage-changed' or 'deal-document-signed' trigger) to a stage of ITS pipeline, as the rule's author. Skips a closed deal, a deal already in that stage, a backwards move under only_forward, and a stage not in the deal's pipeline. The move fires the 'deal-stage-changed' rules, so 'meeting booked → move to Engaged' chains into the engagement rules; one rule refuses to move the same deal twice within an hour, so two rules cannot ping-pong. - 'create-task' { title, project_ref, description?, assign_to?, due_in_days?, priority? } — open a task in a project on ANY trigger, as the rule's author, once per event (a re-synced booking or a retried event finds it already there). Placeholders in title/description: ${deal.name}, ${contact.name}, ${contact.company}, ${meeting.start} (in the author's timezone), ${event.summary}, and ${task.title} / ${task.id} on a task trigger; one the event has no value for renders empty. assign_to: 'deal_lead' (the deal's owner), 'rule_author', 'none', or a member's roster name or email — someone who cannot be resolved leaves the task unassigned rather than inventing an assignee. due_in_days 0–365; priority Normal|Medium|High. The project is checked when the rule fires. Use 'invoke-agent' when the response needs judgment; use the fixed actions when the response is mechanical (they are cheaper and deterministic). Pass project_ref to scope a TASK or property rule to one project, or omit for workspace-wide. Deal-stage and external-event rules are ALWAYS workspace-wide — those events belong to no project, so a project_ref there is ignored (a rule tied to a project could never fire).

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional. Scopes a task/property rule to one project; ignored for deal-stage and external-event triggers.

params.name: trigger_config
params.description: Type-specific trigger configuration

params.name: action_config
params.description: Type-specific action configuration

params.name: enabled
params.description: Default true

tools.name: create_availability_request
tools.description: Open a new availability request (leader → team). project_ref is optional — omit for a workspace-wide ask. Dates are ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

params.name: message
params.description: Body of the request to the team.

params.name: period_start

params.name: period_end
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD

params.name: project_ref

params.name: due_date

tools.name: create_boardroom
tools.description: Create a standing exec meeting between AI executive personas. The personas must already exist (create them first with the persona roster if needed) — a seat references a persona by id. The meeting runs in three phases: each exec delivers a performance update on its own area using read-only tools, then the table discusses, then the chair closes with action items which become tasks. IMPORTANT: this only creates the room. It does NOT start it meeting — the workspace admin must turn on 'Exec meetings' in Settings → AI Agent and arm the boardroom, because each meeting costs real model usage. Say so when you create one.

params.name: name
params.description: What the meeting is called, e.g. 'Daily Leadership Sync'.

params.name: kind
params.description: What kind of standing meeting this is. exec (default): executives give a performance update. board: directors review the North Star and the strategy and endorse or flag it (advisory to the humans). department: a VP and their directors review the team. standup: a short daily done/next/blocked check-in for an IC team — pair it with frequency 'weekdays' and 0 discussion rounds.

params.name: model
params.description: Optional model for every seat in this series: a model id, 'auto' (a router picks the cheapest model that fits), or 'default' to use each employee's own model / the workspace background model. A cheaper model makes a stand-up much cheaper.

params.name: agenda
params.description: Optional standing agenda, prepended to every exec's update prompt. Use for things the meeting must always cover, e.g. 'Always lead with runway and churn.'

params.name: chair_persona_id
params.description: The persona who chairs: opens the meeting and writes the closing synthesis and action items. Usually the CEO persona. Required before the meeting can run.

params.name: seats
params.description: Who sits at the table (2-6). Each exec reports only on its own area, bounded by that persona's allowed_scopes — so give the CFO persona the `finance` scope, the CRO `crm`, and so on, or its update will have nothing to read.

params.name: discussion_rounds
params.description: Rounds of open discussion after the updates. 0-3, default 2. This is the biggest cost lever: each round is one model call PER SEAT.

params.name: frequency
params.description: Default daily. weekdays skips Saturday and Sunday (UTC) — use it for stand-ups.

params.name: hour_utc
params.description: Hour to meet, 0-23, UTC. Convert from the user's local time (8am PST = 16).

params.name: minute_utc
params.description: Minute, 0-59. Default 0.

params.name: day_of_week
params.description: For weekly only: 0=Sunday … 6=Saturday.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.description: Schedule a meeting / calendar event. Stored as a task with tag='Meeting' so it appears on calendars, timelines, and reminders. Use this when the user asks to schedule a meeting, set up an event, book time on the calendar, or anything similar — do not fall back to create_task for time-of-day events.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project reference the event belongs to. Required so the event surfaces on that project's calendar.

params.name: title
params.description: Event title (e.g., "Audit follow-up review").

params.name: start
params.description: Event start. Preferred: naked local time `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` (24-hour, no `Z`, no offset) — the handler will interpret it in the user's timezone (shown in the system prompt). You may also send ISO 8601 with an explicit offset (e.g. `2026-06-09T13:00-07:00`). Never hand-compute a UTC `Z` time. Use `YYYY-MM-DD` for all-day events.

params.name: end
params.description: Optional event end, same format rules as `start`. If omitted, provide `duration_minutes` instead.

params.name: duration_minutes
params.description: Optional duration in minutes (used when `end` is not provided).

params.name: location
params.description: Optional location or video link.

params.name: attendees
params.description: Optional comma-separated list of attendee names.

params.name: description
params.description: Optional agenda / notes for the event.

tools.name: create_chat_channel
tools.description: Create a new workspace chat channel with the caller as its first admin member. Use for team spaces; not for one-off DMs (use post_chat_message).

params.name: name
params.description: Channel name (without a leading #).

params.name: description
params.description: Optional channel description/topic.

params.name: is_private
params.description: When true, only invited members can see/join. Default false (public).

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project ref to scope the channel to a project. Omit for a workspace-level channel.

tools.name: create_client
tools.description: Create a new client. Only company is required. Omit contact_name and email when you do not know them — never invent placeholder people or addresses; a fabricated email can misdirect real client communication later.

params.name: logo_url
params.description: Direct URL of an image to use as the client's logo. Leave unset to keep the automatic behavior (the logo is derived from the website's OpenGraph image or favicon). Pass an empty string to clear an override and go back to auto-detection.

params.name: links
params.description: Reference links for this client — dataroom, Drive folder, contract, press kit, anything. `label` is free text; there is no fixed set of link types. URLs must be http/https. Replaces the whole list, so include existing links you want to keep (read them first with get_client_links).

params.name: next_renewal
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: create_component
tools.description: Create a component on a project. lead_user_id is the workspace user owning the component (optional).

tools.name: create_custom_property
