Both are computed at read time and never stored as values. For select/multi_select, pass config.options as [{value, label, color?}].

params.name: name
params.description: Display name

params.name: key
params.description: Stable key used in formulas / API. Auto-derived from name if omitted.

params.name: config
params.description: Type-specific config. select/multi_select: {options:[…]}; formula: {expression:'…'}; rollup: {source:'children'|'related', aggregator:'sum'|'count'|'avg'|…, target_key:'…'}

tools.name: create_custom_status
tools.description: Create a new custom status (board column) on a project. `slug` must be unique within the project and contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and dashes (e.g. 'in-review', 'blocked'). `category` controls how the board treats the column for completion/cycle-time math: 'backlog' (not started), 'active' (in flight), 'done' (counts as completed), or 'cancelled' (terminal, doesn't count as done).

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project ref (e.g. '1').

params.name: name
params.description: Display name for the column.

params.name: slug
params.description: URL/identifier slug. Lowercase letters, numbers, and dashes only.

params.name: color
params.description: Optional column accent color, hex (e.g. '#8bb7ff'). Defaults to a neutral gray.

params.name: category
params.description: How the column is classified for completion math. Defaults to 'active'.

params.name: wip_limit
params.description: Optional WIP cap (non-negative integer). Tasks past the cap are flagged on the board.

params.name: sort_order
params.description: Optional sort order. Higher values appear further right. Defaults to next-available (100 after the current max).

tools.name: create_deal
tools.description: Create a new deal in the workspace. Pipeline defaults to the workspace default. Stage defaults to the first 'open' stage. Amount/revenue are dollars (NOT cents) — the tool converts.

params.name: name
params.description: Deal name (e.g. 'Acme — Series B').

params.name: pipeline
params.description: Pipeline id or slug. Defaults to workspace default.

params.name: stage
params.description: Stage id or slug. Defaults to the first open stage.

params.name: revenue_dollars
params.description: Fee or commission to Kavanah's workspace, in dollars.

params.name: expected_close
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD.

params.name: category
params.description: Line of business this deal belongs to ('Series A', 'Secondaries', 'Fund II'). Free text — use whatever the desk already calls it; do not invent a taxonomy. Drives the Deal Room's Rollup breakdown, where deals with none are grouped as Uncategorised.

params.name: contact_name
params.description: If set, also create/link a primary contact.

tools.name: create_deal_cadence
tools.description: Define a reusable follow-up cadence: an ordered list of email steps, each a number of days after the previous. Bodies/subjects may use {{contact_name}}, {{contact_first_name}}, {{deal_name}}, {{sender_name}}, and {{booking_link}} (the cadence's booking_url — a step using it is refused unless booking_url is set). Or start from a TEMPLATE: template 'issuer-curious' is a 3-step NETWORK cadence for issuer prospecting in a curious tone — wanting to learn about their business, offering to sign their NDA first, exploring fit — that never assumes the prospect is raising; it fills the steps, kind and name you leave out. Show the user the template's copy before you create it. Creating a cadence sends NOTHING — sends only start when someone explicitly enrolls a deal contact.

params.name: template
params.description: Start from a template. Fills steps, kind and name when you omit them; anything you pass wins.

params.name: steps
params.description: 1–8 steps. First step's days_after_previous is measured from enrollment (0 = immediately).

params.name: sender_pool
params.description: Display names to rotate across arms, for testing which sender identity performs best. At most 4 entries (one per arm, A–D); more, or an entry missing user_id or from_name, is refused rather than silently dropped. Each entry needs a user_id whose mailbox is connected — the from_name is a DISPLAY override only, because a From name with no mailbox behind it fails SPF/DKIM and lands in spam.

params.name: kind
params.description: 'deal' (default) — enrolled as (deal, contact), and cancelled if the deal closes. 'network' — investor / issuer / BD relationship outreach that is not about a transaction, enrolled against a contact alone. A network cadence gets the same A/B arms, personalization and stop-on-reply as a deal one; before this existed, non-deal campaigns had to run outside Kavanah and inherited none of it.

params.name: enforce_structure
params.description: Refuse to save any step that is not in the house shape (second_paragraph + exactly 3 bullets + a non-yes/no cta). Off by default. Turning it on later re-validates the steps already stored and fails if they do not comply, rather than reading as enforced while sending unstructured bodies.

params.name: include_unsubscribe
params.description: Append an unsubscribe line to every email and, on native Gmail / iCloud / ProtonMail sends, the one-click List-Unsubscribe headers. Default TRUE. Always on for a network cadence (cold outreach legally needs an opt-out) — passing false there is refused. Someone who unsubscribes goes on this workspace's suppression list and every sequence they are in stops.

params.name: booking_url
params.description: The booking page {{booking_link}} renders to, e.g. https://calendly.com/your-name/intro. Must be a public https URL (no http:, no credentials, no spaces). Required when any step uses {{booking_link}}.

tools.name: create_decision

Pick a metric_source: 'task_completion_rate' (%, optionally per project), 'open_task_count', 'overdue_task_count', 'tasks_completed_last_7d', 'manual' (you set the number), or 'clearbooks_metric' (a finance number read live via the clearbooks_* tools). Set a target_value and comparator ('gte' = at least, 'lte' = at most, 'eq' = exactly). warn_threshold is the fraction of target (e.g. 0.1 = 10%) inside which the goal is 'at risk' rather than 'off track'.

params.name: project_ref

params.name: metric_key

params.name: target_value

params.name: warn_threshold
params.description: At-risk band as a fraction of target. Default 0.1.

params.name: unit
params.description: Optional unit label, e.g. '%', '$', 'tasks'.

params.name: due_date
params.description: Optional deadline (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: create_invoice_from_billable_time
tools.description: Create a DRAFT ClearBooks invoice from a client's unbilled billable time and stamp those entries as invoiced. Draft only — this never sends anything; emailing the invoice stays behind clearbooks_send_invoice. Requires the client to have a stored ClearBooks customer mapping, or pass clearbooks_customer_id explicitly (find it with clearbooks_list_customers; an explicit id is remembered on the client when it has no mapping yet). Already-invoiced entries are never selected again, so a retry cannot double-bill. Preview first with preview_billable_time. Admin only.

params.name: client_id
params.description: Kavanah client id (look up with list_clients).

params.name: from
params.description: Optional ISO timestamp — only entries started at/after this.

params.name: to
params.description: Optional ISO timestamp — only entries started at/before this.

params.name: project_refs
params.description: Optional subset of the client's project refs.

params.name: clearbooks_customer_id
params.description: ClearBooks customer UUID; needed only when the client has no stored mapping.

params.name: invoice_date
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today server-side.

params.name: due_date

params.name: notes
params.description: Optional notes shown on the invoice.

tools.name: create_knowledge_document
tools.description: Create a knowledge document. Prefer structured `blocks` over `body` — each block has {id, type, text} where type is one of paragraph, heading_1..3, bulleted_list_item, numbered_list_item, todo, quote, callout, code, divider. Use [[Page Title]] inside text to link to another doc. Set is_template=true to register a reusable template; pair with template_category to surface it under a heading in the templates gallery.

params.name: body
params.description: Plain markdown fallback. Ignored when `blocks` is supplied. Prefer `blocks`.

params.name: blocks
params.description: Block array. Each element: { id (any stable string), type, text, checked? (todo), language? (code), emoji? (callout) }.

params.name: icon

params.name: template_category

params.name: project_ref

params.name: parent_document_id
params.description: Optional existing document id to nest this page under (keeps the library tree organized). Omit for a top-level page.

tools.name: create_message_template
tools.description: Create a reusable message template.

tools.name: create_my_note

tools.name: create_my_todo
tools.description: Add a to-do item to the caller's own private list. New items sort to the top. Personal data only.

params.name: text
params.description: The to-do text.

tools.name: create_network_contact
tools.description: Create or update ONE person in the Deal Room network — an investor, a family-office principal, a broker-dealer contact — with NO deal attached. This is the tool for someone you found rather than someone on a live deal; add_deal_contact is for the latter and needs a deal_id. GAP-FILLS: a value already on the record is never replaced, tags are added rather than swapped, and a contact already attached to a firm keeps that firm. An address whose contact was merged away lands on the record it was merged INTO, so a scan can never un-merge what a person just merged. Undoable while nothing has used the contact.

params.name: full_name
params.description: The person's name, as it should display.

params.name: email
params.description: Their address, when you actually have one. Never invent or guess an address — the workspace's sending reputation pays for a bounce.

params.name: company
params.description: Where they work, as free text. WITHOUT an email this is what identifies them: a person with no address and no company cannot be saved, because the next scan would create them again.

params.name: title
params.description: Their role, e.g. 'Managing Partner'.

params.name: tags
params.description: Lowercase labels to filter on later, e.g. ['family-office','data-centre']. ADDED to any tags the contact already carries — nothing is dropped.

params.name: notes
params.description: What you learned about them. Only written when the contact has no notes yet.

params.name: relationship_status
params.description: A human label for the relationship ('Warm', 'Cold', 'Introduced'). Distinct from the computed warmth score. Only written when none is set.

params.name: firm
params.description: The institution they belong to — a firm id, or a firm NAME, in which case the firm is resolved by name (and created if it is genuinely new) exactly as upsert_firm would. A contact already pointed at a firm is never re-pointed.

params.name: source
params.description: Where this person came from — 'linkedin', 'referral', 'conference'. Recorded on the record, kept for ever once set, and what lets someone ask later which contacts a scan produced. Defaults to 'agent'.

params.name: firm_roles
params.description: Roles for a firm this call CREATES. An existing firm keeps the roles it has. Without one, a new firm is created with no roles and will not appear in role-filtered lists or investor ranking.

tools.name: create_onboarding_doc

tools.name: create_org

params.name: description

tools.name: create_recurring_task
tools.description: Create a recurring-task generator. recurrence_rule is an iCal-style RRULE string (e.g. 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO'). For a reminder that should run only UNTIL some task is done ("remind me daily until #5074 is closed"), set stop_when_task_completed to that task's id — the generator switches itself off once that task is completed or deleted. Without it the rule runs forever.

params.name: recurrence_rule
params.description: RRULE string

params.name: next_due

tools.name: create_report

params.description: Display name shown in the Reports list.

params.name: report_type
params.description: Report type. One of: status, burndown, burnup, cycle_time, lead_time, velocity, completion_rate, overdue, new_vs_resolved, time_tracking, billing, cross_project, client_health, discussion_activity, storage_usage, workspace_usage, custom, progress_weekly, progress_monthly, progress_yearly, my_work, daily_digest. `my_work` / `daily_digest` produce a personalized 'what should I work on today' brief (overdue + due-today + due-soon + in-progress tasks) for one person — ideal for a recurring morning email via create_report_schedule.

params.name: config
params.description: Optional per-report configuration. For most types: project_ref, date range, etc. For my_work / daily_digest: `user_id` (defaults to you if omitted) and `horizon_days` (how many days ahead counts as 'due soon', default 7). Defaults to {}.

tools.name: create_report_schedule
tools.description: Schedule a recurring report. Provide a 5-field UTC cron expression (e.g. `0 9 * * MON` for every Monday at 09:00 UTC) plus a recipient set. Recipients can be any combination of literal emails AND dynamic groups (workspace, project members, team members, department members, individual member user_ids). Dynamic groups re-resolve at every delivery, so adding a user to a department auto-includes them in the next report. Use `list_reports` first to obtain the `report_id`.

params.name: report_id
params.description: ID of an existing saved report (see `list_reports` / `create_report`).

params.name: cron_expression

params.name: format

params.name: recipient_emails
params.description: Optional literal email addresses. May be empty if `recipient_groups` is provided.

params.name: recipient_groups

Any combination of: { workspace_all: boolean, project_refs: string[], team_ids: string[], team_handles: string[], department_ids: string[], department_names: string[], user_ids: string[], emails: string[] }. Resolved to actual addresses at every delivery, so membership changes (someone joins a department) automatically affect who gets the report. Cross-reference with `list_departments`, `list_projects`, and the workspace teams catalog to pick valid identifiers.

params.name: enabled

tools.name: drive_create_folder
tools.description: Create a new (empty) folder in the user's Google Drive. Returns the new folder's id and web-view link. Pass parent_folder_id to nest it inside an existing folder; omit it to create the folder at the top level of My Drive. To populate the folder afterward, create files with drive_create_text_file (parent_folder_id = this folder's id) or move existing items in with drive_move_file.

params.name: name
params.description: Folder name.

params.name: parent_folder_id
params.description: Optional Drive folder id to create this folder inside (the `/folders/<id>` segment of a Drive URL).

tools.name: drive_create_text_file
tools.description: Create a new text file in the user's Google Drive with the given UTF-8 content. Returns the new file's id and (when available) a web-view link. Use this to save notes, transcripts, or short documents to Drive — for binary uploads or large files use the Drive UI directly. IMPORTANT: create at most ONE file per response — never batch several file creations in one turn, and for a long document keep the content focused (a very large content argument can exceed the response window and fail). When asked to save multiple documents, create the first, wait for its result, then continue with the next in your following response.

params.name: name
params.description: Filename (with or without extension).

params.name: content
params.description: UTF-8 text content. Empty string creates an empty file.

params.name: mime_type
params.description: Optional MIME type (e.g. `text/markdown`). Defaults to `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`.

params.name: parent_folder_id
params.description: Optional Drive folder id to create the file inside.

tools.name: drive_delete_file
tools.description: Delete a Google Drive file or folder. By default the item is moved to the Drive trash (recoverable, and undoable). Set permanent=true to delete it irreversibly — there is NO undo for a permanent delete, so only use it when the user explicitly asks to delete permanently. Deleting a folder removes everything inside it; confirm with the user before deleting a folder. Pass the id, not a URL.

params.name: file_id
params.description: The Drive file or folder id to delete.

params.name: permanent
params.description: When true, permanently delete (irreversible) instead of moving to trash. Default false.

tools.name: drive_get_file
tools.description: Look up a single Google Drive file or folder by its id and return its metadata (name, MIME type, modified time, size, web-view link, parent folder, trashed flag). When the user pastes a file URL like `https://docs.google.com/document/d/<FILE_ID>/edit` or `https://drive.google.com/file/d/<FILE_ID>/view`, extract the `<FILE_ID>` (the segment after `/d/`) and pass it here. IGNORE any `/u/<N>/` or `?u=<N>` part of the URL — it is only the account index signed into the user's browser and is irrelevant to this connector, which uses Kavanah's own server-side OAuth token. If the MIME type is `application/vnd.google-apps.folder`, use drive_list_files with `query: "'<FILE_ID>' in parents"` to see what's inside.

params.name: file_id
params.description: The Drive file or folder id (the `/d/<id>` or `/folders/<id>` segment of a Drive URL).

tools.name: drive_import_to_knowledge
tools.description: Deep-dive Google Drive content INTO the company knowledge base: reads up to 20 Drive files (by explicit file_ids, or a Drive query like "'<folderId>' in parents") and creates one knowledge document per file. mode='full_text' (default) stores the file's text; mode='summarize' condenses each file with an LLM first (slower, one call per file). Imports are idempotent — each document is tagged with its Drive file id, so re-importing skips already-imported files unless overwrite=true (which refreshes the existing document). PDFs and uploaded Word/Excel/PowerPoint files are read by converting a temporary copy, so a whole data-room folder can be imported in one call. Folders, images and video are skipped with a reason. Optionally file everything under a parent knowledge document and/or a project.

params.name: file_ids
params.description: Explicit Drive file ids (or URLs) to import (max 20). Use this OR query.

params.name: query
params.description: Drive search query to select files (e.g. "'<folderId>' in parents", "name contains 'spec'"). Used when file_ids is omitted.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max files to import when using query (1..20, default 10).

params.name: mode
params.description: full_text (default) = store the file's text verbatim; summarize = LLM-condense each file into sections first.

params.name: overwrite
params.description: true = refresh a previously imported document with the file's current content. Default false (skip already-imported files).

params.name: parent_document_id
params.description: Optional knowledge document id to nest all imported docs under (keeps the library organized).

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project ref to scope the imported docs to. Omitted = workspace-shared.

tools.name: drive_list_files
tools.description: List files in the user's Google Drive. The connector uses the full `drive` scope, so ALL of the user's Drive files are visible (not just files created with or opened through Kavanah). Supports Drive's query syntax (e.g. `name contains 'report'`, `mimeType='application/pdf'`, `modifiedTime > '2026-01-01'`). When the user gives a Drive folder URL like `https://drive.google.com/drive/u/4/folders/<FOLDER_ID>`, extract the trailing `<FOLDER_ID>` and list the folder's contents with `query: "'<FOLDER_ID>' in parents"`. IGNORE the `/u/<N>/` segment in the URL: it is only the account index of whichever Google account is signed into the user's *browser*, and has NOTHING to do with which account this connector is authorized for. This tool authenticates with Kavanah's own server-side OAuth token, not the browser session, so `/u/0/`, `/u/4/`, etc. are all irrelevant here — never tell the user a folder is inaccessible because of the `/u/N/` number. If a folder ID genuinely returns nothing or errors, the real causes are that the connected Google account lacks access to that folder (ask them to share it with the connected account) or the folder is empty.

params.name: query
params.description: Optional Drive query string (same syntax as the Drive API `q` parameter).

params.name: page_size
params.description: Max files to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: drive_move_file
tools.description: Move a Google Drive file or folder into a different folder. By default the item is removed from its current parent folder(s) and placed in the new one (a true move). Set keep_in_current=true to instead ADD the new folder as an additional location (the item then appears in both). Pass ids, not URLs (the `/d/<id>` or `/folders/<id>` segment).

params.name: file_id
params.description: The Drive file or folder id to move.

params.name: new_parent_folder_id
params.description: The destination folder id. Use 'root' for the top level of My Drive.

params.name: keep_in_current
params.description: When true, keep the item in its current folder(s) too instead of moving it out. Default false (move).

tools.name: drive_read_file
tools.description: Read a Google Drive file's CONTENT as plain text. Google Docs/Slides export as text, Sheets as CSV, and text-like uploads (txt/md/csv/json/code) download directly. PDFs and uploaded Word/Excel/PowerPoint files ARE readable too — Drive converts a temporary copy to read them, which is how a deal data room full of PPMs and decks gets analysed; the user's file is never modified. A scanned, image-only PDF will come back with a note saying so rather than blank text. Images, video and archives are still refused with a reason. Use it to inspect a file before answering questions about it — for bulk import into the knowledge base use drive_import_to_knowledge instead.

params.name: file_id
params.description: The Drive file id (or URL) to read.

params.name: max_chars
params.description: Cap on returned characters (1000..20000, default 20000). Longer content is truncated with a note.

tools.name: drive_rename_file
tools.description: Rename a Google Drive file OR folder. Pass the item's id (the `/d/<id>` or `/folders/<id>` segment of a Drive URL — ignore any `/u/<N>/` part) and the new name. Returns the updated name and link.

params.name: file_id
params.description: The Drive file or folder id to rename.

params.name: new_name
params.description: The new name.

tools.name: duplicate_project_file
tools.description: Duplicate a project file (creates a `_copy` version).

tools.name: duplicate_role
tools.description: Duplicate an existing role (system or custom) into a new custom role with the same permissions, as a starting point for editing. Creates a new grantable role. Requires workspace owner/admin.

params.name: role_id
params.description: Id (UUID) of the source role to copy.

params.name: new_name
params.description: Name for the new duplicated role (must be unique).

tools.name: duplicate_saved_view
tools.description: Duplicate a saved view. The copy is owned by the caller, defaults to private (shared=false), and appends ' (copy)' to the name.

tools.name: duplicate_tasks
tools.description: Duplicate one or more tasks. Creates copies in the same or a different project.

params.name: task_ids
params.description: Task IDs to duplicate

params.name: target_project_ref
params.description: Optional: project to duplicate into (defaults to same project)

tools.name: email_my_digest
tools.description: Email a Kavanah digest to YOURSELF (the current user, or in a scheduled run the run owner), to a named teammate in THIS workspace (`to_member`), or — inside a scheduled run — to someone OUTSIDE the workspace (`to_email`). Use `to_member` for per-person reminders to members ('each morning, email Sophia her open HR tasks'). Use `to_email` when a schedule's instructions name an outside address ('email the forecast to mitch@example.com'): it goes out as a normal email from the schedule owner's connected mailbox. `to_email` reaches ONLY addresses written in the running schedule's own instructions, and works only in a scheduled run — in a conversation, send outside email with gmail_send_email or your connected mail tool. This is the delivery step for a briefing: gather the content with your other tools (tasks, goals, waiting-on ledger, calendar), then call this to send it. Works inside a safe-mode scheduled run, where the general email-send tools are unavailable. One recipient per call. Provide the fully-composed subject and body.

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line. Defaults to 'Your Kavanah digest'.

params.name: body
params.description: The message body. Plain text (or lightweight markdown) by default; set is_html:true if you're passing HTML.

params.name: to_member
params.description: Optional. Name of a teammate in THIS workspace to send to (matched case-insensitively against members and the People roster — a first name is fine). Omit to email yourself / the run owner. An unknown or ambiguous name is reported back and NOTHING is sent — it never silently falls back to your own inbox. For someone outside the workspace use to_email.

params.name: to_email
params.description: Optional, scheduled runs only. One outside email address to send the digest to, as a normal email from the schedule owner's connected mailbox. It must be an address the schedule's own instructions name — any other address is refused and nothing is sent. Do not combine with to_member.

params.name: is_html
params.description: Set true if `body` is HTML rather than plain text. Defaults to false.

tools.name: enqueue_bulk_create_tasks
tools.description: Enqueue a background job that creates many tasks in one project. Use this instead of bulk_create_tasks when more than ~25 tasks need to be created — the job runs out-of-band so the chat doesn't block. Returns a job id; the agent will post a follow-up message in this conversation when the job finishes.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project id (string form, e.g. "1").

params.name: tasks
params.description: List of tasks to create. Each item is the same shape used by bulk_create_tasks.

tools.name: enrich_firm_profile
tools.description: Look up a company and fold what is found into its firm record — website, LinkedIn, description, industry, location. FREE. Never overwrites a field a human curated, and never replaces a value the workspace already holds; it fills gaps only. Use it to flesh out a firm before scoring it against a deal.

params.name: firm_id
params.description: An existing firm to enrich.

params.name: domain
params.description: Company domain, when creating or matching by domain.

params.name: name
params.description: Company name.

params.name: roles
params.description: Roles to set if the firm is newly created. Existing roles are never removed.

tools.name: enroll_contact_in_network_cadence
tools.description: Enroll a contact in a NETWORK cadence — relationship / BD outreach that is not about a deal. This ARMS UNATTENDED OUTBOUND EMAIL exactly as enroll_deal_in_cadence does: every step sends through the enrolling user's mailbox until the sequence completes, the contact replies (stop-on-reply), or someone stops it. Confirm with the user first. ONE active network cadence per contact workspace-wide — two campaigns emailing the same person is the thing that guard exists to prevent.

params.name: cadence
params.description: A cadence whose kind is 'network' — id or exact name.

params.name: provider
params.description: Send provider. Defaults to auto.

tools.name: enroll_contacts_in_cadence
tools.description: Enroll up to 200 contacts in one cadence in a single call, and get back what happened to EACH one: enrolled (with the first send time), already enrolled, not on the deal, no email, suppressed (on a do-not-email list), archived, not found, or an error. This ARMS UNATTENDED OUTBOUND EMAIL to every contact enrolled: each step sends through your mailbox until the sequence ends, they reply, or someone stops it — confirm with the user first. For a DEAL cadence pass deal_id; a contact must be on the deal, because stop-on-reply follows the deal's contacts — pass add_to_deal to link the ones who are not (as role 'other'). For a NETWORK cadence omit deal_id. One active cadence per contact per deal, and one active network cadence per contact. More than 200 contacts is refused, not truncated. For investors on a deal, start_investor_campaign does the picking and linking for you.

params.name: cadence
params.description: Cadence id or exact name (list_deal_cadences).

params.name: contact_ids
params.description: Deal-contact ids, 1 to 200.

params.name: deal_id
params.description: Required for a deal cadence; omit for a network cadence.

params.name: add_to_deal
params.description: Link contacts who are not yet on the deal (role 'other') before enrolling them. Default false: they are reported as not on the deal.

params.name: provider
params.description: Send provider. Defaults to auto.

tools.name: enroll_deal_in_cadence
tools.description: Enroll a deal's contact in a follow-up cadence. This ARMS UNATTENDED OUTBOUND EMAIL: every step sends automatically through the enrolling user's mailbox until the sequence completes, the contact replies (stop-on-reply), or someone stops it. Confirm with the user before enrolling. One active cadence per contact per deal.

params.name: cadence
params.description: Cadence id or exact name.

params.name: provider
params.description: Send provider. Defaults to auto.

tools.name: escalate_to_user
tools.description: Escalate something that needs a human. The workspace escalation policy routes it: at/above the immediate-severity threshold (outside quiet hours) recipients get an alert + push right now; otherwise it's queued as a morning-briefing alert. Use 'critical' ONLY for urgent, business-impacting issues (it can break through quiet hours); 'warning' for needs-attention-today (blocked work, 2+-nudge waiting-on entries, pending approvals); 'info' for FYI items. Don't escalate what a task comment or notification already covers. One escalation per subject (task, deal or headline) per 7 days; a repeat is not re-sent.

params.name: severity
params.description: How urgent this is. Drives immediate-vs-deferred routing.

params.name: title
params.description: Short headline (under ~80 chars).

params.name: message
params.description: What happened, why it matters, and what you need from the human.

params.name: action_url
params.description: Optional in-app path to act on it (e.g. '/projects/2').

params.name: related_task_id
params.description: Optional Kavanah task id.

tools.name: estimate_meeting_twin_cost
tools.description: Preview sending the caller's OWN AI twin (audio or video) or the silent notetaker to an outside Zoom / Google Meet / Microsoft Teams / Webex meeting: whether it is allowed right now (and if not, exactly why, in plain words), the most it can cost (Kavanah credits and what the vendors bill the workspace), the bot's display name and the disclosure it says first. Creates nothing. Use before dispatch_meeting_twin.

params.name: meeting_url
params.description: The full https:// meeting join link.

params.name: mode
params.description: audio = twin speaks in the caller's voice; video = twin with their video avatar; notetaker = a silent bot that only records and transcribes a meeting the caller attends.

params.name: max_minutes
params.description: Hard cap on time in the meeting (default 45, max 90).

tools.name: estimate_task_time
tools.description: Estimate how long a task will take using the AI estimator. Takes the task's title, description, project context, assignee role, and comparable past tasks into account, then writes back a single value + unit (minutes/hours/days) and a ± uncertainty range. Pass a single task_id or up to 10 task_ids for bulk estimation.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Single task to estimate (use this OR task_ids)

params.name: task_ids
params.description: Multiple tasks to estimate at once (max 10)

tools.name: expect_outcome
tools.description: Record a post-condition on work you just did: a fact about the world that should become TRUE by a deadline if the action actually worked. Kavanah re-checks it against the database later and marks it met or missed — you are not asked, and your own summary does not count as evidence. Use this whenever you take an action whose success is not immediately observable: you assigned a task and it should reach a status; you asked someone for something and they should deliver; you made a change that should move a goal. Do NOT use it for work that is already verifiably done at the moment you finish (you created a document and it exists) — there is nothing to wait for. One check per claim; keep the description specific enough that a human reading it later can tell whether it was a fair test.

params.name: description
params.description: Plain-language statement of what should become true, e.g. 'Task 412 (migrate billing webhook) reaches review after Marcus picks it up'. Shown to admins in the oversight ledger and in any escalation. Max 500 chars.

params.name: check_source
params.description: How Kavanah will observe it. task_status: a task reaches one of an expected set of statuses. task_completed: a task is finished. followup_resolved: a waiting-on ledger entry (see track_waiting_on) gets resolved. goal_on_track: a goal's measured value is on track.

params.name: check_config
params.description: Parameters for the check. task_status: { task_id: number, expected_status: string[] }. task_completed: { task_id: number }. followup_resolved: { followup_id: uuid }. goal_on_track: { goal_id: uuid }.

params.name: due_in_hours
params.description: How long the world has to catch up, in hours. Minimum 0.084 (5 minutes), maximum 2160 (90 days). Pick a horizon that is fair: a task you just assigned to a busy person does not become a failure in an hour.

params.name: tool_name
params.description: Optional. The tool you called that this is the post-condition for, e.g. 'update_task'.

tools.name: explain_user_permissions
tools.description: Explain WHY a member has the access they have: their effective capabilities and the source of each (owner status, legacy role, assigned roles, time-bound grants, project overrides). Answers questions like 'why can Sarah access X?'. Admin only.

params.name: user_id
params.description: Member user id (UUID) to explain.

tools.name: export_report
tools.description: Run a report definition ad-hoc and render it as a downloadable document string in csv, markdown, or html. Nothing is persisted. Output is capped in length — the summary says if it was truncated. For raw rows instead of a formatted document, use generate_report_now.

params.name: report_type
params.description: The report type to run (see generate_report_now).

params.name: format
params.description: Output format. Defaults to csv.

params.name: config
params.description: Report parameters, same shape as generate_report_now's config.

tools.name: find_bd_partner_matches
tools.description: Which PARTNERED broker-dealers (agreed / active) offer what another partner's mandate asks for — one firm's supply_offered against the other's sectors, stages, geographies and mandate notes. Directional (A's supply for B's demand is a different introduction from B's for A's) and explained: each pairing carries its reasons, and near-misses carry why they were rejected. Pass firm_id to see one partner's pairings. Computes live; nothing is saved or sent.

tools.name: find_broker_dealer_matches
tools.description: Which partnered broker-dealers fit a deal, and WHY — scored on sector, issuance stage, geography and whether the raise fits their cheque range. Also returns the near-misses with the reason each was rejected, so 'why didn't you suggest X' has an answer. Requires the deal to carry a sector: without one, fit cannot be judged and nothing is surfaced rather than everything.

tools.name: find_course_lessons
tools.description: Search the course catalogue for lessons relevant to a topic. Scores each lesson against the query using title, subtitle, learning objectives, and section headings, and returns the top matches with their slugs, their course, and why they matched. Use whenever a user asks a how-to, setup, or methodology question the courses cover — 'how do I connect Gmail?', 'what can the AI agent actually do?', 'how do I set up approvals?', 'what's the right way to estimate?'. Then call get_course_lesson on the top hit if the user wants the full answer.

params.name: query
params.description: What the user is asking about. Free text — 'connecting Google Calendar', 'agent safe mode', 'custom task statuses', 'metrics to track for burnout'.

params.name: course
params.description: Optional course slug to restrict the search to. Omit to search everything.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max matches to return (1–10). Defaults to 3.

tools.name: find_duplicate_tasks
tools.description: Find existing tasks in this workspace that are near-duplicates of a given title/description (trigram or token-overlap similarity). Call this BEFORE creating a task to avoid filing a duplicate, or to identify merge candidates. Read-only.

params.name: title
params.description: The task title to check for duplicates.

params.name: description
params.description: Optional description to improve the match.

params.name: exclude_task_id
params.description: Optional task id to exclude from results (e.g. when checking an existing task against others).

params.name: limit
params.description: Max candidates to return. Default 8, capped at 25.

tools.name: find_ui_feature
tools.description: Find where a feature, button, page, or setting lives in the Kavanah UI. Searches the product map by name, keywords, location, and description, and returns the best-matching surfaces with their sidebar location and route. Use this whenever the user asks 'where is …?', 'how do I get to …?', 'which page has …?', or 'is there a … in Kavanah?'. Then call get_feature_guide for step-by-step instructions on the top hit if the user wants to actually do the thing.

params.name: query
params.description: What the user is looking for, in free text — e.g. 'connect Gmail', 'time tracking', 'where do I change my plan', 'kanban board', 'invite a teammate', 'keyboard shortcuts'.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max matches to return (1–15). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: forget_memory
tools.description: Delete a saved memory by id (from recall_memories) when it is wrong or obsolete. If a fact CHANGED, forget the old memory and `remember` the new version.

tools.name: forward_chat_message
tools.description: Forward an existing message from one of the caller's direct threads into another of their direct threads. This DELIVERS a real message to the target contact — only forward on the user's behalf when they've asked you to. Forwarding into group/channel threads is not supported.

params.name: source_thread_id
params.description: Id of the thread the message is currently in (from list_chat_threads).

params.name: message_id
params.description: Id of the message to forward (from list_chat_messages).

params.name: target_thread_id
params.description: Id of the direct thread to forward the message into (from list_chat_threads).

tools.name: generate_ai_persona_avatar
tools.description: Generate a profile picture for an existing AI Employee with AI, and save it to their profile. Workspace owners and admins only. COSTS CREDITS per image — tell the user and get agreement before calling, and don't retry on a whim. There is a 10-second cooldown between generations. Create the employee first, then call this with their id. Describe the person you want to see (appearance, style, mood); the studio-headshot framing is added automatically. The image is written straight to the employee's profile — you never see the bytes, so confirm the result by telling the user to look at the roster.

params.name: persona_id
params.description: UUID of the employee to generate a picture for.

params.name: persona_name
params.description: Exact name of the employee, if you don't have the id.

params.name: visual_description
params.description: What the picture should show — appearance, age, styling, mood, background. If omitted, the employee's stored avatar_prompt, role, and personality are used instead.

tools.name: generate_forecast_charts
tools.description: Render 8 executive revenue-forecast charts as email-ready PNG images and return their URLs plus paste-ready HTML. Use this for any forecast/pipeline report that goes out by EMAIL — chart widgets do not render in email. Charts: 1 30-day best/base/worst scenarios, 2 pipeline by stage, 3 probability by close date (50% threshold), 4 contribution waterfall (top 12 deals), 5 probability decay by deal age, 6 top revenue risks, 7 deal health matrix (LOCK NOW / CONFIRM / RED FLAG / NOISE), 8 weekly runway by stage. Each carries a computed one-line insight. Omit `deals` to read open deals straight from the Deal Room (one call, exact numbers — prefer this over copying numbers out of get_deal). In Deal Room mode the returned HTML also opens with a DEAL FACTS table built from the timeline — stage, fee, close date, last inbound / outbound, and every activity row in the last facts_since_hours (default 12), or "no change recorded" — so the email's per-deal lines are records, not prose. Then send the returned HTML with email_my_digest (is_html: true). Free; no credits.

params.name: deals
params.description: Optional. Deals to chart when they don't live in the Deal Room. Omit to use the Deal Room. Max 500.

params.name: scenario
params.description: Which scenario charts 3, 4, 7 and 8 show. Chart 1 always shows all three. Default base.

params.name: pipeline
params.description: Deal Room pipeline id or slug (Deal Room mode only). Default: the default pipeline.

params.name: deal_room_value
params.description: Deal Room mode: chart the deal amount (default — the raise / deal size) or the revenue/fee field. A placement or advisory desk earns the FEE, so a revenue forecast for one must pass "revenue"; charting the raise overstates it by the fee ratio.

params.name: committed_stages
params.description: Stage names whose deals are SIGNED AND COLLECTIBLE (e.g. ["Collecting","Signed"]). Given, the scenarios follow the committed rules: worst = those deals only, at 100% on their close date, everything else $0; base = worst + every other deal at its recorded probability; best = base + the fresh-contact uplift. Omit for the momentum rules (worst = probability decayed by silence, close dates slip 14 days).

params.name: stage_order
params.description: Stage names from MOST advanced to least (e.g. ["Collecting","Verbal","Diligence","Interest"]). Drives colour (green→red) and the 'advance one stage' maths. Deal Room mode uses the pipeline's board order.

params.name: as_of
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD the forecast is measured from. Default: today in the user's timezone.

params.name: facts_since_hours
params.description: Deal Room mode: how far back the deal-facts table looks for timeline activity, 1–336 hours. Default 12 (an evening report covers the morning one; pass 24 for a daily report).

params.name: deal_facts
params.description: Deal Room mode: false leaves the deal-facts table out. Default true.

params.name: horizon_days
params.description: Forecast window, 7–90. Default 30.

params.name: insights
params.description: Optional one-line overrides keyed by chart: revenue-scenarios, pipeline-by-stage, probability-timeline, revenue-contribution, probability-decay, revenue-at-risk, deal-health-matrix, revenue-runway. Omitted charts use the computed insight. Only override with numbers you verified.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generate a picture from a text description with AI, and show it in this conversation. Use for illustrations, concept art, mockup imagery, logos, headers, or any 'draw me / make me a picture of' request. COSTS CREDITS per image — say so and get the user's agreement before the first call, and do not silently retry for a better result. There is a 10-second cooldown between images. NOT for charts or diagrams: to plot data use a chart widget, and for a flow/box diagram write the SVG yourself — both are free and sharper than a generated raster. You never see the image itself. This returns a URL plus the exact widget tag to emit; copy that tag into your reply verbatim and the picture renders inline for the user.

params.name: prompt
params.description: What to draw. Be specific about subject, style, composition, colour, and mood — a richer description is a better image. Do not include text/words in the image; models render them badly.

params.name: aspect
params.description: Frame shape. Default square. Landscape suits headers/banners, portrait suits characters.

params.name: quality
params.description: Default low, which is quick and cheap and fine for drafts. Only use medium/high when the user asks for something polished — it costs several times more.

tools.name: generate_project_kvn
tools.description: AI-draft a single axis of a PROJECT's KVN charter, grounded in the company charter and this project's own other axes. Returns the draft WITHOUT saving — call set_project_kvn to persist. Reach for this whenever a project has no charter and work is being created under it: the project Negation is the one the enforcement gate actually reads, so a project without one is a project where nothing is checked. Draft all three axes (three calls), show them to the user, and save them once they agree — do not save a Negation the user has not seen, because every task created in that project is checked against it.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project to draft a charter axis for.

params.name: axis
params.description: Which axis to draft.

params.name: prompt
params.description: Optional operator note to steer the draft.

tools.name: generate_report_now
tools.description: Run a report definition ad-hoc and return its rows (NOT a saved report — nothing is persisted). Use this to compute a report on demand. Supported report_type values include status, burndown, burnup, cycle-time, lead-time, velocity, completion-rate, overdue, new-vs-resolved, time-tracking, billing, cross-project, client-health, discussion-activity, storage-usage, workspace-usage, weekly-status, bottlenecks, scope-creep, deadline-forecast, standup-summary, sprint-comparison, idle-tasks, executive-summary, client-health-analysis, anomalies, my_work, progress-weekly/monthly/yearly, github-contributor, comparison. Row output is capped — the summary says how many rows were truncated.

params.name: report_type
params.description: The report type to run (see the list above).

params.name: config
params.description: Report parameters, matching the report type. Common keys: projectRef, startDate, endDate, days, groupBy ('project'|'person'|'task'), sprintWeeks, sinceDays, idleDaysThreshold, sprintIds, metric, p1Start/p1End/p2Start/p2End (comparison), horizonDays (my_work). Omit for reports that take no params.

tools.name: generate_task_kvn
tools.description: AI-draft one axis of a task's KVN block, using the company charter and the task itself for grounding. Returns the draft text WITHOUT saving — call set_task_kvn to persist. Use to fill in missing axes when delegating.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Task to draft for.

params.name: axis
params.description: Which axis to draft.

params.name: prompt
params.description: Optional operator note to steer the draft.

tools.name: generate_weekly_checkin
tools.description: Generate (or fetch the existing) DRAFT weekly check-in for a member and a week. Defaults to the calling user and the last 7 days. Insert-or-do-nothing: if a check-in already exists for that member+week it is returned untouched (edits are never clobbered). Creates a draft only — it does not send email.

params.name: member_user_id
params.description: User id to generate for. Defaults to the calling user.

params.name: week_start
params.description: Start of the week to summarize; defaults to 7 days ago (format: YYYY-MM-DD).

params.name: week_end
params.description: End of the week to summarize; defaults to today (format: YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: generate_workspace_kvn
tools.description: AI-draft a single axis of the company's KVN charter, using the other two axes and workspace context (projects, clients) for grounding. Returns the draft text WITHOUT saving — call set_workspace_kvn to persist. Use when the user says 'help me write our vision', 'draft a negation', etc.

params.name: axis
params.description: Which axis to draft.

params.name: prompt
params.description: Optional operator note to steer the draft (e.g. 'focus on enterprise SaaS').

tools.name: get_active_sprint
tools.description: Return the currently active sprint for a project (status='active'), or null if none.

tools.name: get_agent_activity_report
tools.description: Summarize the agent's own activity over the last N days (admin-only): actions executed / parked for approval / blocked by policy / failed, undone-by-human count, approval outcomes, per-category and top-tool breakdowns. Use when the user asks what the agent has been doing, or to ground a self-report.

params.name: days
params.description: Window in days. Default 7, max 90.

tools.name: get_agent_conversation
tools.description: Read the transcript of ONE of the current user's past AI-agent conversations by id (from list/search_agent_conversations). Returns the displayed user/assistant turns, most recent last. Read-only, self-scoped.

params.name: conversation_id
params.description: Id of the conversation to read.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max messages to return (1..200, default 50 most recent).

tools.name: get_ai_persona
tools.description: Fetch one AI persona's full configuration by id or name (instructions, allowed_scopes, model, disclosure_policy).

params.name: persona_id
params.description: UUID of the persona.

params.name: persona_name
params.description: Exact persona name.

tools.name: get_ai_usage_breakdown
tools.description: Where this workspace's AI usage goes ('why is my AI usage so high', 'cut token costs'): unattended usage by kind, per-schedule runs/tokens/model, chat usage by model, est. USD, current cost settings, ranked recommendations. Admins: workspace; members: their own. Propose changes; apply only when the user agrees.

params.name: days
params.description: How many days back to look (1–90). Defaults to 7.

tools.name: get_angelsend_audience_sync
tools.description: The scheduled AngelSend audience sync for this workspace: which directions are on (opt-outs in hourly; contacts pull and push daily), whose AngelSend key runs it, and each direction's last run and result. All directions are off unless an admin turned them on.

tools.name: get_angelsend_campaign_mirror
tools.description: Whether a cadence (the network campaign, or a deal / investor-funnel cadence — per deal) is backed by a native AngelSend campaign: on/off, status, the AngelSend campaign id, channel and daily limit, AngelSend's own sender capacity, the archive copy as last VERIFIED on AngelSend, AngelSend's sent/open/click/reply counts, and the last problem (e.g. why it was refused). Off unless an admin turned it on.

params.name: deal_id
params.description: For a deal cadence: which deal's campaign. Omit to list every mirror of the cadence.

tools.name: get_anomalies
tools.description: Detect anomalies and flag issues (US-60). Finds stale tasks (open > 30 days), severely overdue items (> 14 days past due), unassigned high-priority tasks, effort overruns (actual > 2x estimate), and SLA breaches.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project reference to filter by.

tools.name: get_app_manifest
tools.description: Read the full manifest of one app this workspace owns, plus its version history (semver, review state, which is current), whether it is installed here, and any non-fatal lint warnings (over-requested scopes, a placeholder endpoint that will fail every call, a screen that can never render). Use it to answer questions about what an app declares, to find a version to roll back to, or to fetch the current manifest before proposing an edited version.

params.name: slug
params.description: The app's slug, e.g. 'acme-crm'.

tools.name: get_assignment_decision_metrics
tools.description: Summarise the assignment ledger: total decisions, override count and RATE (healthy 20–40%), how many overrides have a recorded reason, the breakdown by reason category, and who is most often the recommended-but-skipped pick. Read-only, pure aggregation. Empty unless assignment-decision logging is enabled.

params.name: days
params.description: Window in days (default 90).

tools.name: get_blueprint
tools.description: Show a Blueprint: items by group with cost, blockers, compliance notes, what is applied, and the diff vs what is applied. Omit blueprint_id for the latest.

tools.name: get_boardroom
tools.description: Get one exec boardroom in full: its seats (which persona holds which chair, and each seat's remit), the chair, the standing agenda, the cadence, and when it last met. Use before changing a boardroom, so you describe accurately what is there now.

params.name: boardroom
params.description: The boardroom's id, or its exact name.

tools.name: get_bottlenecks
tools.description: Identify bottlenecks by finding which status columns have the most stuck tasks (US-50). Shows task count per status, average days in status, and the oldest stuck task.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project reference to filter by.

tools.name: get_broker_dealer_scan_coverage
tools.description: How much of the open pipeline the hourly broker-dealer scan can actually judge: open deals, how many were scanned in the last day, how many were SKIPPED because no sector could be found (the deal's own field, its data-room profile, its category and its name were all tried), which ones, and how many were matched on an inferred sector. Use it when someone asks why a deal produced no broker-dealer matches.

tools.name: get_budget_burn
tools.description: Per-project budget burn-down and end-of-project spend forecast: total budget, spent-to-date, and a P10/P50/P90 forecast of final spend with a confidence grade derived from logged budget entries. Read-only.

tools.name: get_burndown_data
tools.description: Get burndown chart data for a project showing remaining tasks over time (US-56). Use to generate a burndown narrative, not just chart data — explain trends, inflection points, and what happened.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: The project reference.

params.name: start_date
params.description: Start date for the burndown (ISO format, e.g. 2025-01-01).

params.name: end_date
params.description: End date for the burndown (ISO format, e.g. 2025-01-31).

tools.name: get_burnup_data
tools.description: Get burnup chart data for a project showing total scope and completed tasks over time. Useful alongside burndown for a complete narrative.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: The project reference.

params.name: start_date
params.description: Start date (ISO format).

params.name: end_date
params.description: End date (ISO format).

tools.name: get_cadence_variant_stats
tools.description: A/B/C/D results for one cadence: sends, replies and reply RATE per arm, with the subject line and the sender display name each arm ACTUALLY went out under (and how many sends the provider could not put the requested name on — Outlook and the AngelSend send-email gateway cannot). Compare rates, never raw reply counts — arms rarely receive equal volume, and comparing counts across unequal denominators is how a losing subject gets declared the winner. Treat small samples as inconclusive rather than reporting a leader. Also reports the cadence's experiment: its design (linked = subject and sender confounded; factorial = independent), per-factor results per contact (replies, positive replies, meetings — opens are not tracked) with each level's probability to be best, the automatic winner policy and its verdict, and recent winner decisions.

params.name: cadence
params.description: Cadence id or exact name.

tools.name: get_client_health_analysis
tools.description: Analyze client health with recommended actions (US-59). Shows health score (0-100), status, overdue tasks, and top issues for each client.

tools.name: get_client_links
tools.description: List the reference links on a client (dataroom, Drive folder, contract, etc). Read this before calling set_client_links, which replaces the whole list.

tools.name: get_client_sheet_link
tools.description: Show how the workspace's client list (Accounts) is connected to a Google Sheet: which spreadsheet and tab it imports from, how many columns are mapped, whether the outbound mirror is on, when it last pulled in / mirrored out, and the last error. Read-only.

tools.name: get_company_profile
tools.description: Read this workspace's structured company profile: legal name, address, phone, website, support email, tax id / EIN, industry, plus freeform key facts. Check here FIRST when the user asks for a basic org fact (address, zip code, EIN, phone) — before searching documents or email.

tools.name: get_completion_rates_by_member
tools.description: Get task completion rates per team member (US-48). Shows total assigned, completed count, completion rate percentage, and average days to complete for each assignee.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project reference to filter by.

params.name: days
params.description: Number of days to look back. Defaults to 30.

tools.name: get_compliance_archiving_status
tools.description: Compliance (broker-dealer) archiving status for this workspace. ANY member may ask: they get whether it is ON, the retention period, what is and is not archived, and who can change it. Owners and admins also get the archive/journaling address, how many communications are journaled or waiting for delivery, the last delivery and any delivery error. Use whenever someone asks about their archiving setup or status, whether their communications are archived or monitored, SEC 17a-4 / FINRA 4511 recordkeeping, or how to turn archiving on. Settings: Settings → Audit Logs → Archiving (/settings/audit-logs?tab=archiving).

tools.name: get_compliance_summary
tools.description: Generate a high-level compliance report for the workspace: counts of recent audit events by category, severity, and success/failure (admin-only).

tools.name: get_contact_research
tools.description: Show the VERIFIED research facts held for a contact and their firm — recent posts or articles, deals the firm funded, background, news — each with its source URL, the verbatim quote that supports it, the source date, when it was retrieved and verified, and when it expires. Also shows recent research runs and why candidates were discarded. Free. Use this to answer 'what do we know about X', to check what a personalized opener may cite, or to show a compliance reviewer where a sentence came from. Facts that failed the fact-check are never stored, so an empty list means nothing passed, not that nobody looked.

params.name: contact_id
params.description: Deal Room / network contact id.

params.name: contact_email
params.description: The contact's email, when you do not have the id.

params.name: include_expired
params.description: Also list expired and retracted facts (for review). Default false: only facts an opener may use.

tools.name: get_contact_runway
tools.description: How many days each LIVE network cadence can keep reaching NEW people before it runs out of contacts: sendable contacts never enrolled in it (has an email, not archived, not suppressed) plus those enrolled but not yet emailed, divided by its measured pace of first emails over the last week (capped by today's send capacity). Also returns the warning threshold and when admins were last warned. Admins are warned automatically — in-app and by email, at most every 3 days — when a cadence drops below the threshold (default 7 days). A cadence that sent no first email in the last week has no runway clock and is reported as not consuming contacts. Use this before promising a campaign can run for N weeks, and whenever the user asks how long their list will last.

tools.name: get_contact_warmth
tools.description: The computed warmth score (0-100) for a contact, with the component breakdown that produced it and a plain-English explanation. Seven inputs: responsiveness (reply RATE), recency of their last action, meetings granted, document read-depth, deal progression, connectedness (how many of our people they have actually answered, and how many relationships we hold at their firm), and background similarity (a shared school, employer or city with someone on our team). It deliberately ignores how much we emailed them, so it cannot be raised by sending more — and connectedness counts colleagues who were REPLIED TO, not colleagues who sent something. This is distinct from the human 'relationship_status' label, which is someone's judgement; both are shown and they can disagree.

tools.name: get_course_lesson
tools.description: Read a single lesson in full — title, subtitle, learning objectives, prose sections, the 'Kavanah in practice' steps, the lesson's metrics block, key takeaways, and any citations. Use after find_course_lessons or list_course_lessons identifies the right lesson, when the user asks how a Kavanah feature works or how to set it up, or when a metric needs its canonical definition (the metrics block is the source of truth). Lesson slugs are unique across the whole catalogue, so `course` is optional — pass it only to disambiguate intent.

params.name: slug
params.description: Lesson slug (e.g. 'kvn-methodology', 'task-anatomy', 'agent-autonomy-and-safe-mode'). Get from list_course_lessons or find_course_lessons.

params.name: course
params.description: Optional course slug. Omit to search the whole catalogue.

tools.name: get_critical_path
tools.description: Compute the critical path (CPM) across the workspace's task dependency graph: per-task earliest/latest start/finish, slack, and which tasks are critical (zero slack), plus the total project duration in days. Returns nothing when there are no task dependencies, and reports a cycle when the graph can't be ordered. Read-only.

tools.name: get_cross_project_report
tools.description: Get task counts across multiple projects for comparison.

params.name: project_refs
params.description: Optional list of project references to include.

tools.name: get_day_plan
tools.description: Read the caller's own AI day plan: their current energy level, suggested tasks ranked by energy-fit, recommended deep-work blocks, and auto-placed calendar slots. Task fit is scored against the CURRENT user's energy and recent time entries. To actually start a timer on a planned task, use start_timer.

tools.name: get_deadline_forecast
tools.description: Get a data-driven deadline forecast for projects (US-52). Shows remaining tasks, velocity, estimated weeks remaining, and whether the deadline will be met with confidence level.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project reference to filter by.

tools.name: get_deal
tools.description: Fetch one deal by deal_id (the id list_deals prints) with its stage, amount, revenue, probability, owner, expected close, notes, its team (the lead and the members on our side, with each member's title on the deal), contact list, and its 20 most recent activity events.

tools.name: get_deal_data_room_insights
tools.description: The stored data-room reading for a deal: when it was read, which files were read or skipped and why, the sourced insight library (each insight with its file and quoted passage), how many proposed insights were dropped as unsupported, and whether the analyzer wrote the deal's investment profile. Free; reads nothing from Drive. Run analyze_deal_data_room to (re)read the room.

tools.name: get_deal_forecast
tools.description: The Deal Room revenue forecast, calculated live from the deal records: expected FEE revenue by closing week (weeks 1–4, plus overdue / later / no close date), stage distribution, confidence levels, the top 5 revenue risks each with a recommended action, and the upside if deals advance a stage. Probability = the stage's baseline probability × momentum ÷ 50, where momentum (50 = neutral) comes from counterparty emails, calls, meetings and document views on the deal's timeline, time in stage, and a passed close date. Revenue is each deal's recorded fee, or deal size × the workspace's assumed fee % when none is recorded. Deals on a forecast hold, with only internal contacts, or in a stage with no baseline are excluded and listed. Quote its figures under the labels it uses, carry any disclaimer it prints, and if it reports fee bands separately never add the bands together.

params.name: pipeline
params.description: Pipeline id or slug. Omit for every pipeline.

params.name: include_deals
params.description: Also list every open deal's forecast line (probability, momentum, fee, expected fee, close week).

tools.name: get_deal_forecast_settings
tools.description: Read how the revenue forecast is configured: the assumed fee % for deals with no recorded fee, fee bands and their labels, the disclaimer, whether automatic daily recalculation is on (and when it last ran), and the WEEKLY FORECAST EMAIL — on or off, day, time, timezone, every recipient, subject, next send and what the last delivery did. Any member can read it. Call it before changing any of these with configure_deal_forecast, and whenever someone asks when or to whom the forecast goes out.

tools.name: get_deal_investment_profile
tools.description: The stored data-room reading for a deal: themes, sectors, stages, geographies, minimum position, summary, and which files it came from. Use it to check whether a deal is rankable before calling rank_investors_for_deal, and to see whether the profile predates a change to the data room.

tools.name: get_deal_sheet_link
tools.description: Show how a pipeline is connected to a Google Sheet: which spreadsheet and tab it imports from, how many columns are mapped, whether the outbound mirror is on (and to which tab), when it last pulled in / mirrored out, and the last error. Read-only — use before sync_deal_sheet to confirm a link exists.

params.name: pipeline
params.description: Pipeline id or slug. Defaults to the workspace default pipeline.

tools.name: get_deal_space
tools.description: Where a deal's data room is, and what is in it: the deal's Slack channel and Google Drive folder (id and link), plus a listing of the folder's files and its sub-folders' files read through YOUR Google Drive connection. This is step one of an investor campaign — read the documents it lists with drive_read_file, then record what they say with set_deal_investment_profile. If no folder is recorded, it says so; link one that was made outside Kavanah with link_deal_drive_folder.

tools.name: get_dependency_graph
tools.description: Whole-graph dependency HEALTH CHECK: builds the task dependency DAG, runs cycle detection, and flags orphan edges (referencing deleted tasks) and deadline conflicts (a predecessor due after its successor). This is the CYCLE-DETECTING graph-wide view — distinct from list_task_dependencies, which just lists one task's direct predecessors/successors. Read-only.

tools.name: get_document_publish_status
tools.description: Read the current publication record (active state, token, display options).

tools.name: get_document_tree
tools.description: Read the knowledge library's page hierarchy (parent → child nesting) for the workspace, rendered as an indented outline with each page's id and title. Use this before moving a page so you know the current structure and the ids to pass to set_document_parent. Templates are excluded (they are never tree nodes).

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional. Stringified project id (same form as app_tasks.project_ref) to scope the tree to one project's pages plus workspace-shared pages. Omit to include every page in the workspace.

tools.name: get_energy_level
tools.description: Read the caller's own current energy level ('deep', 'steady', or 'shallow'). This is the current user's personal setting only.

tools.name: get_enrichment_supply
tools.description: Whether a campaign can actually be sustained, from BOTH ends: how much send capacity remains today per mailbox (the provider caps this, not us — Gmail refuses at roughly 2,000/day for a Workspace account and 500 for a consumer one), and how many contacts still have no email address. Use it before launching or scaling a sequence. Two caveats it returns and you must repeat: only some enrichment providers report a real balance, so 'unknown' is never 'fine'; and the send count covers queued mail only, so it is a floor on today's volume rather than a full account of what the provider has seen.

tools.name: get_entity_properties
tools.description: Resolved custom-property values for one entity. Returns literal values plus computed values (formula + rollup) evaluated at read time. Use for 'what's this task's story points?' / 'what's the rollup total?' style questions.

params.name: entity_id
params.description: Task id (numeric string), project ref, or client id depending on entity_type.

tools.name: get_estimate_calibration
tools.description: Estimate-vs-actual accuracy over the last 90 days of completed tasks (with both an estimate and logged actual hours). Per assignee: mean actual/estimate ratio (>1 = under-estimating, <1 = over-estimating), sample count, and a recent-vs-older trend, plus a team-wide ratio. Read-only.

tools.name: get_exec_meeting
tools.description: Read the full minutes of one exec meeting: every exec's performance update, the discussion round by round, and the chair's close with its action items. Use when the user wants to know what was actually SAID, not just the summary.

params.name: meeting_id
params.description: The meeting's id.

tools.name: get_executive_summary
tools.description: Generate an executive summary across all projects (US-58). Shows completion %, overdue count, health status, velocity, and budget variance for each project.

tools.name: get_feature_guide
tools.description: Get full detail for one Kavanah surface: exactly where it is (sidebar path + route), the key buttons/actions on the page, a step-by-step how-to for the common task, and related surfaces. Use after find_ui_feature identifies the right feature, or directly when you already know the feature id/name (e.g. 'projects-tasks', 'Integrations', 'KVN'). This is the canonical source for walking a user through a task — quote its steps rather than improvising UI directions.

params.name: feature
params.description: Feature id, exact label, or route. Examples: 'settings-integrations', 'Projects & Tasks', '/calendar', 'automations'. Get ids from find_ui_feature or list_app_navigation.

tools.name: get_feature_request
tools.description: Read one feature request by its numeric id, including its status, category, upvote count, and any admin response.

params.name: id
params.description: The feature request id.

tools.name: get_firm
tools.description: One firm in full, including every contact we have there with their warmth score. This is the answer to 'who do we know at this firm and how well'.

tools.name: get_firm_coverage
tools.description: How much of the workspace lives in the institution layer: total contacts, how many are attached to a firm, how many still carry an employer name with no firm, and how many firms exist. Use it to decide whether reconcile_contacts_into_firms is worth running, and to answer 'is our investor matrix actually populated'.

tools.name: get_focus_mode
tools.description: Read the caller's own Focus Mode snapshot: whether a focus session is active (and when it ends), plus the caller's batched drafts awaiting review and the workspace's async-meeting candidates. This is the current user's personal focus state — never another member's.

tools.name: get_github_connect_status
tools.description: Check whether GitHub is linked to this workspace: GitHub App installations (which org/user, how many repos visible), whether the calling user has connected a personal GitHub account, how many repos are connected to the /dev page, and — when something is missing — the exact connect links to share with the user (App install and personal OAuth). Call this whenever the user wants GitHub data but /dev has no repos, or asks how to connect GitHub. Read-only.

tools.name: get_god_mode_setup_status
tools.description: Read the God Mode setup checklist (what's left to set up) — the live status of everything the deal machine needs: each person's Google accounts (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides; a revoked grant reads as 'reconnect'), sending capacity, the sending domain's SPF/DKIM/DMARC with the exact records to add, compliance mode + archive address, the email finder (Apollo/Hunter/ppl.contact), XDocs + the engagement envelope rule, AngelSend + audience sync, Slack permissions, Stripe, the remote browser, linked spreadsheets, the Drive folder for client spaces, cadence booking links, the deal automation chain, the North Star, AI employees, reply supervision (FINRA 3110) and the agent switches with their credit cost. Returns the open items, each with a status, a plain-language reason and the link that fixes it. Owners/admins get the whole workspace; a member gets only their own connections. Read-only.

tools.name: get_grooming_proposals
tools.description: Generate backlog-grooming proposals (read-only — this only PROPOSES, it does not apply anything): close stale open tasks (>90 days), deprioritize long-blocked tasks (>30 days), retag untagged tasks, split chronically underestimated tasks (actual ≥1.5× estimate), and merge likely-duplicate clusters by title. Read-only.

tools.name: get_idle_tasks
tools.description: Find tasks that have been idle (not completed) for too long (US-57). Shows task details and how many days each has been idle.

params.name: idle_days_threshold
params.description: Minimum days idle to include. Defaults to 7.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project reference to filter by.

tools.name: get_investor_match_calibration
tools.description: How well the investor-match ranking predicted outcomes: reply and meeting rate by score band, and by scoring component (thesis, sector, stage, geography, capacity, warmth) with and without it, over approaches at least 14 days old. Shows the weights in use and, when the data supports it, a BOUNDED proposed weight change (each weight within 0.5x–1.5x of its default, at most ±5 points per application, total 100). Nothing changes until apply_investor_match_weights is run.

params.name: deal_id
params.description: Limit to one deal (optional).

params.name: metric
params.description: Outcome the proposal optimizes (default reply).

tools.name: get_knowledge_document
tools.description: Fetch a single knowledge document by id. Returns title, tags, icon, template state, and either the structured block list (preferred — each block has a stable id usable in add_document_block_comment) or the legacy markdown body when blocks haven't been written.

tools.name: get_knowledge_index_stats
tools.description: Report how much of this workspace is indexed for knowledge retrieval: total chunks and a per-surface breakdown (Tasks, Discussions, Replies, Docs, Decisions, Retros, Onboarding, Glossary, Memories) plus when it was last refreshed. Read-only — use it to gauge whether ask_knowledge_base has enough to draw on.

tools.name: get_manager_agreement
tools.description: Read the caller's own Manager Mode agreement: whether Kavanah is acting as their manager, their management style, stated objectives, working capacity (days per week, focused hours per day), deadline confidence level, check-in cadence, and reward settings. Returns a disabled default if they have never set one up — call this before any other manager tool so you know whether the feature is on. Personal data only.

tools.name: get_manager_briefing
tools.description: The caller's current standing with their manager in one call: open commitments with their deadlines, anything overdue, the oldest unanswered check-in, and headline scorecard numbers (points, streak, on-time rate). Use this to open a management conversation, answer 'what should I be doing?', or ground a nudge. Personal data only.

tools.name: get_manager_scorecard
tools.description: The caller's own reward standing: points balance, lifetime earned, level, current on-time streak and its multiplier, points earned against this week's ceiling, commitment counts and on-time rate, plus how many credits (if any) their points could currently be redeemed for. Personal data only.

tools.name: get_meeting_twin_session
tools.description: One twin / notetaker meeting: live status, the summary and action items once it has ended, and the transcript (who said what, including exactly what the twin said).

params.name: include_transcript
params.description: Default false — the transcript can be long.

tools.name: get_member_profile
tools.description: Read one member's full experience profile: LinkedIn URL, experience summary, and the extracted resume text (truncated when very long). Use when deciding whether a specific person fits a task, or when the user asks about someone's background.

params.name: member_name
params.description: Member display name, as used in app_tasks.assigned_to / list_members.

tools.name: get_my_note
tools.description: Read the full title and body of one of the caller's own notes by id. Personal data only.

params.name: id
params.description: Id of the note to read (from list_my_notes).

tools.name: get_my_notepad
tools.description: Read the caller's own default notepad (their most-recently-updated note). The Notepad now holds MANY titled notes — use list_my_notes / get_my_note to work with a specific one. This is the current user's personal data — never another member's.

tools.name: get_my_profile
tools.description: Read the calling user's own profile: name, email, job title, department, timezone, website, calendar booking link, bio, and their contact details (phone, address, city). Their job title, booking link, and bio are ALREADY in your system prompt — only call this when you specifically need the contact details, which are not. This is the caller's own record and never anyone else's; for a teammate's job title or booking link use list_members, and for their skills use get_member_profile.

tools.name: get_network_sheet_status
