tools.description: The Google Sheet(s) linked to the network (firms + contacts): which tab, the column mapping, when it last imported and mirrored, and the last import's summary — rows read, firms/contacts created and updated, fields filled, fields KEPT because someone edited them in Kavanah, and the cells that could not be read (an unparseable AUM, an unknown partner status). Use it before answering 'is the sheet synced' or 'why didn't X come through'.

tools.name: get_new_vs_resolved_trend
tools.description: Get the trend of new tasks created vs tasks resolved per day over a period.

params.name: days
params.description: Number of days to look back. Defaults to 30.

tools.name: get_north_star
tools.description: Read the North Star for the workspace or a project — the one metric that makes the Vision falsifiable. Returns where it stands now, its target and direction, the trend across recent readings, and how much of the open work in scope actually declares a contribution to it. A project without its own metric INHERITS the workspace's, and the answer says so. Use when the user asks what to prioritise, whether work is moving the needle, how progress is measured, or 'are we on track?'.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project to read. Omit for the company-wide North Star.

tools.name: get_operating_metrics
tools.description: Read the workspace's OPERATING metrics — the system-as-a-whole layer from the PM course (lesson 6.4): negation reuse rate (how often per week the charter's Negations are cited), AI Employee contribution (fraction of completed estimated-hours assigned to personas), and time-to-first-real-task (median days from a member joining to their first shipped task). Three further operating metrics — capture latency, project Vision hit rate, and project-to-outcome conversion — are returned marked 'unavailable' with the reason, because the product does not yet capture the data they need. Use for 'how is the workspace doing overall?', a quarterly operating review, or 'are the AI Employees earning their keep?'. Read-only.

params.name: days
params.description: Lookback window in days for the rate and contribution metrics. Default 90; clamped to 7–365. Time-to-first-task is all-time.

tools.name: get_org
tools.description: Read one organization the caller belongs to (by org id), including its workspaces and members. Returns null-equivalent (an error) if the caller isn't an active member of that org.

params.name: org_id
params.description: The organization id.

tools.name: get_overdue_tasks
tools.description: Get a list of all overdue tasks with details including how many days past due.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project reference to filter by.

tools.name: get_pipeline_summary
tools.description: Stage-by-stage money rollup for a pipeline: deal count, total deal amount, total revenue (fees), and probability-weighted versions of both, plus open-pipeline ('capturable') and won totals. Use for questions like 'how much capturable revenue is sitting at interest level?'. This is the source for pipeline reads, forecasts and weighted-value questions — a task board whose columns look like deal stages is not the pipeline.

params.name: pipeline
params.description: Pipeline id or slug. Defaults to the workspace default.

tools.name: get_portfolio_forecasts
tools.description: Get completion forecasts for active projects based on current velocity, plus workload summaries (over-allocation), and budget rollups. Read-only summary.

tools.name: get_productivity_insights
tools.description: Read the caller's own personal productivity insights: their weekly time mirror (hours by project), week-over-week outliers, the team capacity heatmap, and burnout signals private to the caller. The weekly mirror, outliers, and burnout signals are scoped to the current user — never another member's private signals.

tools.name: get_project_cycle_time
tools.description: Per-status cycle-time stats for a project: count, mean, median (p50), and p90 time tasks spent in each column over the last N days. Defaults to 90 days, max 365. Use this to identify bottleneck columns ('review' takes 4× longer than 'in progress', etc.).

params.name: since_days
params.description: Lookback window in days. 1-365, default 90.

tools.name: get_project_kvn
tools.description: Read a project's KVN charter — the K/V/N constitution every task in that project inherits from, plus the project's false-friends list. Call this before recommending an approach for a project task so the recommendation respects the project's negation space.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Stringified project id. Same form used by app_tasks.project_ref.

tools.name: get_project_readme
tools.description: Read a project's 'Living README' — an executive snapshot (what the project is, where it stands, what's in flight, constraints, open risks) with cited sources. Read-only. Pass project_ref to target a specific project; omitted, it uses the workspace's first project. Returns null-ish text if no README has been generated yet (use regenerate_project_readme to build one).

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project ref to read the README for. Omitted = first project in the workspace.

tools.name: get_project_status_report
tools.description: Get a detailed project status report with status breakdown, priority breakdown, completion percentage, and overdue count.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project reference to filter by.

tools.name: get_project_visibility
tools.description: List project visibility restrictions: which roles/teams a project is limited to (an empty list for a project means it is visible to all). Admin only.

tools.name: get_report_insight
tools.description: Run one of the deep-analytics insight getters and return its data. insight_type selects the analysis: 'cohort' (task cohorts by tag), 'forecast' (revenue/throughput forecast), 'quality' (rework/quality metrics), 'time-breakdown' (logged hours grouped by project/person/tag), 'goal-drift' (projects drifting from their goals), 'sprint-history' (recent sprint stats), 'custom-context' (workspace context for custom reports). Read-only; output is capped.

params.name: insight_type
params.description: Which insight to compute.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project to scope to (cohort, quality, sprint-history).

params.name: days
params.description: Look-back window in days (quality defaults 90, time-breakdown defaults 30).

params.name: weeks
params.description: Weeks ahead to forecast (forecast; defaults 4).

params.name: lookback
params.description: Number of sprints to include (sprint-history; defaults 6).

params.name: group_by
params.description: Grouping for time-breakdown. Defaults to 'project'.

tools.name: get_resource_leveling
tools.description: Show this week's per-person workload: allocated vs. capacity hours, utilization, and suggested task reassignments from over-capacity to under-utilized (<70%) teammates. Read-only — suggestions are advisory, nothing is reassigned.

tools.name: get_role
tools.description: Read one RBAC role by id, including its full permission map (resource → view/create/edit/delete). Admin only.

params.name: role_id
params.description: Id (UUID) of the role to read.

tools.name: get_runbook
tools.description: Get one runbook's full step list by id or name. Shows each step's instruction, category, and whether it's a human checkpoint.

params.name: runbook
params.description: Runbook id or exact name.

tools.name: get_saved_view
tools.description: Read one saved view by id, including its filter/sort/group config.

tools.name: get_scope_creep
tools.description: Detect scope creep by showing how many new tasks have been added since a given period (US-51). Shows tasks at start, tasks added, and scope creep percentage.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project reference to filter by.

params.name: since_days
params.description: Number of days to look back for scope changes. Defaults to 14 (sprint length).

tools.name: get_slip_risk
tools.description: Score every open task in this workspace for risk of slipping its deadline (a heuristic blend of schedule pressure, inactivity, blockers, assignee load, priority) and return the highest-risk tasks with the reasons why. Use for 'what's at risk this week' / standup prep. Caches the scores into the task-intelligence sidecar.

params.name: limit
params.description: How many top-risk tasks to return. Default 15, capped at 50.

tools.name: get_sms_alert_status
tools.description: Report whether SMS alerts can currently be delivered: whether the workspace has them switched on, whether a given member has a verified and consented number, and how much of the monthly message budget is spent. Read-only and free. Call this before sms_send_alert, and to answer 'why didn't I get a text?' — it distinguishes not-enrolled from opted-out from over-budget, which the send tool deliberately does not.

params.name: member_email
params.description: Optional — check one member's enrolment. Omit for workspace-level status only.

tools.name: get_sprint_comparison
tools.description: Compare two or more sprints/periods side by side (US-54). Shows total tasks, completed tasks, completion rate, story points, average cycle time, and scope changes for each sprint.

params.name: sprint_ids
params.description: Optional array of sprint IDs to compare. Omit for all sprints.

tools.name: get_sprint_velocity
tools.description: Compute average velocity across the last N completed sprints for a project (default 5).

params.name: sprint_count
params.description: How many recent completed sprints to average (default 5)

tools.name: get_standup_summary
tools.description: Generate a standup summary from yesterday's task activity (US-53). Shows tasks completed yesterday, tasks in progress today, and blocked/overdue items.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project reference to filter by.

tools.name: get_task_access
tools.description: Read whether a task is restricted (visible only to named members + admins) and who its access members are. Read-only.

params.name: task_id
params.description: The task ID

tools.name: get_task_transitions
tools.description: Return the move history for one task — every column it has lived in, who moved it, when, and how long it stayed in the previous status (ms_in_prev_status). Useful for answering 'how did this task get here?' or 'why did it sit in review so long?'.

tools.name: get_team_skills_context
tools.description: Read the workspace-level team context — a standing admin-maintained text block about the team's collective skills, experience, and assignment conventions. Already injected into your system prompt; call only when you need fresh values mid-conversation.

tools.name: get_time_tracking_summary
tools.description: Summarize time tracking data showing where the team's hours went (US-55). Can group by project, person, or task.

params.name: group_by
params.description: How to group the time data. Defaults to 'project'.

params.name: start_date
params.description: Optional start date (ISO format) to filter time entries.

params.name: end_date
params.description: Optional end date (ISO format) to filter time entries.

tools.name: get_trash_item
tools.description: Read one Trash item by its trash id (from list_trash_items), including its type, label, and summary. Read-only.

params.name: trash_id
params.description: The trash item id (from list_trash_items).

tools.name: get_triage_metrics
tools.description: Report the triage queue's health: current queue size, oldest pending item, median time-in-queue, median seconds spent per triaged candidate, and the dismissal-reason distribution over a trailing window. Use for a 'how is our triage doing?' question or a weekly review.

params.name: days
params.description: Trailing window for the reviewed stats (default 30, max 365).

tools.name: get_velocity_trends
tools.description: Get velocity trends showing tasks completed per week over time (US-49). Use to answer whether the team is speeding up or slowing down.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project reference to filter by.

params.name: weeks
params.description: Number of weeks to look back. Defaults to 12.

tools.name: get_viable_scope
tools.description: Rank open tasks as scope-cut candidates by inferred value (priority, milestones, must-keep pins, load-bearing tags like security/billing) and estimate points, plus the team's points-per-day velocity. Use to decide what can be deferred to hit a date. Read-only.

tools.name: get_weekly_checkin
tools.description: Read one weekly check-in by id (full summary markdown + metrics + recipients). Read-only.

params.name: id
params.description: The check-in id (from list_weekly_checkins).

tools.name: get_weekly_status_report
tools.description: Get a weekly status report for one or all projects. Shows task counts by status, tasks completed/created this week, overdue count, and high-priority items. Use for generating weekly status reports (US-46) and client-facing project updates (US-47).

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project reference to filter by. Omit for all projects.

tools.name: get_winning_openers
tools.description: Personalized opening sentences from past cadence sends that earned a reply (meetings first), excluding contacts who later opted out, plus the reply rate of personalized vs generic step sends. Use as examples when writing a personalize_brief or judging whether personalization is paying for itself. Changes nothing.

params.name: limit
params.description: Examples to return (1–20, default 8).

tools.name: get_workspace_kvn
tools.description: Read the company's standing KVN charter (Know-how / Vision / Negation). Use this whenever the user asks about company vision, what the company does/refuses, capabilities, or anti-goals. Already injected at the top of the system prompt — call this only when you need fresh values mid-conversation.

tools.name: gmail_create_draft
tools.description: Write an email and save it as a Gmail draft WITHOUT sending it — use this when the user wants to review or edit before it goes out, or asks you to 'draft'/'write up' an email. Same backends as gmail_send_email (AngelSend Gmail bridge preferred, native Gmail OAuth fallback). The draft appears in the user's Gmail Drafts folder. To send immediately instead, use gmail_send_email; to send it later automatically, use schedule_email.

params.name: to
params.description: Recipient email address(es). Accepts a single address or a comma-separated list.

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line.

params.name: body
params.description: Message body (plain text by default; HTML if `is_html` is true).

params.name: cc
params.description: Optional CC address(es) — single or comma-separated.

params.name: bcc
params.description: Optional BCC address(es) — single or comma-separated.

params.name: reply_to
params.description: Optional Reply-To address (native draft only).

params.name: is_html
params.description: Set to true if `body` contains HTML rather than plain text. Defaults to false.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Optional Gmail thread id to attach the draft to (used to draft a reply in a conversation).

params.name: in_reply_to
params.description: Optional RFC 5322 Message-ID of the message being replied to.

params.name: attachment_ids
params.description: Optional ids of files the user uploaded into this chat, to attach to the draft. Ids come from the uploaded-files list shown in the user's turn. Drafting with attachments uses native Gmail (the AngelSend bridge can't carry files).

tools.name: gmail_get_message
tools.description: Fetch a single Gmail message by id, including the FULL parsed body, sender, recipients, subject, and labels. Use after `gmail_list_messages` to read a message's full content — this is the right tool when you need details that aren't in the list snippet (e.g. a contact's email address inside the message). Works with both the AngelSend bridge and a native Gmail connection. If only a snippet is available the response says so explicitly.

params.name: message_id
params.description: Gmail message id (the `id` field returned by `gmail_list_messages`).

tools.name: gmail_get_thread
tools.description: Fetch a Gmail conversation thread by id, returning every message in the thread with bodies. Use after `gmail_list_threads` to read a conversation. AngelSend-backed only.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Gmail thread id (the `id` field returned by `gmail_list_threads`).

tools.name: gmail_list_labels
tools.description: List all Gmail labels in the user's mailbox — both system labels (INBOX, SENT, IMPORTANT, …) and user-defined labels. Useful for discovering label ids to pass to `gmail_list_messages` / `gmail_list_threads`. AngelSend-backed only.

tools.name: gmail_list_messages
tools.description: List messages in the user's Gmail inbox. Prefers AngelSend's Gmail bridge (returns full headers + snippets); falls back to native Gmail OAuth (ids only). Supports Gmail search syntax (e.g. `from:alice@example.com newer_than:7d`, `is:unread`, `after:2026/05/01`) and pagination via `page_token`. Pass the `next_page_token` returned in the previous call to fetch the next page; stop when no token is returned.

params.name: query
params.description: Optional Gmail search query (same syntax the Gmail web UI accepts).

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max messages to return per page. Default 25, capped at 500.

params.name: page_token
params.description: Pagination cursor — pass the value of `next_page_token` from the previous response to fetch the next page.

params.name: label_ids
params.description: Optional list of Gmail label ids to scope the search (e.g. ['INBOX', 'IMPORTANT']).

params.name: include_body
params.description: Set to false to skip message bodies for faster listing (AngelSend only). Defaults to true.

tools.name: gmail_list_threads
tools.description: List conversation threads in the user's Gmail mailbox. Supports Gmail search syntax (`q`), label filtering, and pagination via `page_token` (same convention as `gmail_list_messages`). AngelSend-backed only.

params.name: query
params.description: Optional Gmail search query.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max threads per page. Default 25, capped at 500.

params.name: page_token
params.description: Pagination cursor from the previous response's `next_page_token`.

params.name: label_ids
params.description: Optional Gmail label ids to filter by.

tools.name: gmail_profile
tools.description: Show the connected Gmail account's email address and mailbox totals (messages, threads, history id). Useful for confirming which mailbox the agent is operating on. AngelSend-backed only.

tools.name: gmail_send_email
tools.description: Send an email through the user's connected Gmail account (AngelSend Gmail bridge preferred, native Gmail OAuth as fallback). Set `is_html` to true to send an HTML body. Pass `thread_id` and `in_reply_to` to reply inside an existing conversation. To attach files the user uploaded into this chat, pass their ids in `attachment_ids` (the uploaded-files list in the user's turn shows each file's id). For the AngelSend gateway send (used for outbound campaigns / non-Gmail-account sends) use `angelsend_send_email` instead.

params.name: to
params.description: Recipient email address(es). Accepts a single address or a comma-separated list (e.g. `alice@example.com, bob@example.com`).

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line.

params.name: body
params.description: Message body (plain text by default; HTML if `is_html` is true).

params.name: cc
params.description: Optional CC address(es) — single or comma-separated.

params.name: bcc
params.description: Optional BCC address(es) — single or comma-separated.

params.name: reply_to
params.description: Optional Reply-To address (native send only).

params.name: is_html
params.description: Set to true if `body` contains HTML rather than plain text. Defaults to false.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Optional Gmail thread id to send the message into (used to reply to a conversation).

params.name: in_reply_to
params.description: Optional RFC 5322 Message-ID of the message being replied to.

params.name: attachment_ids
params.description: Optional ids of files the user uploaded into this chat, to attach to the email. Ids come from the uploaded-files list shown in the user's turn. Sending with attachments uses native Gmail (the AngelSend bridge can't carry files), so the user must have Google connected.

tools.name: google_admin_get_user
tools.description: Get one directory user by email or id (read-only). Returns email, full name, admin/suspended flags, and org-unit path. Requires Workspace admin access.

params.name: user_key
params.description: The user's primary email or numeric id.

tools.name: google_admin_list_groups
tools.description: List groups in the connected Google Workspace directory (read-only). Returns each group's email, name, and member count. Requires Workspace admin access.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max groups to return (default 100).

tools.name: google_admin_list_users
tools.description: List users in the connected Google Workspace directory (read-only). Returns email, full name, admin/suspended flags, and org-unit path. Optionally filter with a directory query like 'isAdmin=true' or 'orgName=Engineering'. Requires Workspace admin access.

params.name: query
params.description: Optional Admin SDK users query, e.g. 'isAdmin=true' or 'email:jane*'.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max users to return (default 100).

tools.name: google_calendar_create_event
tools.description: Create an event in one of the user's Google calendars (defaults to the primary calendar). Use this when the user asks to put a meeting on their *personal* / Google calendar. For events that should live inside a Kavanah project use `create_calendar_event` (the Kavanah one) instead.

params.name: calendar_id
params.description: Optional target calendar id. Defaults to `primary`.

params.name: summary
params.description: Event title.

params.name: start
params.description: Event start. Preferred: naked local time `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]` (no `Z`, no offset) — the handler pairs it with `time_zone` (defaulted to the user's IANA zone from the system prompt) so Google handles DST correctly. Or send ISO 8601 with an explicit offset (e.g. `2026-06-09T13:00:00-07:00`). NEVER hand-compute a `Z` time.

params.name: end
params.description: Event end, same format rules as `start`.

params.name: description
params.description: Optional event body / agenda.

params.name: location
params.description: Optional location string or video link.

params.name: time_zone
params.description: Optional IANA time zone (e.g. `America/Los_Angeles`). When omitted, the handler defaults this to the calling user's profile timezone — so a naked local `start`/`end` resolves correctly without you having to specify it. Override only when the event genuinely lives in a different zone (e.g. a meeting hosted in another city).

params.name: attendees
params.description: Optional list of attendee email addresses.

params.name: send_updates
params.description: Optional invite delivery mode: `all`, `externalOnly`, or `none` (default: do not notify).

tools.name: google_calendar_delete_event
tools.description: Cancel (delete) an event in the user's Google Calendar. Get the event id from `google_calendar_list_events`. Undo re-creates it with the same details (as a new event).

params.name: event_id
params.description: The event's id (from google_calendar_list_events).

params.name: calendar_id
params.description: Optional calendar id. Defaults to `primary`.

params.name: send_updates
params.description: Optional: `all`, `externalOnly`, or `none` (default: do not notify attendees).

tools.name: google_calendar_list_calendars
tools.description: List the user's Google calendars (primary + any shared calendars they've added). Returns calendar id, name, and access role. Call this when you need a calendar id to pass to `google_calendar_list_events` or `google_calendar_create_event` (other than the user's primary calendar, which is the implicit default).

tools.name: google_calendar_list_events
tools.description: List events from one of the user's Google calendars in a given time window. Defaults to the primary calendar. Each line includes the event id that `google_calendar_update_event` / `google_calendar_delete_event` need. Use this for personal-calendar / Google-calendar questions; for Kavanah task due-dates use `list_calendar_tasks` instead. For AngelSend's calendar use `angelsend_list_calendar_events`.

params.name: calendar_id
params.description: Optional calendar id. Defaults to `primary`.

params.name: time_min
params.description: Start of the window, ISO 8601 (e.g. 2026-05-20T00:00:00Z). Optional.

params.name: time_max
params.description: End of the window, ISO 8601. Optional.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max events to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: google_calendar_update_event
tools.description: Change an existing event in the user's Google Calendar: move it, rename it, or change its description, location or attendees. Only the fields you pass are changed. Get the event id from `google_calendar_list_events`. Same time rules as `google_calendar_create_event` (naked local time, never a hand-computed `Z`). Undoable.

params.name: event_id
params.description: The event's id (from google_calendar_list_events).

params.name: calendar_id
params.description: Optional calendar id. Defaults to `primary`.

params.name: summary
params.description: New title.

params.name: start
params.description: New start; pass `end` too when moving an event.

params.name: end
params.description: New end.

params.name: description
params.description: New event body / agenda.

params.name: location
params.description: New location or video link.

params.name: time_zone
params.description: Optional IANA zone for start/end; defaults to the user's profile timezone.

params.name: attendees
params.description: Replaces the attendee list with these email addresses.

params.name: send_updates
params.description: Optional: `all`, `externalOnly`, or `none` (default: do not notify attendees).

tools.name: google_chat_list_messages
tools.description: List recent messages in a Google Chat space. Returns sender, text, and time. Read-only.

params.name: space_name
params.description: 'spaces/<id>' from google_chat_list_spaces.

tools.name: google_chat_list_spaces
tools.description: List the Google Chat spaces (rooms + DMs) the user belongs to, with their resource name + display name. Call this first to get a space name before reading or posting.

tools.name: google_chat_send_message
tools.description: Post a text message to a Google Chat space as the user. Confirm the destination space with the user before sending to an unfamiliar space.

params.name: space_name
params.description: 'spaces/<id>' to post into.

params.name: text
params.description: Message text to send.

tools.name: google_docs_append
tools.description: Append content to the end of an existing Google Doc (any doc the user has, by id). Use this to add a section, a meeting note, or a log entry. Markdown renders as real Docs formatting (headings, bold, bullets, numbered lists, links, code). Prefix the text with a leading newline if you want it to start on a fresh line.

params.name: document_id
params.description: The document id from its URL.

params.name: text
params.description: Content to append. Markdown is rendered with real styling. Use \n for line breaks.

tools.name: google_docs_create
tools.description: Create a new Google Doc with the given title and optional initial body. Returns the new document's id and a shareable edit URL. Use this to draft notes, summaries, proposals, or reports into the user's Google Docs. Markdown in `text` renders as REAL Docs formatting — `#` headings, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `- ` bullets, `1. ` numbered lists, [links](url), and ``` code blocks — so write documents in Markdown rather than plain text when structure matters.

params.name: title
params.description: Title of the new document.

params.name: text
params.description: Optional initial body. Markdown is rendered with real styling (headings, bold, bullets, links). Use \n for line breaks.

tools.name: google_docs_get
tools.description: Read the full plain-text content (and title) of a Google Doc. The `document_id` is the id in the doc's URL (`/document/d/<id>/edit`). Tables, images, and rich formatting are flattened to text.

params.name: document_id
params.description: The document id from its URL.

tools.name: google_drive_activity_query
tools.description: Query the Google Drive activity feed (read-only). Returns recent activity entries with timestamp, action (edit/create/move/comment/…), and the file titles touched. Optionally scope to one file via item_name ('items/<fileId>') or pass an EBNF time filter.

params.name: item_name
params.description: Optional Drive item to scope to, e.g. 'items/<fileId>'.

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional EBNF filter, e.g. time >= "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z".

params.name: page_size
params.description: Max entries to return (default 25).

tools.name: google_forms_add_question
tools.description: Append a question to a Google Form. `kind` is 'text' (short answer), 'paragraph' (long answer), or 'choice' (single-select radio — supply `options`).

params.name: form_id
params.description: The form id to add to.

params.name: title
params.description: The question text.

params.name: kind
params.description: Question type.

params.name: options
params.description: Choice options (required when kind='choice').

params.name: required
params.description: Whether an answer is required. Default false.

tools.name: google_forms_create
tools.description: Create a new Google Form with the given title. Returns its id and edit URL. Add questions with google_forms_add_question.

params.name: title
params.description: Title of the new form.

tools.name: google_forms_get
tools.description: Read a Google Form's structure: title, description, responder URL, and the list of questions (with type, required flag, and choice options). The `form_id` is in the form's edit URL (`/forms/d/<id>/edit`).

params.name: form_id
params.description: The form id from its URL.

tools.name: google_forms_list_responses
tools.description: Read the submitted responses to a Google Form (most recent first). Returns each response's answers keyed by question id. Read-only.

params.name: form_id
params.description: The form id to read responses for.

tools.name: google_meet_create_space
tools.description: Create a Google Meet space; returns its join URL + meeting code.

tools.name: google_meet_get_space
tools.description: Look up a Meet space by 'spaces/<id>' from create_space (not a meeting code).

params.name: name
params.description: 'spaces/<id>' or bare id.

tools.name: google_meet_get_transcript
tools.description: Read a past Meet call's transcript and recording link (plus notes and tasks if Kavanah imported it). Give either field.

params.name: conference_record
params.description: conferenceRecords/<id>

params.name: meeting_code
params.description: abc-defg-hij: its newest call

tools.name: google_meet_list_conference_records
tools.description: List recent past Meet calls with start/end times.

params.name: filter
params.description: e.g. space.meeting_code = "abc-defg-hij"

tools.name: google_sheets_append_rows
tools.description: Append one or more rows after the last row of data in a tab (a 'log a new entry' operation). `range` is usually just the tab name (e.g. `Sheet1`); Sheets finds the table and inserts below it. `values` is an array of rows.

params.name: spreadsheet_id
params.description: The spreadsheet id from its URL.

params.name: range
params.description: Tab name or A1 range identifying the table to append to, e.g. `Sheet1`.

params.name: values
params.description: Rows to append — an array of arrays of cell values (string or number).

params.name: input_option
params.description: Value parsing mode. Default USER_ENTERED.

tools.name: google_sheets_get
tools.description: Inspect a Google Sheets spreadsheet's metadata — its title and the list of tabs (with row/column counts). Use this first to discover tab names before reading or writing ranges. The `spreadsheet_id` is the long id in the sheet's URL (`/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit`).

params.name: spreadsheet_id
params.description: The spreadsheet id from its URL.

tools.name: google_sheets_read_range
tools.description: Read the cell values in an A1 range of a Google Sheet (e.g. `Sheet1!A1:D50`). Returns the rows as text. Defaults to unformatted values; pass render_option to control formatting.

params.name: spreadsheet_id
params.description: The spreadsheet id from its URL.

params.name: range
params.description: A1-notation range, e.g. `Sheet1!A1:D50`. A bare tab name reads the whole used range of that tab.

params.name: render_option
params.description: How values render. Default UNFORMATTED_VALUE.

tools.name: google_sheets_update_range
tools.description: Overwrite the cell values in an A1 range of a Google Sheet. `values` is an array of rows (each row an array of cells). The range's top-left cell anchors the write. Use `USER_ENTERED` (default) to let Sheets parse numbers/dates/formulas, or `RAW` to write strings verbatim.

params.name: spreadsheet_id
params.description: The spreadsheet id from its URL.

params.name: range
params.description: A1-notation range whose top-left cell anchors the write, e.g. `Sheet1!A1`.

params.name: values
params.description: Rows to write — an array of arrays of cell values (string or number).

params.name: input_option
params.description: Value parsing mode. Default USER_ENTERED.

tools.name: google_slides_add_image
tools.description: Insert an image (by public https URL) onto a specific slide. The URL must be publicly reachable by Google. Position/size in points; defaults to a 300×200 box if omitted.

params.name: presentation_id
params.description: The presentation id.

params.name: slide_object_id
params.description: Object id of the slide to place the image on.

params.name: image_url
params.description: Public https URL of the image.

params.name: x
params.description: Left position in points (default 40).

params.name: y
params.description: Top position in points (default 40).

params.name: width
params.description: Width in points (default 300).

params.name: height
params.description: Height in points (default 200).

tools.name: google_slides_add_slide
tools.description: Append a new slide to a presentation and (optionally) fill its title/body text. Use this to build a deck slide by slide. For free-form placement, follow up with google_slides_add_text_box / google_slides_add_image targeting the returned slide id (re-read with google_slides_get to get ids).

params.name: presentation_id
params.description: The presentation id to append to.

params.name: title
params.description: Slide title text (used by all layouts except BLANK).

params.name: body
params.description: Optional body text (TITLE_AND_BODY only). Use \n for line breaks/bullets.

params.name: layout
params.description: Slide layout. Default TITLE_AND_BODY. For a section divider use TITLE_ONLY.

tools.name: google_slides_add_text_box
tools.description: Add a free-floating text box with text to a specific slide. Get the slide's object id from google_slides_get. Position/size are in points on a 720×405 (16:9) canvas; sensible defaults are used if omitted.

params.name: presentation_id
params.description: The presentation id.

params.name: slide_object_id
params.description: Object id of the slide to place the text box on.

params.name: text
params.description: The text to put in the box.

params.name: x
params.description: Left position in points (default 40).

params.name: y
params.description: Top position in points (default 40).

params.name: width
params.description: Width in points (default 640).

params.name: height
params.description: Height in points (default 120).

tools.name: google_slides_create
tools.description: Create a new (empty) Google Slides presentation with the given title. Returns its id and a shareable edit URL. Follow up with google_slides_add_slide to add content.

params.name: title
params.description: Title of the new presentation.

tools.name: google_slides_delete_object
tools.description: Delete a slide or a single element (shape/image/etc.) by its object id (from google_slides_get). Deleting a slide id removes the whole slide.

params.name: presentation_id
params.description: The presentation id.

params.name: object_id
params.description: Object id of the slide or element to delete.

tools.name: google_slides_duplicate_object
tools.description: Duplicate a slide or element by its object id (from google_slides_get). Returns the new object's id. Duplicating a slide id copies the whole slide.

params.name: presentation_id
params.description: The presentation id.

params.name: object_id
params.description: Object id of the slide or element to duplicate.

tools.name: google_slides_get
tools.description: Read a Google Slides presentation: its title, slide count, the plain text of each slide, and each slide's object id plus the object ids/kinds of the elements on it (so you can target a specific slide or shape with the edit tools). The `presentation_id` is the id in the deck's URL (`/presentation/d/<id>/edit`).

params.name: presentation_id
params.description: The presentation id from its URL.

tools.name: google_slides_insert_text
tools.description: Insert text into an existing shape or placeholder by its object id (from google_slides_get). Appends at insertion_index (default 0 = start).

params.name: presentation_id
params.description: The presentation id.

params.name: object_id
params.description: Object id of the shape/placeholder to insert text into.

params.name: text
params.description: The text to insert.

params.name: insertion_index
params.description: Character index to insert at (default 0).

tools.name: google_slides_replace_text
tools.description: Find-and-replace text across the entire presentation — ideal for filling a templated deck (e.g. replace {{client}} with a name). Returns how many occurrences changed.

params.name: presentation_id
params.description: The presentation id.

params.name: find
params.description: Text to find.

params.name: replace
params.description: Replacement text.

params.name: match_case
params.description: Case-sensitive match (default false).

tools.name: google_tasks_create_task
tools.description: Create a new task in a Google Tasks list. `due` is an RFC3339 timestamp (Google honors only the date portion).

params.name: tasklist_id
params.description: The task-list id to add to.

params.name: title
params.description: Task title.

params.name: notes
params.description: Optional notes/details.

params.name: due
params.description: Optional due date, RFC3339 e.g. 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z.

tools.name: google_tasks_list_tasklists
tools.description: List the user's Google Tasks lists (each has an id + title). Call this first to get a task-list id before listing or creating tasks.

tools.name: google_tasks_list_tasks
tools.description: List the tasks in one Google Tasks list. Returns title, status (needsAction/completed), notes, and due date. By default hides completed tasks — set show_completed to include them.

params.name: tasklist_id
params.description: The task-list id from google_tasks_list_tasklists.

params.name: show_completed
params.description: Include completed tasks. Default false.

tools.name: google_tasks_update_task
tools.description: Update a Google Task — change its title/notes/due, or mark it complete (status=completed) or reopen it (status=needsAction). Only the fields you pass are changed.

params.name: tasklist_id
params.description: The task-list id the task belongs to.

params.name: task_id
params.description: The task id to update.

params.name: title
params.description: New title.

params.name: notes
params.description: New notes.

params.name: due
params.description: New due date, RFC3339.

params.name: status
params.description: Set 'completed' to mark done, 'needsAction' to reopen.

tools.name: icloud_create_event
tools.description: Create an event on the user's iCloud Calendar (CalDAV; lands on their first event calendar). Times are ISO datetimes — interpret the user's local times via their timezone before calling. Confirm details with the user first.

params.name: summary
params.description: Event title.

params.name: start
params.description: Start (ISO datetime).

params.name: end
params.description: End (ISO datetime).

tools.name: icloud_list_contacts
tools.description: List the user's synced iCloud Contacts (name, emails, phones, organization). Read-only; served from the background sync's mirror.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max contacts (1..200, default 50).

params.name: q
params.description: Optional name/email substring filter.

tools.name: icloud_list_events
tools.description: List the user's iCloud Calendar events in a window (live CalDAV read across their event calendars; recurring events come back expanded). Read-only. Defaults to the next 7 days.

params.name: from
params.description: Window start (ISO datetime). Default: now.

params.name: to
params.description: Window end (ISO datetime). Default: from + 7 days.

tools.name: icloud_list_messages
tools.description: List recent iCloud Mail INBOX messages (envelopes synced by the background sync: subject, from, to, date, unread). Read-only. Requires the user to have connected iCloud in Settings → Integrations. Bodies are not synced — this is for scanning what arrived, not reading full mail.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max messages (1..100, default 25).

tools.name: icloud_send_email
tools.description: Send an email from the user's iCloud Mail account (SMTP). Confirm recipients and content with the user before sending — this leaves the workspace.

params.name: to
params.description: Recipient address(es), comma-separated.

params.name: body
params.description: Plain-text body.

params.name: cc
params.description: Optional CC address(es), comma-separated.

params.name: bcc
params.description: Optional BCC address(es), comma-separated.

params.name: reply_to
params.description: Optional Reply-To address.

tools.name: import_tasks_from_csv
tools.description: Import tasks from CSV text into a NEW project in this workspace. Recognizes the standard, Jira, and Asana CSV column layouts; rows become tasks and any section/status column becomes a board column. Assignees are matched to workspace members by name. Returns a summary of what was created.

params.name: content
params.description: The raw CSV text to import.

params.name: project_name
params.description: Name for the new project the tasks are created under. Defaults to "CSV import".

tools.name: import_tasks_from_monday
tools.description: Import a Monday.com board export (JSON or CSV) into a NEW project in this workspace. Items become tasks, groups become board columns, and people are matched to workspace members by name. Re-importing the same export is skipped (no duplicate). Returns a summary of what was created.

params.name: content
params.description: The raw Monday.com export, as a JSON or CSV string.

params.name: format
params.description: Force the export format. When omitted it is sniffed from the content.

params.name: project_name
params.description: Optional name for the new project. Defaults to the Monday board's name.

tools.name: import_tasks_from_trello
tools.description: Import a Trello board export (the raw JSON you get from Trello's 'Export as JSON') into a NEW project in this workspace. Cards become tasks, lists become board columns, and members are matched to workspace members by name. Re-importing the same board is skipped (no duplicate). Returns a summary of what was created.

params.name: content
params.description: The raw Trello board export, as a JSON string.

params.name: project_name
params.description: Optional name for the new project. Defaults to the Trello board's name.

tools.name: inbox_list_unread
tools.description: List unread messages in the user's inbox (`is:unread in:inbox` — spam, trash and archived mail excluded). Returns two sections: (1) exactly the messages the /inbox sidebar badge counts — mail synced from natively connected mailboxes — and (2) the AngelSend Gmail bridge mailbox, read live, when connected. These can be different accounts; when the user asks about the badge, answer from section 1 and never say you checked a mailbox you did not list. Bridge ids work with `inbox_reply` / `gmail_get_message`. For full Gmail search syntax use `gmail_list_messages` directly.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max messages to return. Default 15, capped at 100.

tools.name: inbox_reply
tools.description: Reply to a specific inbox message by id. Fetches the original message to populate Subject (`Re: …`), thread id, and In-Reply-To headers, then sends the reply via the user's connected Gmail. The agent only needs to supply the body — and optionally an explicit recipient override or HTML flag.

params.name: message_id
params.description: Gmail message id of the message being replied to (the `id` from `inbox_list_unread` / `gmail_list_messages`).

params.name: body
params.description: Reply body (plain text by default).

params.name: is_html
params.description: Set to true if `body` is HTML rather than plain text.

params.name: to_override
params.description: Optional override recipient address. Defaults to the original sender. Useful if the original was sent via a mailing list.

params.name: cc
params.description: Optional Cc recipients (single address or comma-separated).

params.name: reply_all
params.description: When true, addresses the reply to the original sender plus everyone on To/Cc (excluding the connected account). Defaults to false.

tools.name: inbox_status
tools.description: Check the user's inbox: how many unread INBOX messages the /inbox badge counts (mail synced from natively connected Gmail / Outlook / Proton), and whether the AngelSend Gmail bridge is connected, which account it points at and its unread-in-inbox count. The badge and the bridge can be DIFFERENT mailboxes. Use this as a quick first-pass before suggesting inbox actions.

tools.name: ingest_meeting_transcript
tools.description: Process a meeting transcript (paste the text): extract a concise summary, the decisions made, action items (with owners/deadlines where stated), and topics — then optionally create tasks from the action items. Owners are matched to workspace members by name; action-item tasks land in the workspace's default project tagged 'Meeting'. Idempotent: re-ingesting the same transcript returns the prior result without duplicating tasks. Use this whenever the user shares meeting notes or a standup/call transcript.

params.name: title
params.description: A name for the meeting, e.g. 'Weekly standup 2026-07-07'.

params.name: transcript
params.description: The full transcript text.

params.name: meeting_date
params.description: Optional meeting date (YYYY-MM-DD).

params.name: create_tasks
params.description: Whether to create tasks from the action items. Default true.

tools.name: install_app
tools.description: Install a community app into this workspace, or re-install one to move it onto its current version, granting it scopes. Granting a scope is consent on the workspace's behalf: the app's tools then reach the agent (once the workspace's app-agent opt-in is on) and its screens render, so name the scopes you are granting to the user before calling. Defaults to every scope the app requests; pass granted_scopes to grant fewer. After installing, the user still mints the app's signing secret on the Apps page (Apps -> the app -> Signing secret); this tool cannot, and says so. Works for apps this workspace built and for marketplace apps it can see.

params.name: slug
params.description: The app's slug.

params.name: granted_scopes
params.description: Scopes to grant, each one the app requested. Omit to grant everything it requests.

params.name: agent_access
params.description: Whether the agent may call the app's tools. Defaults to true on first install; omit on re-install to keep the current setting.

tools.name: instantiate_project_template
tools.description: Create a new project from a template. Copies the template's task list, phases, statuses, and custom fields onto a new project.

params.name: category
params.description: Override template category

params.name: start_date
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD

params.name: deadline
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: integrations_status
tools.description: List the integrations (AngelSend, etc.) the current user has connected, including the account email and the most recent error if any. Call this before suggesting an external action so you know whether the user already authorized the relevant provider.

tools.name: invite_member
tools.description: Invite an email address to the workspace. `role` defaults to 'member'; pass 'admin' to grant admin on accept. ('guest' is reserved for portal flows.) Sends an invite email and starts the row as 'pending'.

params.name: role
params.description: Role granted on accept. Defaults to 'member'. Owners can't be created via invite.

tools.name: jira_create_issue
tools.description: Create an issue in a Jira project. The issue is owned by the connected Jira account. For a task that should live on Kavanah's own board use `create_task` (the Kavanah one) instead.

params.name: project_key
params.description: Jira project key to create the issue in (e.g. "ENG").

params.name: summary
params.description: Issue summary (title).

params.name: issue_type
params.description: Optional issue type name (e.g. "Task", "Bug", "Story"). Defaults to "Task".

params.name: description
params.description: Optional issue description (plain text).

params.name: due_date
params.description: Optional due date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

tools.name: jira_get_issue
tools.description: Get a single Jira issue by its key (e.g. "ENG-123"): summary, status, assignee, due date, and type.

params.name: issue_key
params.description: Jira issue key, e.g. "ENG-123".

tools.name: jira_list_issues
tools.description: List issues on the connected Jira site, optionally filtered. Pass a `project_key` to scope to one project, or a raw `jql` query for anything more specific. For Kavanah's own task board use `search_tasks` instead.

params.name: project_key
params.description: Optional Jira project key (e.g. "ENG") to list issues from.

params.name: jql
params.description: Optional raw JQL query (overrides `project_key`), e.g. 'assignee = currentUser() AND statusCategory != Done'.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max issues to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: jira_list_projects
tools.description: List the projects on the connected Jira site. Returns each project's key and name. Call this first to get a project key for `jira_list_issues` / `jira_create_issue`.

tools.name: jira_list_transitions
tools.description: List the workflow transitions available from a Jira issue's CURRENT status (e.g. 'Start Progress → In Progress', 'Done → Done'). Which transitions exist depends on where the issue is now and the project's workflow. Use this to discover the transition id (or confirm a target status is reachable) before calling `jira_transition_issue`.

params.name: issue_key
params.description: Jira issue key, e.g. "ENG-123".

tools.name: jira_transition_issue
tools.description: Move a Jira issue to a new status by applying a workflow transition. Provide either `transition_id` (from `jira_list_transitions`) or `target_status` (the status name you want, e.g. "In Progress" — it's matched against the available transitions). Only transitions valid from the issue's current status work; if none matches, the available options are returned.

params.name: issue_key
params.description: Jira issue key, e.g. "ENG-123".

params.name: transition_id
params.description: The transition id from jira_list_transitions. Preferred when known.

params.name: target_status
params.description: The status name to move to (e.g. "Done"). Used when transition_id isn't provided.

tools.name: jira_update_issue
tools.description: Update an existing Jira issue's summary, description, or due date. Pass `issue_key` and any fields to change. To change an issue's STATUS (e.g. move to "In Progress"/"Done"), use `jira_transition_issue` instead — status is a workflow transition, not a field. For Kavanah's own tasks use `update_task` instead.

params.name: issue_key
params.description: Jira issue key, e.g. "ENG-123".

params.name: summary
params.description: New summary (title).

params.name: description
params.description: New description (plain text).

params.name: due_date
params.description: New due date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or empty string to clear it.

tools.name: link_client_sheet
tools.description: Connect a Google Sheet tab to the workspace's client list and run the first import, saving the column mapping that sync_client_sheet reuses. Call with just `spreadsheet` to list the tabs; add `tab` to map the headers and import. Clients are matched by company name — existing companies are updated, new ones created. Headers with no Kavanah field are carried through verbatim (and mirrored back) but aren't typed or displayed. Does NOT write to their sheet (only enabling the mirror does).

params.name: spreadsheet
params.description: Google Sheets URL or bare spreadsheet id.

params.name: tab
params.description: Tab name holding the client rows. Omit to list tabs.

params.name: column_mapping
params.description: Optional explicit header → field map. Valid fields: company, contact_name, contact_role, email, location, website, owner_name, stage, health, arr_dollars, next_renewal, invoice_status. Omit to auto-map.

tools.name: link_contact_to_firm
tools.description: Attach a contact to a firm, or pass firm_id null to detach. Most contacts link themselves by email domain on the nightly pass; use this for the ones that cannot — a personal address, a stealth entity, someone who moved firms.

params.name: firm_id
params.description: Firm to attach to, or null to detach.

tools.name: link_deal_drive_folder
tools.description: Record the Google Drive folder that holds a deal's data room, for a folder created outside Kavanah. Accepts a folder id or any Drive folder URL. Verified through your Drive connection when you have one (a file, or a folder your Drive cannot see, is refused). Once recorded, get_deal_space reads it and the provision-client-space automation will not create a second folder. Refuses to replace a different folder already recorded unless replace is true.

params.name: folder
params.description: Drive folder id, or its URL (…/drive/folders/<id>).

params.name: folder_name
params.description: Display name, used only when your Drive cannot be asked for the real one.

params.name: replace
params.description: Replace a DIFFERENT folder already recorded for this deal.

tools.name: link_deal_sheet
tools.description: Connect a Google Sheet tab to a pipeline and run the first import, which SAVES the link + column mapping that sync_deal_sheet later reuses. Call with just `spreadsheet` to list the tabs; call with `spreadsheet` + `tab` to auto-map the headers and import. Always tell the user which columns were mapped — auto-mapping is a guess. Headers with no Kavanah field are carried through verbatim (and mirrored back) but aren't typed or displayed, so one that should be a real field is worth flagging. Does NOT write anything to their sheet (that only happens if the mirror is later enabled).

params.name: spreadsheet
params.description: Google Sheets URL or bare spreadsheet id.

params.name: tab
params.description: Tab (worksheet) name to import from. Omit to list the available tabs.

params.name: pipeline
params.description: Existing pipeline id or slug to import into. Defaults to the workspace default.

params.name: new_pipeline_name
params.description: Create a new pipeline with this name instead of using an existing one.

params.name: column_mapping
params.description: Optional explicit map of sheet header → Kavanah field, e.g. {"Deal":"deal_name","Amount":"amount_dollars"}. Valid fields: deal_name, stage_name, owner_name, initial_closer_name, final_closer_name, amount_dollars, revenue_dollars, expected_close, notes, contact_name, contact_email, contact_phone, contact_company. Omit to auto-map from the headers.

tools.name: link_network_sheet
tools.description: Link a Google Sheet tab (the desk's partners / investors list) to the firm and contact layer, and run the first import. Call with just `spreadsheet` to list its tabs; add `tab` to map the headers and import. The import GAP-FILLS: an empty Kavanah field takes the sheet's value, a value the sheet supplied last time follows the sheet, but a value someone edited in Kavanah is never overwritten. Linking also turns on the HOURLY re-import for this tab. It never writes to the sheet — only set_network_sheet_mirror does. Money cells accept '$1.2B', '250M', '$5M - $25M'; an unreadable cell is skipped and reported, never guessed. A bare 'Name' header is not auto-mapped (it is as often the firm as the person) — pass column_mapping when the guess leaves something important unmapped.

params.name: spreadsheet
params.description: Google Sheets URL or spreadsheet id.

params.name: tab
params.description: Tab to link. Omit to list the tabs first.

params.name: column_mapping
params.description: Optional explicit header → field map. Firm fields: firm_name, firm_website, firm_domain, firm_linkedin, firm_roles, firm_aum, firm_dry_powder, firm_check_min, firm_check_max, firm_check_range, firm_thesis, firm_sectors, firm_stages, firm_geographies, firm_partner_status, firm_supply_offered, firm_mandate_notes. Contact fields: contact_name, contact_first_name, contact_last_name, contact_email, contact_title, contact_phone, contact_relationship_status, contact_tags. Omit to auto-guess.

tools.name: link_tasks
tools.description: Link two or more related tasks together. Creates a bidirectional link.

params.name: task_ids
params.description: Array of task IDs to link together

tools.name: list_active_timers
tools.description: List currently running (un-ended) time entries in the workspace.

tools.name: list_agent_conversations
tools.description: List the current user's most recent AI-agent conversations (id, title, last activity). Read-only, self-scoped — only the calling user's own chats. Use when the user refers vaguely to an earlier session ('that chat from last week') and you need to find it; feed an id to get_agent_conversation.

tools.name: list_agent_schedules
tools.description: List the recurring autonomous agent runs in this workspace — name, prompt, frequency, UTC time, autonomy level, enabled flag, model (null = inherited; 'auto' = routed per run), only_when_tasks_for / task_gate (the person whose tasks gate each run, if any), next_run_at, last run status/error, and an estimated credits/month per schedule from its recent runs. Use before update/cancel to get the schedule id.

params.name: persona_id
params.description: Optional — only schedules bound to this persona.

tools.name: list_ai_personas
tools.description: List the AI Employee personas configured in this workspace. Use when the user asks 'which AI employees are available?' or wants to inspect persona capabilities, scopes, or assigned models.

params.name: include_disabled
params.description: Default false. Pass true to include disabled personas.

tools.name: list_app_navigation
tools.description: List the whole Kavanah navigation map — every page/surface grouped by area (Main, Inbox, Build, Insights, Workspace, Settings, Admin, global), each with its sidebar location, route, and a one-line description, plus the keyboard shortcuts. Use to answer broad questions like 'what can Kavanah do?', 'give me a tour', 'what's in the sidebar?', or to orient a brand-new user during onboarding.

tools.name: list_approvals
tools.description: List approval asks: the ones still waiting on a human (oldest first, with age and reviewer), and the ones decided recently with the reviewer's answer and comments. Call this before request_approval, and at the start of any run that is waiting on a decision, so you act on an answer instead of asking again.

params.name: status
params.description: open = still waiting; decided = answered in the last `days`; all = both. Default all.

params.name: days
params.description: Look-back for decided asks, in days. Default 14, max 90.

tools.name: list_assignment_decisions
tools.description: List recent human task-assignment decisions from the assignment ledger — who was recommended vs. who was actually chosen, and any recorded reason. Read-only. Only returns rows if the workspace enabled assignment-decision logging (Settings → AI Agent); otherwise empty. Use with get_assignment_decision_metrics to review override patterns at a retro.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max rows (default 50, max 200).

params.name: days
params.description: Only decisions in the last N days.

params.name: overrides_only
params.description: Only decisions where the chosen assignee differed from the recommendation. Default false.

tools.name: list_autolink_rules
tools.description: List this workspace's auto-link rules — patterns (literal or regex) that turn matching phrases in text into links to a doc, decision, glossary term, or code target. Read-only.

tools.name: list_automation_runs
tools.description: Recent execution history for one automation rule — when it fired, success/skipped/error, and the detail message from the action handler. Use this to answer 'did my rule fire?' or 'why didn't it do anything?'.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max rows to return. 1-200, default 50.

tools.name: list_automations
tools.description: List automation rules in the workspace, optionally filtered by project_ref.

tools.name: list_availability_requests
tools.description: List availability requests in this workspace (leaders → team asks for who's free during a period). Optionally filter by status (open|closed).

tools.name: list_availability_submissions
tools.description: List member availability responses. Pass request_id to filter to one request, or user_id to filter to one member. Without filters it returns the workspace's full submission set (admin-only).

tools.name: list_bd_partner_matches
tools.description: The partner pairings the hourly scan has already surfaced (and alerted on), with their status. Filter by firm or status (surfaced / dismissed).

tools.name: list_boardrooms
tools.description: List this workspace's standing meeting series (boardrooms) between AI employees — exec meetings (e.g. a daily leadership sync between the Agentic CEO, COO, CRO and CFO), board meetings, department meetings and stand-ups. Shows each series' kind, who sits at each table, the cadence, the model, whether it is armed, and its estimated monthly credit cost. Use when the user asks about their exec meetings, the leadership sync, or which AI executives meet.

tools.name: list_budget_entries
tools.description: List actual spend entries on a project's budget (or all projects if project_ref omitted).

tools.name: list_budgets
tools.description: List all project budgets with planned vs actual spending for the workspace.

tools.name: list_calendar_tasks
tools.description: List tasks with due dates that fall in a date window, grouped for calendar/timeline views. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD; window is inclusive on both ends.

params.name: from
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive)

params.name: to
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive)

tools.name: list_capacity
tools.description: List team capacity (hours per week, cost per hour) per member.

tools.name: list_chat_channels
tools.description: List the workspace chat channels visible to the caller (public channels plus private ones they belong to), with member counts and the caller's role. Read-only.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project ref to scope to that project's channels (workspace-level channels are always included). Omit for every visible channel.

tools.name: list_chat_messages
tools.description: Read the message history of a single chat thread (works for direct, group, channel, and workspace_team threads). Returns top-level messages in chronological order with sender, timestamp, and message_id — thread-replies (messages with a parent) are excluded, matching the main chat pane. Use this BEFORE drafting a reply so you have full context, and to give the user feedback on a conversation. Page backwards through history with before_message_id (must be a message_id from the same thread).

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Thread UUID from list_chat_threads.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max messages to return (default 30, max 100).

params.name: before_message_id
params.description: Page backwards: return messages older than this message_id.

tools.name: list_chat_replies
tools.description: List the threaded replies under a parent message in one of the caller's chat threads, oldest first. Read-only.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Id of the thread the parent message is in (from list_chat_threads).

params.name: parent_message_id
params.description: Id of the parent message whose replies to list.

tools.name: list_chat_shared_files
tools.description: List file/image attachments shared in the caller's chat threads, newest first. Optionally filter to one conversation (thread_id) and/or a kind. Read-only.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Optional thread id (from list_chat_threads) to only list files shared in that conversation.

params.name: file_type
params.description: Optional filter: only images, or only non-image files.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 50, capped at 100.

tools.name: list_chat_threads
tools.description: List the current user's chat threads with last-message previews and the thread kind (direct, group, channel, workspace_team). Returns thread_id values usable by list_chat_messages and post_chat_message.

params.name: include_archived
params.description: Include archived threads (default false).

params.name: kind
params.description: Optional filter by thread kind.

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: List clients in the workspace with stage, health, owner, and id.

tools.name: list_column_limits
tools.description: List per-column WIP limits and current task counts for a project. Returns one row per status with its configured wip_limit, optional name_override, and the live count of open tasks in that column.

tools.name: list_components
tools.description: List components on a project. include_archived=true also returns archived components.

tools.name: list_condensable_threads
tools.description: List discussion threads that are long enough to be worth condensing into a clean document (enough replies or body). Read-only. Returns each thread's id, title, message count, and participants — feed an id to condense_thread_to_document.

tools.name: list_connectable_github_repos
tools.description: List GitHub repositories this workspace could connect to the /dev page. Default source 'installation' reads the cached repo list from the workspace's GitHub App install(s) (fast). Pass source='oauth' to list repos visible to the calling user's connected personal GitHub account live (covers orgs without the App). Marks repos already connected to /dev. Read-only — connecting happens via connect_github_repo.

params.name: source
params.description: Where to read repos from: 'installation' (default, cached GitHub App repos) or 'oauth' (live, the calling user's personal GitHub account).

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 50, capped at 200.

tools.name: list_course_lessons
tools.description: List the course curriculum. Kavanah ships 7 free courses, 231 lessons total: `mastering-kavanah` (68 lessons, 12 modules) — Beginner to expert on the actual application — every page, every setting, every workflow. · `project-management-with-kavanah` (28 lessons, 7 modules) — The discipline of management, taught against the surfaces you already use. · `art-of-management` (33 lessons, 7 modules) — Five thousand years of the craft, from the granaries of Sumer to the age of the agent. · `securities-industry-essentials-sie` (20 lessons, 5 modules) — The foundation exam, taught from the rules themselves. · `series-7-general-securities-representative` (55 lessons, 11 modules) — The securities broker licence, taught from the rules themselves. · `series-63-uniform-securities-agent-state-law` (12 lessons, 4 modules) — The state law exam, taught from the Act and the statements of policy. · `series-82-private-securities-offerings-representative` (15 lessons, 5 modules) — The private placement licence, taught from Regulation D itself.. Returns lesson numbers, slugs, titles, subtitles, and estimated reading times, grouped by module. Omit `course` to list the whole catalogue; pass it to scope to one. Pass `module` to filter to a single module. Use as a discovery tool before recommending a specific lesson, or to answer 'what does the course cover?'. Valid module ids by course — mastering-kavanah: getting-started, projects-and-tasks, people-and-clients, communication, time-and-planning, knowledge-tools, agent-basics, agent-governance, integrations, build-and-extend, administration, expert-practice | project-management-with-kavanah: foundations, conversation-to-commitment, right-person-right-work, estimation-and-time, operating-cadence, metrics, agentic-management | art-of-management: foundations, ancient, classical, industrial, modern, contemporary, future | securities-industry-essentials-sie: sie-exam, sie-economics, sie-products, sie-trading, sie-framework | series-7-general-securities-representative: exam-and-license, equity-securities, debt-securities, municipal-securities, packaged-products, options, markets-and-trading, new-issues, customer-accounts, conduct-and-records, passing | series-63-uniform-securities-agent-state-law: usa-foundations, usa-registration, usa-conduct, usa-enforcement | series-82-private-securities-offerings-representative: s82-licence-and-exam, s82-exemptions, s82-distribution, s82-customers, s82-transactions-and-exam.

params.name: course
params.description: Optional course slug to scope the listing to. Omit to list every course.

params.name: module
params.description: Optional module id to filter the listing to (e.g. 'foundations', 'getting-started'). Omit to list all modules.

tools.name: list_custom_properties
tools.description: List custom property definitions (the workspace's user-defined fields) for a scope. Scope is the entity type the properties attach to: task, project, or client. Omit scope to list all.

tools.name: list_custom_statuses
tools.description: List the workspace's custom task statuses (board columns). Pass `project_ref` to scope to one project — that variant also seeds the default columns (Open / In Progress / In Review / Completed) on first read. Without `project_ref` returns every status row across all projects in the workspace.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project ref (e.g. '1'). When provided, the result is scoped to that project and the defaults are seeded if the project has no columns yet.

tools.name: list_custom_task_emojis
tools.description: List the workspace's CUSTOM task-emoji palette — the emojis someone has added on top of Kavanah's built-in picker groups. Use before adding one (to avoid proposing something already there) and when the user asks what emoji conventions this workspace uses. Note this lists only the custom additions; the built-in groups are always available in the picker and are not returned here.

tools.name: list_dashboard_widgets
tools.description: List the widgets (charts/cards) on a saved dashboard by dashboard id (from list_report_dashboards). Returns each widget's id, type, title, and config. Read-only.

params.name: dashboard_id
params.description: Id of the dashboard whose widgets to list.

tools.name: list_deal_cadences
tools.description: List the workspace's follow-up cadences (standing multi-step outreach sequences): each cadence's steps, day offsets, and how many active enrollments are running. Read-only.

tools.name: list_deals
tools.description: List deals in Deal Room, the workspace's pipeline of record. Filter by pipeline (id or slug), stage, owner_name, or search by deal name. Returns id, name, stage, owner, revenue, expected close date, and primary contact — call get_deal with that id as deal_id for amount, probability, notes, and activity. Default excludes closed and archived deals; set include_closed to see won/lost too, and include_archived to see deals that were archived (marked ARCHIVED, for archive_deal with restore).

params.name: pipeline
params.description: Pipeline id or slug (e.g. 'bau' or 'top-client').

params.name: stage
params.description: Stage id or slug (e.g. 'interest', 'verbal').

params.name: owner_name
params.description: Filter by deal owner name (case-insensitive).

params.name: search
params.description: Substring match on deal name.

params.name: include_archived
params.description: Also list archived deals.

tools.name: list_decision_suggestions
tools.description: List AI-DETECTED decision candidates awaiting human review — statements in documents or meeting transcripts that look like decisions worth recording. Each carries the suggested title, what was decided, a verbatim source quote, the source it came from, and a confidence level. Read-only. The suggestions are assistive and may miss decisions; only a human review (review_decision_suggestion, or Knowledge → Decisions → Suggested) turns one into a real decision record.

params.name: status
params.description: Which candidates to list: 'pending' (default), 'accepted', 'dismissed', or 'all'.

tools.name: list_decisions
tools.description: List architecture / product decisions, most-recently decided first.

tools.name: list_department_members
tools.description: List the people (and AI personas) that belong to a department. Use to see who's responsible for a queue.

params.name: department_id
params.description: Department UUID

params.name: department_name
params.description: Department name (alternative)

tools.name: list_departments
tools.description: List all departments in the current workspace, with member counts. Use to discover what teams exist before routing a task or assigning members.

tools.name: list_deployments
tools.description: List deployments recorded on this Kavanah workspace's /dev page, newest first. Returns each deploy's id, repo id, environment, status, sha, who triggered it, start label, and duration. Read-only history — this does NOT start a deploy. Kavanah's own dev data.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: list_detected_activities
tools.description: List the caller's own captured work: pending detected activities awaiting review (from their connected sources), their connected activity sources, and their snoozed/blocked tasks. All rows are scoped to the CURRENT user — never another member's captured activity.

tools.name: list_dev_repos
tools.description: List the code repositories connected to this Kavanah workspace's /dev page (GitHub-synced). Returns each repo's id, full name, provider, default branch, language, star + open-PR counts, health status, and last-sync label. Reads Kavanah's own dev data, not an external service.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: list_discussion_threads
tools.description: List recent discussion threads, optionally filtered by project_ref.

tools.name: list_docs_pages
tools.description: List every page of Kavanah's official documentation, grouped by section (Getting Started, Core Features, Dev & AI, Integrations & Apps, API Reference), with each page's slug and title. Use to see what documentation exists before reading a page, or to tell the user what the /docs site covers.

tools.name: list_document_backlinks
tools.description: List documents that link to this one (via @-mentions or wiki-style title references). Returns id + title for each source document.

tools.name: list_document_block_comments
tools.description: List block-level comments on a document. Each comment is anchored to one block; replies carry parent_comment_id.

tools.name: list_document_templates
tools.description: List all documents flagged as templates. Use before create_document_from_template to find the right template_id.

tools.name: list_engineering_notes
tools.description: List every internal engineering note with its title and the sections inside it. Use to orient before searching, or to answer 'what internal notes exist?' / 'what areas are documented?'.

tools.name: list_escalation_rules
tools.description: List escalation rules in the workspace, optionally scoped to a project.

tools.name: list_exec_meetings
tools.description: List exec meetings that have actually happened, newest first: when each met, the chair's closing summary, how many tasks it produced, and what it cost in model calls. Use when the user asks what the execs decided, what came out of the leadership sync, or what the meetings are costing.

params.name: boardroom
params.description: Optional: only meetings from this boardroom (id or exact name).

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 20, capped at 100.

tools.name: list_feature_requests
tools.description: List the product feature-request board (public ideas, most-upvoted first) plus the caller's own submissions and summary counts by status. Optional filters: status, category, search.

params.name: status
params.description: Filter: 'active' (default, excludes declined/duplicate), 'all', or a specific status (submitted/under_review/planned/in_progress/shipped/declined/duplicate).

params.name: category
params.description: Optional category filter (general/ux/integration/performance/mobile/reporting/ai/security/other).

params.name: search
params.description: Optional substring search over title/description.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 100, capped at 200.

tools.name: list_field_permissions
tools.description: List all field-level permission rules in the workspace (per role, per resource field: can-view / can-edit). Admin only.

tools.name: list_firms
tools.description: List institutions (investors, issuers, broker-dealers) in the workspace with their AUM, dry powder, check size, thesis, sectors and how many contacts we know there. Filter by role, sector, minimum AUM, or a text search across name and thesis. Use this to answer 'which allocators could write this cheque' before looking at individual people.

params.name: role
params.description: Only firms carrying this role.

params.name: search
params.description: Text match against name and thesis.

params.name: sector
params.description: Only firms tagged with this sector.

params.name: min_aum_dollars
params.description: Only firms with at least this AUM, in dollars.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max firms. Default 50, capped at 500.
