tools.name: list_glossary
tools.description: List glossary terms.

tools.name: list_goals
tools.description: List the workspace's goals/OKRs with each one's target, latest measured value, and status (on_track / at_risk / off_track). Use when the user asks 'how are we tracking?' or to ground a review.

params.name: status
params.description: Optional filter. Default: all.

tools.name: list_inbound_requests
tools.description: List inbound submissions from external request pages. Filter by status (new|in_review|resolved|archived|all) and/or page_id. Non-admin callers see only requests against pages they own.

params.name: limit
params.description: Default 50, max 200.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: List engineering incidents tracked on this Kavanah workspace's /dev page, newest first. Returns each incident's id, title, severity (SEV1–SEV3), owner, detected/mitigated labels, alert source, summary, and any linked task refs. Kavanah's own dev data.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: list_installed_apps
tools.description: List every community app INSTALLED in this workspace (built here or from the marketplace): slug, pinned version, enabled, whether the agent may use its tools, whether its screens render, the scopes granted, tool-call health, and whether a newer version is available. Use it to answer 'which apps do we have', to find what to configure_app_install or uninstall_app, and to see whether an app the user just built is installed yet.

tools.name: list_investor_matches
tools.description: The persisted investor ranking for a deal, best first, with each firm's score, the reasons behind it, its tranche, its status and how many named contacts we hold there. Filter by status to answer specific questions: 'released' is the set being worked now, 'ranked' is what is queued behind it, 'approached' and 'dismissed' are spent. A firm showing 0 contacts needs enrichment before anyone can actually email it.

params.name: limit
params.description: Default 100, capped at 500.

tools.name: list_invites
tools.description: List workspace invites with status, role, expiry, and the inviter. Auto-expires any pending invites past their expiry before reading. Returns up to 50 most-recent rows.

tools.name: list_issuer_campaigns
tools.description: The workspace's issuer campaigns — each a named CLIENT MANDATE (what kind of company this desk wants to represent: themes, sectors, stages, geographies, raise range) with where its prospecting stands: how many issuers are ranked, released, approached, engaged, converted and dismissed, which network cadence it enrolls into, tranche size, whether auto-release is on, and what the 6-hourly scan last did (dated). Start here when someone asks about prospecting, new clients, or the issuer pipeline. No campaigns yet means nothing is being prospected — upsert_issuer_campaign creates one.

params.name: include_archived
params.description: Also list archived campaigns. Default false.

tools.name: list_issuer_matches
tools.description: The persisted prospect ranking for an issuer campaign, best first, with each firm's score, the reasons behind it, its tranche, its status, how many named contacts we hold there and, once converted, the deal it became. Filter by status: 'released' is the set being worked now, 'ranked' is queued behind it, 'approached' has had mail sent, 'engaged' has REPLIED or taken a meeting (the leads — go and talk to them), 'converted' became a deal, 'dismissed' is off the list. A firm showing 0 contacts needs sourcing before anyone can email it.

params.name: campaign
params.description: Campaign id or exact name.

params.name: limit
params.description: Default 100, capped at 500.

tools.name: list_knowledge_documents
tools.description: List knowledge-base documents in the workspace, newest-updated first.

params.name: limit
params.description: Default 25, max 200

tools.name: list_learned_task_templates
tools.description: List the smart task templates this workspace has learned from its own completed work (typical subtask checklist, effort, priority, skill mix per tag). Use to offer a proven starting point when creating a similar task. Read-only.

tools.name: list_linked_accounts
tools.description: List the user's connected third-party integrations (a.k.a. 'Linked accounts' in Settings) with full metadata: provider slug, current status, connected-at, last-used-at, and last-status-reason. More verbose than `integrations_status`. Note: this is distinct from the browser-cookie 'Linked accounts' device account-switcher, which the agent cannot manage (it lives only in the user's browser).

tools.name: list_manager_checkins
tools.description: List the caller's own manager check-ins, newest first, with the prompt they were asked and their answer if they gave one. Use unanswered_only to find what is still outstanding. Personal data only.

params.name: unanswered_only
params.description: Default false.

params.name: limit
params.description: Default 20, max 100.

tools.name: list_meeting_notes
tools.description: List recently ingested meeting transcripts with their summaries and how many tasks each produced. Use to recall what a past meeting decided or committed to.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results. Default 20, capped at 100.

tools.name: list_meeting_twin_sessions
tools.description: The caller's recent twin / notetaker meetings: status (joining, in the meeting, ended…), why it ended, and whether notes are ready.

tools.name: list_member_profiles
tools.description: List every workspace member's experience profile (LinkedIn URL, self-described experience, whether a resume is on file) together with their declared/learned skills. Use before assignment decisions when recommend_assignees' skill scores need human context — e.g. to break a tie or when nobody has skill chips yet.

tools.name: list_members
tools.description: List all workspace team members with their email, role, job title, and calendar booking link (where they have set one). Use to look up a person by name when assigning tasks, and to get someone's booking link when a meeting with them needs scheduling.

tools.name: list_message_requests
tools.description: List the caller's cross-workspace connection (message) requests — pending invites they've received and/or sent. Read-only. This does NOT create or respond to requests.

params.name: direction
params.description: Which requests to list: incoming (received), outgoing (sent), or all. Default all.

tools.name: list_message_templates
tools.description: List message templates in the workspace.

tools.name: list_my_agent_jobs
tools.description: List the current user's recent background agent jobs (queued, running, completed, failed). Use this when the user asks about the status of bulk operations.

tools.name: list_my_commitments
tools.description: List the caller's own commitments — work they promised to finish by a date. Shows the ORIGINAL deadline alongside the current one, so you can see what has been renegotiated. Personal data only.

params.name: status
params.description: Filter by status. Default 'open'.

params.name: limit
params.description: Default 50, max 200.

tools.name: list_my_notes
tools.description: List all of the caller's own saved notes (the multi-note Notepad), newest-updated first. Returns each note's id, title, and size — use get_my_note to read a full body. Personal data only.

tools.name: list_my_open_tasks_across_workspaces
tools.description: List open tasks assigned to the calling user across every workspace they belong to, sorted by overdue → due-soon → newest. Use for cross-workspace 'what's on my plate today' answers.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max rows (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: list_my_orgs
tools.description: List every organization (org) the calling user belongs to, with their role and the number of workspaces in each org. Use as a navigation aid when the user references an org by name.

tools.name: list_my_reminders
tools.description: List the caller's own private reminders, sorted with open ones first by time. This is the current user's personal data only.

tools.name: list_my_reward_history
tools.description: The caller's own points ledger (every award and deduction, with its reason) and their credit payout history. Use this to explain why a balance is what it is. Personal data only.

params.name: limit
params.description: Default 25, max 100.

tools.name: list_my_todos
tools.description: List the caller's own private to-do items, open ones first in sort order. This is the current user's personal data only.

tools.name: list_my_workspaces
tools.description: List every workspace the calling user is an active member of, with their role, open task count, tasks assigned to them, and last activity. Use to answer 'what workspaces am I in?' or 'where do I have the most going on?'

tools.name: list_negation_hits
tools.description: Read the negation ledger — the work this workspace REFUSED, and which charter lines did the refusing. Returns totals, how many were overridden anyway, and the most-cited Negations. Use for 'what did we say no to this quarter?', for the charter review (a Negation with zero hits is either irrelevant or invisible; one with many hits is earning its keep), and whenever the user asks whether the charter is actually doing anything.

params.name: days
params.description: Lookback window in days. Default 90, capped at 365.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Restrict to one project. Omit for the whole workspace.

tools.name: list_network_contacts
tools.description: List PEOPLE in the network — the way to read back what a scan, an import or a research pass saved. Filter by tags (all of them must be present), by source ('linkedin', 'sheet', 'agent'), by a text search across name, email and company, or by firm_id. This is how you answer 'the family offices we found on LinkedIn': list by the tag or source you saved them under, then feed the ids to get_contact_warmth, enroll_contacts_in_cadence or merge_contacts. For the institutions rather than the people, use list_firms; for everyone at ONE firm, get_firm.

params.name: tags
params.description: Only contacts carrying ALL of these tags. Matched lowercase, as they are stored.

params.name: source
params.description: Only contacts recorded with this source, e.g. 'linkedin'.

params.name: search
params.description: Substring match across name, email and company.

params.name: firm_id
params.description: Only contacts attached to this firm.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max contacts. Default 50, capped at 200.

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.description: List the current user's in-app project/board notification feed (the same feed as the notification bell), with optional unread-only filter. Covers kanban/board events (task moved between columns, task completed), assignments, due-date/reminder, comments, milestones, overdue, meetings, project/file and discussion events, and automation alerts — scoped to projects the user is allowed to see. Returns project_ref + notification_id pairs needed by the read/snooze/dismiss tools. This does NOT include chat/DM messages (use list_chat_threads) or email (use inbox_list_unread) — check those separately for full notification coverage.

params.name: limit
params.description: Default 50

tools.name: list_objectives
tools.description: List strategic objectives (OKRs) and their key results in the workspace.

tools.name: list_observability_alerts
tools.description: List observability alerts (Sentry/Datadog/PagerDuty) synced to this Kavanah workspace's /dev page, newest first. Returns each alert's id, source, title, service, severity, 24h event count, first-seen label, and any linked task ref or incident. Kavanah's own dev data.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: list_onboarding_docs
tools.description: List role-based onboarding docs.

tools.name: list_org_templates
tools.description: List the org templates: whole AI organisations (board, C-suite, SVPs/VPs, directors, ICs — each with a job description, least-privilege capabilities, a reporting line and a North Star contribution) plus standing meetings between them. Returns role and series keys.

tools.name: list_outcome_checks
tools.description: List the post-conditions recorded for this workspace and how they settled — met, missed, still pending, or cancelled. Includes the hit rate over the settled ones. Use this to see whether your past actions actually landed before claiming a pattern of success, and to notice work that quietly went nowhere.

params.name: status
params.description: Optional filter. Default: all, with missed and pending surfaced first.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max rows. Default 50, cap 200.

tools.name: list_persona_departments
tools.description: List the departments an AI persona belongs to.

params.name: persona_id
params.description: Persona UUID

params.name: persona_name
params.description: Persona name (alternative)

tools.name: list_pinned_chat_messages
tools.description: List the pinned messages in one of the caller's chat threads. Read-only. Pass a thread_id from list_chat_threads.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Id of the thread (from list_chat_threads).

tools.name: list_pipeline_stages
tools.description: List the stages of a pipeline in board order, with each stage's kind (open = in motion, won/lost = closed), default probability, staleness threshold, and color. Use before create_deal/update_deal_stage when unsure what stages exist, or before reconfiguring stages.

params.name: pipeline
params.description: Pipeline id or slug. Defaults to the workspace default.

tools.name: list_proactive_alerts
tools.description: List proactive agent alerts for the current user (due-soon, overloaded member, stale task, blocked task, deadline conflict, etc.). Returns alert id + type + severity + title + body + metadata + related_task_id / related_project so the model can decide how to remediate. Excludes dismissed by default.

params.name: include_dismissed
params.description: Default false.

params.name: unread_only
params.description: If true, only return alerts the user hasn't read yet.

params.name: alert_type
params.description: Filter by alert type: bd_match, investor_batch_exhausted, issuer_batch_exhausted, contact_runway_low, setup_reminder, credit_refused_request, due_soon, overloaded_member, stale_task, duplicate_task, abandoned_task, health_shift, daily_priority, unread_thread, deadline_conflict, process_improve, effort_mismatch, blocked_task, morning_briefing, escalation, approval_pending, approval_digest, agent_weekly_report, decision_candidate.

params.name: limit
params.description: Default 50, max 200.

tools.name: list_programs
tools.description: List all portfolio programs in the workspace. Programs group projects under a strategic umbrella.

tools.name: list_project_files
tools.description: List files attached to a project.

tools.name: list_project_folders
tools.description: List the workspace's project folders (groupings of projects) in display order. Returns each folder's id, name, color, and sort order. Use the returned folder id with assign_project_to_folder.

tools.name: list_project_keys
tools.description: List per-project issue-key prefixes (e.g. KAV for KAV-123). Each row carries the keyPrefix and the next allocation number.

tools.name: list_project_permission_overrides
tools.description: List a member's per-project role overrides (roles that apply only within a specific project). Admin only.

params.name: user_id
params.description: Member user id (UUID) whose overrides to list.

tools.name: list_project_templates
tools.description: List all project templates in the workspace.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List all projects in the current workspace. Call this first when you need to know which projects exist or need a project_ref for other tools.

tools.name: list_proof_annotations
tools.description: List every proofing annotation (review pin) on an image / PDF attachment, oldest first. Each pin carries a comment, normalized x/y position (0..1), page number, author, and resolved flag. Use to review feedback on a design file before acting on it.

params.name: file_id
params.description: The attachment / project-file id (a global UUID) to list pins for.

tools.name: list_pull_requests
tools.description: List pull requests tracked on this Kavanah workspace's /dev page, newest number first. Returns each PR's id, number, repo id, title, state (draft/review/approved/merged/blocked), author, branch → base branch, linked task ref, additions/deletions, reviewer count, and CI status. Kavanah's own GitHub-synced data.

params.name: limit

tools.name: list_recent_activity_across_workspaces

tools.name: list_recent_commits

tools.name: list_recurring_emails

tools.name: list_recurring_tasks

tools.name: list_report_dashboards
tools.description: List the workspace's saved report dashboards (custom analytics boards), default first. Returns each dashboard's id, name, whether it's the default, and how many widgets it holds. Read-only.

tools.name: list_report_filters

tools.name: list_report_schedules

tools.name: list_reports

tools.name: list_request_page_fields

params.name: request_page_id

tools.name: list_request_pages
tools.description: List the public request-intake pages this workspace has published. Returns each page's title, share token, status, and submission counts.

tools.name: list_resolutions
tools.description: List workspace resolutions (terminal-state reasons applied to closed tasks).

tools.name: list_resource_requests
tools.description: List resource (staffing) requests in the workspace, newest first.

tools.name: list_retros
tools.description: List sprint retros, most recent first.

tools.name: list_role_change_requests
tools.description: List role-change requests in the workspace (the approval queue for privileged role changes), optionally filtered by status. Admin only.

params.name: status
params.description: Optional status filter (e.g. pending, approved, rejected).

tools.name: list_roles
tools.description: List all RBAC roles in the workspace (system + custom), with their id, name, description, and permission map. Admin only.

tools.name: list_runbook_runs
tools.description: List in-progress and checkpoint-paused runbook runs in this workspace.

tools.name: list_runbooks
tools.description: List the workspace's runbooks (reusable SOPs/playbooks). Use this when the user asks to run a process ('do the quarterly close', 'onboard this client') to find the matching runbook, or to show what SOPs exist.

tools.name: list_saved_views
tools.description: List saved views (table/board/calendar/timeline/gallery lenses over tasks). Includes the caller's private views and any workspace-shared views. Pass project_ref to filter to a project; omit for workspace-wide + per-project together.

params.description: Filter to a project ref, or pass '*' for workspace-wide views only.

tools.name: list_scheduled_emails
tools.description: List the emails the current user has scheduled to send later, newest deadline first. Optionally filter by status. Use this to show the user what is queued or to find an id to cancel.

params.name: status
params.description: Optional status filter. Omit to list all of the user's scheduled emails.

tools.name: list_scheduled_messages
tools.description: List the caller's own scheduled (send-later) chat messages in this workspace, earliest first. Optionally filter by status. Read-only — use schedule_message to create one.

params.name: status
params.description: Optional status filter. Omit to list all of the caller's scheduled messages.

tools.name: list_share_links
tools.description: List the workspace's public read-only share links (the tokenized links that let anyone view a project or saved view WITHOUT signing in). Newest first. Optionally filter by resource_type and/or resource_id. The raw token is never stored, so this returns link metadata (id, resource, permission, expiry, revoked/created timestamps) — NOT a usable URL. Use create_share_link to mint a new link and get its URL.

params.name: resource_type
params.description: Optional filter: only links pointing at a project or a saved view.

params.name: resource_id

tools.name: list_sla_breaches

tools.name: list_sla_policies

tools.name: list_sprints
tools.description: List sprints for a project, newest first.

tools.name: list_stale_deals

params.name: only_stale

tools.name: list_stale_documents

tools.name: list_support_tickets
tools.description: List support tickets. scope='mine' returns the current user's tickets; scope='workspace' returns all (admin-only).

tools.name: list_swimlanes
tools.description: List swimlanes for a project. Swimlanes are horizontal rows on the kanban board (e.g. team, epic, priority lane). Pass include_archived=true to include archived swimlanes.

tools.name: list_task_build_statuses
tools.description: List per-task CI build status cards on this Kavanah workspace's /dev page: for each task with active work, its branch, linked PR id, and current build state (passing/failing/running/queued/skipped) with pipeline. Kavanah's own GitHub-synced data.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: list_task_candidates
tools.description: List task candidates in the triage queue (default: pending only). Use to help the user run a triage pass, or before proposing a new candidate to avoid obvious duplicates.

params.name: status
params.description: Default 'pending'.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results (default 50, max 200).

tools.name: list_task_dependencies
tools.description: List dependencies for a task (returns both directions: where the task is a predecessor and where it is a successor) or for an entire project.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Task ID to find dependencies for

params.description: Or list all dependency edges in a project

tools.name: list_task_history
tools.description: List version snapshots for a task. Each entry has a version_no, the user who triggered it, a timestamp, and a summary of the prior values. Use to answer questions like 'who last changed the due date?' or 'what did this task look like yesterday?'.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Task ID to list history for

params.name: limit

tools.name: list_task_lineages
tools.description: List task→ship lineages on this Kavanah workspace's /dev page: for each traced task, the ordered chain of nodes (task → commits → PR → deploys/alerts) linking a Kavanah task to the code that shipped it. Returns the task ref, title, project, and each node's kind/id/label. Kavanah's own dev data.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: list_task_types
tools.description: List workspace task types (Jira-style issue types). Sorted by hierarchy level (epic > story > task > subtask).

tools.name: list_tasks_with_location
tools.description: List the tasks in a project that have a geographic location pinned (for the Map view), including their coordinates and address label. Call list_projects first if you need the project_ref.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: The project reference/ID to list located tasks for.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max tasks to return (default 50, max 200).

tools.name: list_time_bound_grants
tools.description: List all time-bound (temporary) role grants in the workspace, including active, revoked, and expired ones. Admin only.

tools.name: list_time_entries
tools.description: List recorded time entries — running and finished — with the entry id, who logged it, the project and task, the duration, the billing narrative and whether it has been invoiced. This is how you find the entry to hand to update_time_entry, delete_time_entry or split_time_entry: get_time_tracking_summary only reports totals per project/person/task and carries no ids, and list_active_timers only sees timers still running. Filter by person, project or date range; newest first.

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Only this person's entries. Omit for everyone.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Only this project's entries.

params.name: start_date
params.description: ISO date/timestamp — entries started at or after this.

params.name: end_date
params.description: ISO date/timestamp — entries started at or before this.

tools.name: list_trash_items
tools.description: List the workspace's recently deleted items (the recoverable Trash) — tasks, projects, clients, members, teams, and knowledge docs. Returns each item's id, type, label, and when it was deleted. Use restore_trash_item to bring one back.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 50, capped at 200.

tools.name: list_user_departments
tools.description: List the departments a single workspace member belongs to.

params.name: user_id
params.description: Member's user_profiles UUID

params.name: member_name
params.description: Member's display name (alternative)

tools.name: list_user_roles
tools.description: List RBAC role assignments. With a user_id, returns that member's assigned roles; without one, returns every active member and their roles. Admin only.

params.name: user_id
params.description: Optional member user id (UUID). Omit to list all members and their roles.

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description: List versions on a project. status can filter to one or more lifecycle states (unreleased | released | archived), comma-separated.

params.name: status
params.description: unreleased | released | archived (comma-separated for multiple).

tools.name: list_view_fields
tools.description: List the task fields the views runtime knows about. Returns each field's key, label, type, and (for select fields) the valid option values. Use this BEFORE constructing a view config so filter/sort/group references hit real fields.

tools.name: list_waiting_on
tools.description: List the waiting-on ledger — obligations the agent is tracking. Defaults to OPEN entries ordered by due date. Check this on every scheduled run and when the user asks 'what are we waiting on?'; overdue entries should be nudged or escalated.

params.name: status
params.description: Filter by status. Default: open.

params.name: waiting_on
params.description: Optional filter by the person who owes it.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results. Default 50, capped at 200.

tools.name: list_weekly_checkins
tools.description: List per-member weekly check-in reports for the workspace, newest week first. Optionally filter by member, status, or week. Read-only.

params.name: member_user_id
params.description: Optional user id to filter to one member.

params.name: status
params.description: Optional check-in status filter.

params.name: week_start
params.description: Optional week-start date filter (format: YYYY-MM-DD).

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 50, capped at 200.

tools.name: list_workspace_apps
tools.description: List the community apps this workspace has BUILT (its own, from the developer console) — slug, name, version, tool and screen counts, and whether each is installed here. Use this before drafting a new app so you can tell the user what already exists, and to find the slug for get_app_manifest, scaffold_app_code, install_app or publish_app_version. Does not list apps merely installed from the marketplace (see list_installed_apps).

tools.name: log_actual_hours
tools.description: Set the actual_hours value on a task (cumulative, not additive).

tools.name: log_time_entry
tools.description: Log a closed time entry. Two ways: professional-services style, passing `hours` as decimal hours ("0.3") with `started_at` as the date the work happened — this is what someone means by "put 0.3 on the Acme matter"; or stopwatch style, passing explicit started_at and ended_at. `description` is the billing narrative and appears on the invoice line, so write what was actually done ("Drafted motion to dismiss"), not a category. The workspace's rounding policy is applied to the billed quantity.

params.name: started_at
params.description: ISO timestamp — with `hours`, the date/time the work began

params.name: ended_at
params.description: ISO timestamp. Omit when passing `hours`.

params.name: hours
params.description: Decimal hours ("0.3", 1.5) or clock form ("1:30"). Alternative to ended_at.

params.name: description
params.description: What was done — the narrative that appears on the client's bill.

params.name: client_id
params.description: Attribute directly to a client (from list_clients). Otherwise the project's client applies.

tools.name: mark_all_notifications_read
tools.description: Mark every notification as read for the current user.

tools.name: mark_all_proactive_alerts_read
tools.description: Mark every proactive alert as read for the current user.

tools.description: Mark a notification as read or unread for the current user.

params.name: unread
params.description: true=unread, false=read

tools.name: mark_proactive_alert_read
tools.description: Mark a proactive alert as read for the current user. Call this once the model has surfaced the alert to the user in chat.

tools.name: merge_contacts
tools.description: Merge a DUPLICATE contact into the one to keep. Admin only. The kept contact's empty fields are filled from the duplicate — nothing it already holds is overwritten, and any disagreement is reported. Every deal link, cadence enrollment, email/meeting activity, document view and sheet record pointing at the duplicate moves to the kept contact; if both were enrolled in the same sequence, the duplicate's enrollment is cancelled so the person is not mailed twice. The duplicate is archived, and future sheet syncs and AngelSend pulls route its email to the kept contact. Undoable (fields edited since are kept; cancelled enrollments stay cancelled). Confirm which record is kept before calling.

params.name: winner_contact_id
params.description: The contact to KEEP.

params.name: loser_contact_id
params.description: The duplicate to merge away and archive.

tools.name: merge_firms
tools.description: Merge a DUPLICATE firm into the one to keep. Admin only. Empty fields on the kept firm are filled from the duplicate (roles are combined; nothing already set is overwritten; disagreements are reported). Contacts, investor matches, broker-dealer matches and partner pairings move to the kept firm; where both already had a match on the same deal, the kept firm's row stays and a human decision on the duplicate's row (dismissed, approached) carries over. The duplicate is archived and future imports route its name and domain to the kept firm. Undoable. Confirm which firm is kept before calling.

params.name: winner_firm_id
params.description: The firm to KEEP.

params.name: loser_firm_id
params.description: The duplicate to merge away and archive.

tools.name: mindmap_create

params.description: Mind map title. Defaults to "Untitled".

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project ref to associate the mind map with.

params.name: graph
params.description: Optional initial React Flow graph — an object with `nodes` and `edges` arrays, passed through opaquely.

tools.name: mindmap_delete
tools.description: WRITE. Permanently delete a mind map by id.

params.name: id
params.description: The mind map id to delete.

tools.name: mindmap_get
tools.description: READ-ONLY. Fetch a single mind map by id. Returns its title, project ref, timestamps, and a compact summary of the graph (node/edge counts) rather than dumping the full React Flow payload.

params.name: id
params.description: The mind map id.

tools.name: mindmap_list
tools.description: READ-ONLY. List all mind maps in the current workspace (most-recently-updated first). Returns each mind map's id, title, optional project ref, and timestamps — not the graph itself.

tools.name: mindmap_rename
tools.description: WRITE. Rename a mind map (changes the title only, leaves the graph untouched).

params.name: id
params.description: The mind map id.

params.name: title
params.description: The new title.

tools.name: mindmap_update_graph
tools.description: WRITE. Replace a mind map's graph with a new React Flow {nodes, edges} document (passed through opaquely). Uses last-write-wins unless an expected_updated_at guard is supplied.

params.name: id
params.description: The mind map id to update.

params.name: graph
params.description: The full React Flow graph to persist — an object with `nodes` and `edges` arrays.

params.name: expected_updated_at
params.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency guard: the updated_at timestamp last seen. If it no longer matches, the write is rejected as stale.

tools.name: model_planning_scenario
tools.description: Run a what-if scheduling scenario over the current OPEN tasks and their dependencies, and report the schedule delta vs. baseline, the new critical path, any auto-rebalancing, and risks. Presets: 'baseline' (no change), 'person-out' (simulate a teammate being unavailable — pass person_id), 'scope-bump' (+12 points of scope), 'double-down' (+20% capacity). Read-only simulation; changes nothing.

params.name: preset
params.description: Which scenario to model. Defaults to 'baseline'.

params.name: person_id
params.description: For the 'person-out' preset: the planning person id of the teammate to remove (a slugified name, e.g. 'sarah-chen'). Get ids from get_resource_leveling or get_critical_path.

tools.name: monday_create_item
tools.description: Create an item (row) in a Monday board. The item is owned by the connected Monday account. For a task that should live on Kavanah's own board use `create_task` (the Kavanah one) instead.

params.name: board_id
params.description: Monday board id to create the item in.

params.name: item_name
params.description: The item's name.

params.name: group_id
params.description: Optional group (section) id to place the item in (from `monday_list_groups`).

params.name: column_values
params.description: Optional JSON object (as a string) of column values keyed by Monday column id, e.g. '{"status":{"label":"Done"}}'. Column ids are board-specific.

tools.name: monday_list_boards
tools.description: List the boards in the connected Monday.com account. Returns each board's id and name. Call this first to get a board id for `monday_list_groups` / `monday_list_items`.

tools.name: monday_list_groups
tools.description: List the groups (sections) in a Monday board. Pass `board_id` (from `monday_list_boards`). Returns each group's id and title; use a group id when creating an item.

params.name: board_id
params.description: Monday board id.

tools.name: monday_list_items
tools.description: List items (rows) in a Monday board. Pass `board_id` (from `monday_list_boards`). For Kavanah's own task board use `search_tasks` instead.

params.name: board_id
params.description: Monday board id.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max items to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: monday_update_item
tools.description: Update an existing Monday item's column values. Pass `board_id`, `item_id`, and `column_values` (a JSON object keyed by Monday column id). For Kavanah's own tasks use `update_task` instead.

params.name: board_id
params.description: Monday board id the item belongs to.

params.name: item_id
params.description: Monday item id to update.

params.name: column_values
params.description: JSON object (as a string) of column values keyed by Monday column id, e.g. '{"status":{"label":"Working on it"}}'.

tools.name: namespa_create_dns_records
tools.description: Add DNS records to a domain (up to 50 at once). Every record is validated before any is written. This ADDS — it never replaces an existing record; to change one use namespa_update_dns_record. A second SPF (v=spf1) TXT record on the same name is refused because it would break email for the whole domain; to add an email sender use namespa_setup_email, which merges SPF. List the records first so you do not duplicate one.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

params.name: records
params.description: The records to add.

tools.name: namespa_create_url_forwarding
tools.description: Redirect a domain or subdomain to a URL, e.g. example.com → https://www.example.com. type "redirect" is a permanent 301, "302" a temporary one, "masked" keeps the domain in the address bar (a frame). The registrar may change that host's A records to serve it, and it can take up to 24 hours.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

params.name: host
params.description: Host RELATIVE to the domain: "" or "@" for the root (example.com itself), "www" for www.example.com, "_dmarc" for _dmarc.example.com. A full name ending in the domain is accepted and trimmed.

params.name: forwards_to
params.description: Full destination URL starting https:// or http://.

params.name: type
params.description: Default redirect (301).

tools.name: namespa_delete_dns_record
tools.description: Delete one DNS record by id. Deleting the wrong A, MX or TXT record can take a website or mailbox offline, so confirm the record with the user first. Returns the deleted record in full so it can be recreated exactly.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

params.name: record_id
params.description: The record's id from namespa_list_dns_records.

tools.name: namespa_delete_email_forwarding
tools.description: Stop forwarding an alias. Mail to that address will bounce unless a mailbox exists for it.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

params.name: alias
params.description: The alias, e.g. "info" or "*".

tools.name: namespa_delete_url_forwarding
tools.description: Remove a URL forwarding rule by id (from namespa_list_url_forwarding).

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

params.name: forwarding_id
params.description: The rule's id.

tools.name: namespa_get_account
tools.description: Show the connected NameSpa account: its email, how many domains it holds, and which SCOPES the connected API key has — read (look), write (change DNS / email / settings) and purchase (register, renew, transfer). Call this first when a write or purchase is refused, or before promising the user you can make a change.

tools.name: namespa_get_domain
tools.description: Details of one domain in the user's NameSpa account: created and expiry dates, auto-renew, transfer lock, WHOIS privacy, nameservers and renewal price.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

tools.name: namespa_get_transfer_status
tools.description: Status of the user's inbound domain transfers. A transfer usually takes about five days; a completed one becomes a normal domain in the account.

tools.name: namespa_list_contacts
tools.description: List the registrant contacts saved in the user's NameSpa account (ICANN requires one on every registration). The default one is used when a purchase names none.

tools.name: namespa_list_dns_records
tools.description: List every DNS record on a domain, each with its numeric id. The ids are what namespa_update_dns_record and namespa_delete_dns_record take. Read this before changing records so you know what is already there. Records only take effect while the domain uses NameSpa's default nameservers.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

tools.name: namespa_list_domains
tools.description: List the domains in the user's NameSpa account with expiry date, auto-renew, transfer lock, WHOIS privacy and nameservers. Also names any transfers still in progress.

tools.name: namespa_list_email_forwarding
tools.description: List a domain's email forwarding rules (alias → destination inbox).

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

tools.name: namespa_list_url_forwarding
tools.description: List a domain's URL forwarding (redirect) rules, each with its numeric id.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

tools.name: namespa_purchase_domain
tools.description: REGISTER a domain, paid in NameSpa credits. A registration cannot be undone or refunded. Always call namespa_quote_domain first, tell the user the total and the renewal price, and get their explicit yes in this conversation before calling. expected_price_usd must be the per-year price_usd from that quote; if the price has moved the purchase is refused and you must re-quote and re-confirm. Registering accepts the registrar's terms on the user's behalf. Only available when a workspace admin has turned on Domain purchases in Settings → AI Agent, and the NameSpa key needs the Purchase scope.

params.name: domain
params.description: The exact domain from the quote.

params.name: years
params.description: Term, 1-10. Must match the quote. Default 1.

params.name: expected_price_usd
params.description: Per-year price_usd from namespa_quote_domain, e.g. "14.94".

params.name: accept_registration_terms
params.description: Must be true. The user has agreed to register the domain under NameSpa's registration terms.

params.name: contact_id
params.description: Registrant contact id from namespa_list_contacts. Omit to use the account default.

params.name: nameservers
params.description: Optional nameservers to set at registration (two or more).

tools.name: namespa_quote_domain
tools.description: Price ONE exact domain for registration: whether it is available, whether it is premium, the price per year, the total for the term, the NameSpa credits it would cost, and the renewal price. namespa_purchase_domain requires the per-year price this returns, so always quote first and show the user the total before buying.

params.name: domain
params.description: The exact domain, e.g. acmelabs.com.

params.name: years
params.description: Registration term, 1-10. Default 1. Some TLDs have a longer minimum (.ai is 2).

tools.name: namespa_renew_domain
tools.description: RENEW a domain in the user's NameSpa account for 1-10 more years, paid in NameSpa credits. Cannot be undone. Confirm the domain and term with the user first. Only available when Domain purchases is on in Settings → AI Agent.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

params.name: years
params.description: Years to add, 1-10. Default 1.

tools.name: namespa_reveal_transfer_code
tools.description: Reveal a domain's transfer authorization (EPP) code. With this code ANYONE can move the domain to another registrar, taking its website and email with it. Only call when the user has asked, in this conversation, to transfer this specific domain away, and never paste the code anywhere but back to that user. Only available when Domain purchases is on in Settings → AI Agent, and the key needs the Purchase scope.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

tools.name: namespa_search_domains
tools.description: Search for available domain names by keyword, with first-year and renewal prices in USD (NameSpa's prices, markup included). Use for brainstorming. To price ONE exact domain for purchase, use namespa_quote_domain.

params.name: keyword
params.description: Letters, digits, spaces or hyphens, e.g. 'acme labs'.

params.name: tlds
params.description: Optional TLD filter, e.g. ["com", "io"].

params.name: max_results
params.description: Max results to return. Default 20, capped at 50.

tools.name: namespa_set_email_forwarding
tools.description: Forward mail for an address on the domain to another inbox, e.g. info@example.com → someone@gmail.com. Updates the rule if the alias already forwards somewhere. Use "*" as the alias for a catch-all. On a domain with no mail set up the registrar may add its own MX records to make forwarding work; on a domain that already uses a mail provider, forwarding and that provider conflict — check namespa_list_dns_records first.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

params.name: alias
params.description: The part before the @, e.g. "info", or "*" for every address.

params.name: forward_to
params.description: Destination email address.

tools.name: namespa_set_nameservers
tools.description: Point a domain at different nameservers — for example Cloudflare's or Vercel's. This MOVES THE WHOLE DOMAIN'S DNS: every record kept at NameSpa stops being served, so a website or mailbox not recreated at the new provider goes dark once it propagates (up to 48 hours). Confirm with the user first. Returns the previous nameservers so the change can be reverted.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

params.name: nameservers
params.description: Two or more nameserver hostnames, e.g. ["ada.ns.cloudflare.com", "bob.ns.cloudflare.com"].

tools.name: namespa_setup_email
tools.description: Configure a domain's email DNS in one step: MX (where mail is delivered), SPF (who may send — MERGED into any existing SPF record, never duplicated), DKIM (signing keys) and DMARC (policy). Use provider "google" for Google Workspace; for any other provider (Microsoft 365, Fastmail, Zoho, Resend, Postmark…) pass the exact records that provider gave the user. If the domain already delivers mail somewhere else it is refused unless replace_mx is true, and an existing DMARC policy is kept unless replace_dmarc is true: ask the user before setting either. Reports each record created, updated, unchanged or removed.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

params.name: provider
params.description: A built-in preset (MX + SPF). Only Google Workspace is built in.

params.name: mx
params.description: MX records from the provider.

params.name: spf_includes
params.description: SPF include domains, e.g. ["spf.protection.outlook.com"].

params.name: dkim
params.description: DKIM keys from the provider. A value starting v=DKIM1 becomes a TXT record; a hostname becomes a CNAME.

params.name: dmarc
params.description: Full DMARC policy, e.g. "v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@example.com". Start with p=none on a new domain.

params.name: replace_mx
params.description: Remove MX records pointing at other mail servers. Only with the user's explicit agreement — mail moves.

params.name: replace_dmarc
params.description: Overwrite an existing, different DMARC policy.

tools.name: namespa_transfer_in_domain
tools.description: Start transferring a domain INTO NameSpa from another registrar, paid in NameSpa credits (a transfer normally adds a year). Needs the authorization (EPP) code from the current registrar, and the domain must be unlocked there. Call once WITHOUT expected_price_usd to learn the price, tell the user, then call again with it after they agree. Takes about five days; check namespa_get_transfer_status. Only available when Domain purchases is on in Settings → AI Agent.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain to bring in.

params.name: auth_code
params.description: Authorization / EPP code from the current registrar.

params.name: expected_price_usd
params.description: The transfer price the user agreed to, from the first call's refusal message.

tools.name: namespa_update_dns_record
tools.description: Change one DNS record by id (from namespa_list_dns_records). Pass only the fields that change; the rest are kept. Returns the previous record so it can be put back.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

params.name: record_id
params.description: The record's id from namespa_list_dns_records.

params.name: type
params.description: Record type. A CNAME cannot sit at the root; use ANAME or A there.

params.name: host
params.description: Host RELATIVE to the domain: "" or "@" for the root (example.com itself), "www" for www.example.com, "_dmarc" for _dmarc.example.com. A full name ending in the domain is accepted and trimmed.

params.name: answer
params.description: The value: an IP for A/AAAA, a hostname for CNAME/ANAME/MX/NS, the text for TXT (no surrounding quotes needed).

params.name: ttl
params.description: Seconds. Minimum 300 (the registrar's floor); default 300.

params.name: priority
params.description: MX / SRV only. Lower is preferred. Default 10.

tools.name: namespa_update_domain_settings
tools.description: Change a domain's auto-renew, WHOIS privacy or transfer lock. Turning auto-renew off means the domain EXPIRES at its expiry date unless renewed by hand; unlocking is the first step of moving a domain away, so only unlock when the user is transferring it out. Pass only the settings that change.

params.name: domain
params.description: The domain, e.g. example.com. It must be registered through the user's NameSpa account.

params.name: autorenew_enabled
params.description: Renew automatically at expiry (charged to NameSpa credits).

params.name: privacy_enabled
params.description: Hide the registrant's details from public WHOIS.

params.name: locked
params.description: Transfer lock. true blocks transfers away.

tools.name: notion_append_to_page

params.name: content
params.description: Text to append.

tools.name: notion_create_page
tools.description: Create a Notion page. Provide exactly one parent: `parent_page_id` (a sub-page) or `parent_database_id` (a new database row). The page is created in the connected Notion workspace, NOT in Kavanah. For a Kavanah task use `create_task` instead.

params.name: title
params.description: Page title.

params.name: content

params.name: parent_page_id

params.description: Notion page id.

params.name: database_id

params.name: project_ref

params.name: limit

tools.name: notion_list_databases
tools.description: List the Notion databases the connected integration can see. Returns each database's id and title. Use a database id with `notion_query_database` (read rows) or `notion_create_page` (add a row).

params.name: limit

tools.description: List the rows (pages) in a Notion database. Pass `database_id` (from `notion_list_databases` or `notion_search`). Returns each row's id, title, and key property values. To bring these rows into Kavanah as tasks, use `notion_import_database_as_tasks`.

params.name: database_id
params.description: Notion database id.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max rows to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: notion_read_page
tools.description: Read a Notion page's body content as plain markdown-ish text (top-level blocks). Pass `page_id` (from `notion_search` or `notion_get_page`).

params.name: page_id
params.description: Notion page id.

tools.name: notion_search
tools.description: Search the connected Notion workspace for pages and databases by text. Returns each match's id, title, type (page/database), and URL. Use `notion_read_page` to read a page's body. For Kavanah's own knowledge base use `search_knowledge` instead.

params.name: query
params.description: Text to search for in page/database titles. Omit to list the most recently edited items.

params.name: type
params.description: Optional filter to only pages or only databases.

params.name: limit

tools.name: organize_knowledge_library
tools.description: Organize the knowledge base Library into a tidy page tree. Reads the live documents (id, title, tags, current parent), has an LLM propose 3–10 topical sections with each document filed under one, and either RETURNS the proposal (default — a dry run, nothing changes) or APPLIES it with apply=true: missing section pages are created and documents are re-parented. Documents the proposal leaves out stay where they are; cycles are rejected per-move. SLOW (one LLM call over the whole library). Run the dry run first and show the user the proposal before applying unless they explicitly asked you to just organize it.

params.name: apply
params.description: false (default) = return the proposed structure only; true = create section pages and re-parent documents.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project ref to organize only that project's docs (plus workspace-shared). Omitted = whole library.

params.name: instructions
params.description: Optional steering for the structure (e.g. 'group by client', 'keep meeting notes together'). Max 300 chars.

params.name: location

params.description: Max messages to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: outlook_send_email
tools.description: Send an email through the user's connected Microsoft 365 / Outlook account via Microsoft Graph. Use when the user wants to send from their Outlook/Microsoft 365 address rather than Gmail or Proton.

params.description: Recipient email address(es). Single address or comma-separated list.

params.description: Message body.

tools.name: parse_task_from_text
tools.description: Parse a single natural-language sentence ('ask Sarah to redesign onboarding by Friday, blocked by the auth refactor') into a structured task draft — title, assignee, project, due date, priority, dependencies, subtasks — grounded in this workspace's members/projects/tags. Returns a PREVIEW; review it, then commit with create_task. Use this when the user describes a task conversationally.

params.name: sentence
params.description: The natural-language sentence describing the task.

params.name: today_iso
params.description: Optional current date (YYYY-MM-DD) for resolving relative dates like 'Friday'. Defaults to today.

tools.name: peek_undo_stack
tools.description: Check whether the calling user has anything they can undo or redo, and the label of the top entry on each stack. Use this before suggesting 'undo that' so you can tell the user what would actually be undone (e.g. 'I'll undo deleting task X — confirm?'). Per-user stacks: an admin can only undo their own actions.

tools.name: pin_chat_message
tools.description: Pin (or unpin) a message in one of the caller's chat threads so it stays surfaced for participants.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Id of the thread the message is in (from list_chat_threads).

params.name: message_id
params.description: Id of the message to pin (from list_chat_messages).

params.name: pinned
params.description: True to pin (default), false to unpin.

tools.name: plan_outbound_capacity
tools.description: Answer 'can we sustain N emails a day' with arithmetic instead of a setting. Returns every mailbox that could carry load (configured limit, connected provider, or recent queued mail), what the pool can send TODAY after warm-up ramps, what it reaches at steady state and when, what the underlying providers safely support, and how many more mailboxes a target needs. Use it before promising a volume. The distinction it exists to make: raising a cap is one setting and takes a second; sustaining the volume is a property of the mailbox pool, and a single mailbox configured at 1,000/day is refused by the provider at roughly half that while the domain's reputation absorbs the damage.

params.name: target_per_day
params.description: The daily volume to plan against. Omit or 0 to just report what the pool can carry.

tools.name: plan_realistic_deadline
tools.description: Work out an achievable deadline for a piece of work WITHOUT committing to it. Takes an estimate in hours and returns the date it would actually land on, after (a) uplifting the estimate by the caller's own historical estimate-vs-actual ratio, (b) queueing it behind everything they have already promised, and (c) spreading it across their real working days and focused hours. Also reports whether they are already at their open-commitment ceiling. Call this BEFORE proposing a date to the user — a date picked without it is a wish. Read-only.

params.name: estimate_hours
params.description: The user's own estimate of the work in hours, before calibration. Omit for work with no size, which will queue without adding load.

params.name: title
params.description: Optional label, echoed back in the explanation.

tools.name: plan_sprint
tools.description: Recommend a sprint: packs the unstarted backlog into the team's capacity, uplifting each person's estimates by their OWN estimate-vs-actual history, and reports what fits at p50 (the median — a coin flip) AND what fits at p90 (the level worth committing to), with forecast hours vs. total capacity at both, the committed points, a per-person breakdown, and what got deferred. Says so plainly when the workspace has too little history to calibrate, in which case estimates are taken at face value and p50/p90 are identical. READ-ONLY: this only RECOMMENDS — it creates no sprint and assigns no tasks. Committing a sprint is a human action in Planning → Sprint Planner.

params.name: sprint_length_weeks
params.description: Sprint length in weeks: 1, 2, or 3. Defaults to 2.

params.name: capacity_per_person_hours
params.description: Planned working hours per person per week at full-time (scaled by each member's configured weekly capacity). Defaults to 32 — deliberately below 40, since meetings and support eat the rest.

params.name: commit_level
params.description: Confidence level to pack the recommended set against. 'p90' fits less work but is the level a commitment can hold; 'p50' is the median and will miss about half the time. Defaults to 'p90'. Both levels are reported either way.

params.name: goal_emphasis
params.description: Tie-break bias within a priority band: 'ship-fast' prefers smaller items, 'tech-debt' prefers platform-tagged work, 'balanced' does neither. Defaults to 'balanced'.

tools.name: post_chat_message
tools.description: Send a chat message into an existing thread (works for direct, group, channel, and workspace_team threads). Use list_chat_threads first to pick a thread_id, and prefer list_chat_messages first to read recent context before replying.

tools.name: post_chat_reply
tools.description: Post a threaded reply to a message in one of the caller's chat threads. This DELIVERS a real message to the thread's other participants — only reply on the user's behalf when they've asked you to.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Id of the thread the parent message is in (from list_chat_threads).

params.name: parent_message_id
params.description: Id of the message being replied to (from list_chat_messages).

params.name: content
params.description: The reply text.

tools.name: post_discussion_reply
tools.description: Post a reply on an existing discussion thread.

tools.name: predict_and_apply_due_dates
tools.description: Compute and write a due_date for each task based on its AI/legacy estimate (hours), starting from start_date. Picks task hours from estimate_value+unit, falling back to story_points/estimated_hours, falling back to assume_unestimated_hours. Two modes: 'parallel' (default — each task's due date = start + its own duration, assumes concurrent work) and 'sequential_per_assignee' (each assignee's tasks stack onto a cursor, so person-by-person workload is reflected). Pass either task_ids OR a filter (project_ref/status_id/assigned_to/tag); a filter without task_ids honors only_open=true by default.

params.name: task_ids
params.description: Explicit task IDs to schedule (takes precedence over filter)

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Filter: project

params.name: status_id
params.description: Filter: status/column

params.name: assigned_to
params.description: Filter: assignee name (substring)

params.name: tag
params.description: Filter: tag (substring)

params.name: start_date
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to today

params.name: business_days
params.description: If true (default), skip Sat/Sun when computing due dates

params.name: mode
params.description: How to schedule — parallel = each task gets start+duration; sequential = stack per assignee

params.name: assume_unestimated_hours
params.description: Hours to assume for tasks without any estimate (default 8 = one working day). Set 0 to skip them.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max tasks when using a filter (1–200, default 50)

tools.name: preview_autolink_matches
tools.description: Preview which of the workspace's auto-link rules would fire on a piece of text — without changing anything. Read-only, no LLM. Returns each matched phrase and the target it would link to. Use it to sanity-check a rule before or after creating it.

params.name: text
params.description: The text to run the auto-link rules against (max 8000 chars).

tools.name: preview_billable_time
tools.description: Preview a client's unbilled billable time as ClearBooks-ready invoice line items (read-only — nothing is created or stamped). Selects billable, not-yet-invoiced entries with an end time on the client's projects, resolves each entry's hourly rate (entry override → project default → client default), and groups them into line items per project. Entries with no resolvable rate and still-running timers are listed as skipped with a reason. Amounts are integer cents. Use create_invoice_from_billable_time to actually bill.

params.name: client_id
params.description: Kavanah client id (look up with list_clients).

params.name: from
params.description: Optional ISO timestamp — only entries started at/after this.

params.name: to
params.description: Optional ISO timestamp — only entries started at/before this.

params.name: project_refs
params.description: Optional subset of the client's project refs.

tools.name: preview_org_template
tools.description: Dry run: who an org template adopts vs creates, and each series' monthly credits if armed. Admin only.

params.name: template
params.description: e.g. broker_dealer

params.name: roles
params.description: only these role keys

tools.name: preview_report_recipients
tools.description: Resolve a recipient set (literal emails + dynamic groups) to the concrete email list that would receive the report right now, without sending anything. Use to confirm a group selector covers the right people before scheduling.

tools.name: propose_follow_up
tools.description: Draft an outbound email to a deal's primary contact (or specified contact) and either save it as a Gmail draft (for human review) or schedule it for a future send. Returns the draft id or scheduled email id so the user can confirm. Use after summarizing why a follow-up is needed. In schedule mode you can also queue a multi-touch SEQUENCE via `sequence` — later touches are auto-cancelled the moment an inbound email from that contact lands on the deal (stop-on-reply).

params.name: contact_id
params.description: Optional — defaults to the deal's primary contact.

params.name: mode
params.description: draft = save to Gmail Drafts; schedule = queue for future send.

params.name: scheduled_at
params.description: When to send; required when mode=schedule. Preferred: a naked local timestamp `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]` (no `Z`, no offset) — the handler converts it from the user's timezone to UTC. Or ISO 8601 with an explicit offset. NEVER hand-compute a `Z`/UTC timestamp — DST math is error-prone.

params.name: provider
params.description: Which provider to send through. Defaults to auto.

params.name: sequence
params.description: schedule mode only: up to 4 additional follow-up touches after the first send. Each is queued relative to the previous touch and auto-cancelled if the contact replies before it goes out. Write each touch's actual email content — do not reuse the first body verbatim.

tools.name: propose_interview_writes
tools.description: Draft the config values from the interview's answers and stage them for review WITHOUT writing anything. Returns the draft so you can show it to the user and ask them to confirm before apply_interview_writes. Call this only after record_interview_answer says all questions are answered.

params.name: interview_id
params.description: The interview to draft from.

tools.name: propose_task_candidate
tools.description: File a CANDIDATE task into the triage queue for human review — do NOT create a task directly — when you detect a commitment or action in a conversation, email, or meeting that someone should probably do but you shouldn't act on unilaterally. The reviewer accepts (creating the real task), edits, or dismisses it. Always ground it: put the exact phrase that implies the work in source_excerpt. If the work is clearly the smallest checkable unit, leave suggested_subtasks empty; if it's a big lump, break it into checkable pieces so the reviewer can accept it as-is.

params.name: title
params.description: Short imperative task title (<= 200 chars).

params.name: description
params.description: One or two sentences of context.

params.name: suggested_project_ref
params.description: Optional project id this belongs to. Omit if unsure — the reviewer picks.

params.name: suggested_assignee
params.description: Optional workspace member name who looks like the right owner.

params.name: suggested_subtasks
params.description: Optional checkable sub-steps if the candidate is too big to be one unit.

params.name: source_kind
params.description: Where you detected it. Default 'agent'.

params.name: source_excerpt
params.description: The verbatim phrase from the source that implies this work. Grounds the candidate.

tools.name: protonmail_list_messages
tools.description: List recent ProtonMail messages already synced into Kavanah by the background ProtonMail sync. Returns subject, from, to, date, and unread flag. Use as the Proton-side equivalent of `gmail_list_messages` — the Bridge has no live search, so this reflects whatever the sync window pulled.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max messages to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: protonmail_send_email
tools.description: Send an email through the user's connected ProtonMail account (via the ProtonMail Bridge — IMAP/SMTP, end-to-end encrypted). Use when the user wants to send from their Proton address rather than Gmail. The Bridge must be reachable from the Kavanah server (works on the Tauri desktop build and self-hosted deployments; will fail with a connection error on cloud deployments where the Bridge is on the user's laptop).

params.name: to
params.description: Recipient email address(es). Single address or comma-separated list.

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line.

params.name: body
params.description: Plain-text message body.

params.name: cc
params.description: Optional CC address(es) — single or comma-separated.

params.name: bcc
params.description: Optional BCC address(es) — single or comma-separated.

params.name: reply_to
params.description: Optional Reply-To header.

tools.name: publish_app_version
tools.description: Add a new version to an app this workspace already owns. The manifest's slug must match the app and its version must be strictly greater than the current latest (semver). For a private app the new version becomes current immediately — but note that workspaces which already INSTALLED the app stay pinned to the version they consented to until someone re-installs, so a new screen or tool will not appear for them automatically (install_app again here to re-pin this workspace). Pass the manifest as a JSON string. This is also how a placeholder endpoint gets replaced with the real one.

params.name: slug
params.description: The slug of the app to add a version to.

params.name: manifest_json
params.description: The full app manifest as a JSON string, with a bumped version.

tools.name: publish_document
tools.description: Publish a document to a tokenized public URL. Templates cannot be published. Returns the token (used in the public URL).

tools.name: quicktube_batch_process
tools.description: Process up to 10 YouTube videos in one call. Choose which artifacts to include (transcripts free; summary or sections = 5 credits each per video). Use this when the user wants several videos analyzed in one shot.

params.name: video_urls
params.description: 1–10 YouTube watch URLs.

params.name: include_transcript
params.description: Default true.

params.name: include_summary
params.description: Default false.

params.name: include_sections
params.description: Default false.

params.name: num_sections
params.description: If include_sections, how many.

tools.name: quicktube_best_sections
tools.description: Identify the most interesting moments of a YouTube video as scored sections with start/end timestamps, title, and reason. Useful for highlight reels or 'what should I watch first' (5 credits).

params.name: video_url
params.description: YouTube watch URL.

params.name: num_sections
params.description: How many sections to return. Default 10.

tools.name: quicktube_chat_with_video
tools.description: Ask a question about a YouTube video's content. Pass a `messages` array of {role,content} (OpenAI-style); optionally pre-feed `transcript_text` or filter by `character`. 1 credit per assistant turn.

params.name: video_url

params.name: transcript_text

params.name: character

tools.name: quicktube_detect_characters
tools.description: Detect the people / speakers / interviewees in a YouTube video (3 credits). Returns named characters with roles when QuickTube can infer them.

params.name: video_url
params.description: YouTube watch URL.

tools.name: quicktube_download_video
tools.description: Render a full video or a stitched highlights reel and return the resulting download URL / job. For highlights mode pass the `sections` you want clipped (start/end in seconds).

params.name: video_url
params.description: YouTube watch URL.

params.name: sections
params.description: Highlight sections (required when video_type='highlights').

tools.name: quicktube_generate_quiz
tools.description: Generate a multiple-choice quiz from a YouTube video's content (3 credits). Returns questions with choices and the correct answer.

params.name: video_url
params.description: YouTube watch URL.

params.name: num_questions
params.description: How many questions to generate. Default 5.

tools.name: quicktube_generate_speech
tools.description: Convert text to speech using OpenAI TTS via QuickTube. Returns an audio URL or base64. Voices: 'alloy', 'echo', 'fable', 'onyx', 'nova', 'shimmer'.

params.name: text
params.description: Text to read aloud.

params.name: voice
params.description: TTS voice id (default 'nova').

tools.name: quicktube_get_channel
tools.description: Fetch details about a YouTube channel by id (title, description, subscriber/video/view counts).

params.name: channel_id
params.description: YouTube channel id (UC…).

tools.name: quicktube_get_download_url
tools.description: Get a direct download URL for a YouTube video (10 credits for the full video). For 'highlights' mode use `quicktube_download_video` with the sections you want stitched together.

params.name: video_url
params.description: YouTube watch URL.

params.name: video_type
params.description: Default 'full'.

tools.name: quicktube_get_related_videos
tools.description: Fetch videos related to a YouTube video by id. 0 credits.

params.name: video_id
params.description: YouTube video id.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Default 10, capped at 50.

tools.name: quicktube_get_transcript
tools.description: Fetch the transcript for a YouTube video (with timestamps when available). Use this before deeper analysis tools — most QuickTube AI tools can also be called directly on a video_url and they'll pull the transcript themselves.

params.name: video_url
params.description: YouTube watch URL.

params.name: languages
params.description: Preferred caption languages (ISO codes, e.g. ['en','es']).

tools.name: quicktube_get_video_comments
tools.description: Fetch comments for a YouTube video by id. 0 credits.

params.name: video_id
params.description: YouTube video id.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Default 100, capped at 500.

params.name: order
params.description: Sort order. Default 'relevance'.

tools.name: quicktube_get_video_metadata
tools.description: Fetch comprehensive metadata for a YouTube video by id (title, channel, duration, view/like counts, thumbnails, publish date). 0 credits.

params.name: video_id
params.description: YouTube video id (the 11-char watch?v=… value).

tools.name: quicktube_popular_videos
tools.description: Fetch trending / popular videos by region code.

params.name: region_code
params.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code (e.g. 'US', 'GB'). Default 'US'.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Default 10, capped at 50.

tools.name: quicktube_search_videos
tools.description: Search YouTube videos by query. 0 credits.

params.name: query
params.description: Search query.

params.name: max_results
params.description: Default 10, capped at 50.

params.name: order
params.description: Sort order. Default 'relevance'.

tools.name: quicktube_summarize_video
tools.description: Generate an AI summary of a YouTube video's content (costs 5 credits). Returns the full summary text — no follow-up call needed.

params.name: video_url
params.description: YouTube watch URL.

tools.name: rank_investors_for_deal
tools.description: Score and rank every qualified investor in the workspace against a deal, then persist the ordering. Scoring is deterministic over the stored investment profile — thesis overlap (30), sector (20), stage (15), geography (10), capacity (15) and relationship warmth (10) — so two runs give the same order. Re-running RE-SCORES without resetting anyone's state: a firm already approached stays approached, and one a human dismissed stays dismissed. Returns the top of the list plus a sample of who was excluded and why. Ranking alone contacts nobody; release_next_investor_batch is what puts firms into the working set.

params.name: batch_size
params.description: Tranche size for the ordering. Default 100.

params.name: show
params.description: How many ranked firms to list back. Default 25.

tools.name: rank_issuers_for_campaign
tools.description: Score and rank every qualified issuer in the workspace against a campaign's mandate, then persist the ordering. Deterministic over the stored mandate — theme overlap with the company's description (25), sector (20), stage (10), geography (10), raise-size fit against the mandate's range (15), timing (10: a recorded raise signal, or a last round 15-42 months old; a round closed in the last six months scores DOWN), and relationship warmth (10) — so two runs give the same order. A firm already converted to a deal by any campaign is excluded: a client is not a prospect. Re-running RE-SCORES without resetting anyone's state. Returns the top of the list plus a sample of who was excluded and why. Ranking contacts nobody; start_issuer_campaign or release_next_issuer_batch puts firms into play.

params.name: campaign
params.description: Campaign id or exact name (list_issuer_campaigns).

params.name: batch_size
params.description: Tranche size for the ordering. Default the campaign's.

params.name: show
params.description: How many ranked firms to list back. Default 25.

tools.name: react_to_chat_message
tools.description: Set the caller's emoji reactions on a chat message. Replaces only the caller's own reactions on that message (other people's reactions are preserved); pass an empty list to clear the caller's reactions.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Id of the thread the message is in (from list_chat_threads).

params.name: message_id
params.description: Id of the message to react to (from list_chat_messages).

params.name: emojis
params.description: The emoji(s) to react with as the caller (e.g. ["👍"]). Empty list clears the caller's reactions.

tools.name: read_agent_share
tools.description: Read a shared agent-answer snapshot by id (the id from an /agent-share/<id> link a teammate sent). Returns the frozen title + markdown content so you can discuss it, turn it into tasks, or save it to the knowledge base. Read-only and workspace-scoped — snapshots are immutable copies shared on purpose; this never reads anyone's live conversation.

params.name: id
params.description: The snapshot id (UUID from the /agent-share/<id> URL).

tools.name: read_docs_page
tools.description: Read one Kavanah documentation page in full, as plain text — the same content published at /docs. Use after search_docs identifies the right page, or directly when you know the page (e.g. 'task-management', 'Client Portal', 'authentication', 'full-reference'). Quote or summarize from this text rather than answering product questions from memory, and point the user to the /docs site for the formatted version.

params.name: page
params.description: Page slug or exact title. Examples: 'introduction', 'time-tracking', 'Tasks API', 'scim-sso-api'. Get slugs from search_docs or list_docs_pages.

tools.name: read_engineering_note
tools.description: Read one internal engineering note in full, as plain text. Use after search_engineering_notes identifies the right note, or directly when you know it (e.g. 'agent-undo', 'kvn', 'platform'). These notes state invariants precisely and often warn against 'simplifying' something — quote them rather than paraphrasing from memory, and say which note you got it from.

params.name: note
params.description: Note slug or exact title. Examples: 'agent-undo', 'kvn', 'agent-governance', 'integrations-mail-calendar'. Get slugs from list_engineering_notes or search_engineering_notes.

tools.name: read_project_file
tools.description: Read a project file's CONTENT as text. Spreadsheets (.xlsx) come back as CSV per sheet, Word documents (.docx) as markdown, and text-like files (txt/md/csv/tsv/json/xml/yaml) as themselves. Images, PDFs and legacy .doc/.xls are refused with a reason — attach those to the chat instead, where the model can see them directly. Read-only. Use `list_project_files` first to get the file id.

params.name: max_chars
params.description: Cap on returned characters (1000..30000, default 30000).

tools.name: read_web_page
tools.description: Open one web page and read its full text as markdown. Use after `search_google` or `web_search` to read a source properly instead of relying on its snippet, or whenever the user gives you a URL and asks what it says. Works on ordinary public pages; it cannot sign in, so pages behind a login return whatever the logged-out visitor sees. Read-only; it never changes workspace data.

params.name: url
params.description: Full http(s) URL of the page to read.

tools.name: recalculate_deal_forecast
tools.description: Recalculate the revenue forecast now and write it onto every open deal (forecast probability, momentum, expected fee, close week, confidence), adding a timeline entry on each deal whose forecast moved. It never changes a deal's own probability or any field a person set. Admin only. Use when someone wants the stored forecast brought up to date immediately rather than at the daily recalculation.

tools.name: recall_memories
