tools.description: Search the workspace's saved agent memories (decisions, commitments, people context, preferences). Call this BEFORE answering questions about past decisions or commitments, and at the start of substantive planning work. Omit `query` to list the most recent memories.

params.name: query
params.description: Natural-language search. Omit to list the newest memories.

params.name: kind
params.description: Optional filter by memory kind.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results. Default 10, capped at 50.

tools.name: recommend_assignees
tools.description: Recommend the best people to assign a task to, ranked by how well their skill profiles match the task's required skills. Read-only — does not change anything. Pass an existing task_id, or an ad-hoc title (+ optional description). Use before create_task with auto_assign, or whenever the user asks who should do something.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Recommend assignees for an existing task by ID

params.name: title
params.description: Ad-hoc task title to evaluate (if no task_id)

params.name: description
params.description: Ad-hoc task description for better skill inference

tools.name: recompute_contact_warmth
tools.description: Force an immediate warmth recompute for a contact or a whole firm, instead of waiting for the hourly pass. Use after logging a meeting or importing history, when the score on screen is visibly behind reality.

params.name: contact_id
params.description: One contact.

params.name: firm_id
params.description: Every contact at this firm.

tools.name: reconcile_contacts_into_firms
tools.description: Build the institution layer from contacts that already exist: group them by their free-text employer, create a firm for each, and attach them. This is what turns 'two contacts at the same fund are two strings that happen to match' into one firm with two relationships. Run it once after importing a contact list, and whenever a bulk import lands. Idempotent — it only ever fills an EMPTY firm link, so a contact someone deliberately pointed elsewhere is never overruled. Pass dry_run to see the plan before writing.

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Return the grouping plan without writing anything. Worth doing first on a large workspace — this reshapes every contact's affiliation in one pass.

params.name: roles
params.description: Roles applied to firms this run CREATES. Existing firms keep the roles they have.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max contacts to consider. Default 5000.

tools.name: record_assignment_reason
tools.description: Attach a reason to a logged assignment decision after the fact ('assign now, explain later') — e.g. why a leader chose someone other than the recommendation. Use when a user explains an override. Find the decision id via list_assignment_decisions.

params.name: decision_id
params.description: Id of the decision to annotate (from list_assignment_decisions).

params.name: reason
params.description: Free-text reason for the choice.

params.name: reason_category
params.description: Optional coarse category for grouping at retros.

tools.name: record_bug_report
tools.description: Record a bug report from the current user. Use this whenever a user describes something that is broken, throwing an error, behaving unexpectedly, or producing wrong output. Files an app_support_tickets row with category='bug' and automatically attaches the user's recent server/client error logs (last 15 min) into diagnostics so engineers can correlate. Prefer this over create_support_ticket for bug reports. Ask the user for reproduction steps and expected vs. actual behavior before calling. Before filing about something YOU observed in this conversation — e.g. a record you just created that a later tool says does not exist or did not persist — re-read it once first (list_projects, search_tasks or the matching get tool), and put the exact tool calls you made and what each returned, in order, into description; a re-read that finds the record means there is nothing to file.

params.name: title
params.description: Short summary of the bug (used as the ticket subject).

params.name: description
params.description: Full description of the bug, including what the user did, what they expected, and what actually happened.

params.name: reproduction_steps
params.description: Numbered or bulleted steps to reproduce, if the user provided them.

params.name: severity
params.description: Maps to ticket priority. Default 'medium'. Use 'urgent' only for data loss or total outage.

params.name: page_path
params.description: The page/route the user was on when the bug occurred, if known (e.g. '/projects/3/board').

params.name: attachment_ids
params.description: Ids of files the user attached in this chat (screenshots, recordings) to include with the report — the id values from the attachment list shown with their message. Only the user's own chat uploads attach; nothing else is included, so never tell the user a screenshot is attached unless you passed its id here.

tools.name: record_deal_activity
tools.description: Append a free-form activity row to a deal's timeline. Use for notes, manual call/meeting logs, and outbound communication that didn't flow through Kavanah.

tools.name: record_goal_value
tools.description: Set the current value for a 'manual' or 'clearbooks_metric' goal (e.g. after reading a finance number with the clearbooks_* tools). Records the value and recomputes the variance verdict.

tools.name: record_interview_answer
tools.description: Record the user's answer to the current interview question and get the next one. When all questions are answered it returns a signal to call propose_interview_writes. Pass the user's reply verbatim (lightly cleaned); do not answer on their behalf.

params.name: interview_id
params.description: The interview to record against.

params.name: answer
params.description: The user's answer to the current question.

tools.name: record_north_star_value
tools.description: Record a new measurement of the North Star. Appends to the trend and updates the current value. Only works on a scope that has its OWN metric — a project inheriting the company metric cannot record against it, because that would edit the company's number by accident. Use when the user tells you where a manually-tracked metric now stands.

params.name: value
params.description: The measured value.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project whose own North Star this measures. Omit for the company-wide one.

params.name: note
params.description: Optional short note about this reading (what changed, where the number came from).

tools.name: record_project_outcome
tools.description: Record whether a project's tagged customer-outcome actually moved, typically a quarter after close. Requires the project to have an outcome_target (set_project_outcome_target). Feeds the project-to-outcome conversion operating metric (course 6.4).

params.name: moved
params.description: true if the tagged customer outcome measurably moved, false if it did not.

params.name: note
params.description: Optional note on the observed delta / confounds.

tools.name: record_waiting_on_nudge
tools.description: Stamp an open waiting-on entry after you nudged the person (message, task comment, queued email). After 2+ nudges surface it to the user once instead. Capped at 5 nudges; past that it is refused and the entry goes on a weekly stuck list, not every digest.

tools.name: redeem_points_for_credits
tools.description: Convert the caller's earned Manager Mode points into REAL account credits. This moves money: credits are the currency that pays for AI usage. Requires the caller to have turned rewards on AND set a non-zero monthly credit cap — both default to off, and the tool fails closed with an explanation when either is missing. The payout is clamped by, in order: the monthly cap, their point balance, and the amount requested. Always tell the user the exact number of credits and points before and after.

params.name: credits
params.description: How many credits to redeem. Omit to redeem as many as the caps and balance allow.

tools.name: redo_last_action
tools.description: Pop the top redoable action off the calling user's redo stack and re-apply it. Mirror of undo_last_action. Only succeeds if the user has undone something since their last new mutation.

tools.name: refresh_learned_task_templates
tools.description: Re-mine the workspace's completed tasks to rebuild the learned task templates, then return them. Idempotent (updates rows in place). Run this when templates feel stale; otherwise prefer list_learned_task_templates.

tools.name: regenerate_project_readme
tools.description: Regenerate a project's Living README from its current tasks, decisions, and threads, and SAVE it. SLOW (one LLM call, can take tens of seconds) and token-costly. Pass project_ref to target a specific project; omitted, it uses the workspace's first project. Fails if the project has no tasks/decisions/threads to summarize.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project ref to regenerate. Omitted = first project in the workspace.

tools.name: release_next_investor_batch
tools.description: Move the next tranche of ranked investors into the working set for a deal — the 'now do the next hundred' step. REFUSES while firms from the current set are still open, and that refusal is the point: a second tranche arriving while the first is half-worked turns a priority order into a dump. Mark firms approached or dismissed to clear the set, or pass force to override deliberately. Releasing sends nothing; it marks who is in play.

params.name: size
params.description: How many to release. Default 100.

params.name: force
params.description: Release even though the current set is unworked. Say why when you do.

tools.name: release_next_issuer_batch
tools.description: Move the next tranche of ranked issuers into a campaign's working set — the 'now do the next hundred' step. REFUSES while firms from the current set are still open, and that refusal is the point: a second tranche arriving while the first is half-worked turns a priority order into a dump. Mark firms dismissed (or let sends and replies mark them approached/engaged) to clear the set, or pass force to override deliberately. Releasing sends nothing; start_issuer_campaign both releases and enrolls.

params.name: campaign
params.description: Campaign id or exact name.

params.name: size
params.description: How many to release. Default the campaign's tranche size.

params.name: force
params.description: Release even though the current set is unworked. Say why when you do.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Save a durable memory for this workspace so future conversations and scheduled runs can recall it. Use for decisions ('we slipped the API launch to Aug 15'), commitments ('Marcus owes the security review Friday'), people context ('Priya is on PTO next week'), or standing preferences ('status updates go in #ops'). Keep each memory to ONE self-contained fact, phrased so it makes sense with no surrounding context. Do NOT store anything already recorded on tasks/projects, or trivia only relevant to the current chat.

params.name: content
params.description: The fact to remember, one or two sentences, self-contained. Include absolute dates (not 'next week').

params.name: kind
params.description: What kind of fact this is. Default: context.

params.name: expires_in_days
params.description: Optional TTL in days for facts with a natural shelf life (e.g. PTO). Omit for durable facts.

tools.name: remove_custom_task_emoji
tools.description: Remove one emoji from the workspace's custom task-emoji palette. This only stops offering it as a quick pick — tasks that already carry that emoji keep it, because the emoji column is free-form and this table is a palette rather than a foreign key. Reversible by adding it again. Reports whether the emoji was actually in the set.

params.name: emoji
params.description: The emoji to remove from the palette, exactly as it appears in list_custom_task_emojis.

tools.name: remove_member_from_department
tools.description: Remove a workspace member from a department.

params.name: department_id
params.description: Department UUID

params.name: department_name
params.description: Department name (alternative to department_id)

params.name: user_id
params.description: Member's user_profiles UUID

params.name: member_name
params.description: Member's display name (alternative to user_id)

tools.name: remove_org_member
tools.description: Remove a member from an organization. The caller must be an owner or admin of that org; the caller can't remove themselves and no one can remove the org owner.

params.name: org_id
params.description: The organization id.

params.name: user_id
params.description: The user id to remove.

tools.name: remove_persona_from_department
tools.description: Remove an AI persona from a department.

params.name: department_id
params.description: Department UUID

params.name: department_name
params.description: Department name (alternative)

params.name: persona_id
params.description: Persona UUID

params.name: persona_name
params.description: Persona name (alternative)

tools.name: remove_portal_member
tools.description: Remove a portal member by id. Confirm with user first.

tools.name: remove_project_member
tools.description: Revoke someone's access to a project (admin/owner only). Identify them by `email` (or `user_id`); `name` is accepted only to clean up legacy roster entries that carry no email. Removing access from a PUBLIC project does not hide it — every workspace member can see a public project regardless. Make the project private with update_project first.

params.name: email
params.description: Email of the person to remove — the access key.

params.name: user_id
params.description: User UUID (alternative to email).

params.name: name
params.description: Legacy fallback: display name, for roster rows with no email.

tools.name: remove_project_permission_override
tools.description: Remove a member's per-project role override, so they fall back to their workspace-wide role in that project. This changes what the member can access. Requires workspace owner/admin.

params.name: user_id
params.description: Member user id (UUID).

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project reference/id whose override to remove.

tools.name: remove_project_team
tools.description: Remove a team from a project. Individual member memberships are not affected.

tools.name: remove_task_from_project
tools.description: Remove a single project membership from a task. The task remains in its other project memberships. Fails if it would leave the task with zero projects (use delete_task or move_task_to_project instead).

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project reference to remove

tools.name: remove_user_role
tools.description: Revoke an RBAC role from a workspace member. This changes what the member can access — it removes the permissions the role carried. Requires workspace owner/admin.

params.name: user_id
params.description: Member user id (UUID) to revoke the role from.

params.name: role_id
params.description: Id (UUID) of the role to revoke.

tools.name: rename_org
tools.description: Rename an organization (and optionally update its description). The caller must be an owner or admin of that org.

params.name: org_id
params.description: The organization id.

params.name: name
params.description: The new organization name.

params.name: description
params.description: Optional new description.

tools.name: rename_project_file
tools.description: Rename a file on a project. Extension is preserved if not given in the new name.

tools.name: renegotiate_commitment
tools.description: Move an open commitment's deadline, with a reason. The ORIGINAL deadline is preserved and remains what the commitment is scored against — delivering against a renegotiated date still earns, but less than delivering against the promise actually made. Use this when the user says something has slipped; it is strictly better than letting a deadline lapse.

params.name: commitment_id
params.description: Id from list_my_commitments.

params.name: new_due_at
params.description: The new deadline as an ISO 8601 datetime.

params.name: reason
params.description: Why the date is moving.

tools.name: reorder_tasks
tools.description: Reorder tasks in a project by priority or due date. Recalculates sort_order for all tasks in the project.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: The project reference

params.name: order_by
params.description: Sort criterion

params.name: direction
params.description: Sort direction (default: asc for due_date, desc for priority)

tools.name: request_approval
tools.description: Ask a human to approve, reject or request changes on a proposal you have written on a task (a campaign package, a plan, a send list). Use this INSTEAD of filing a new 'approval' / 'approval package' / 'for sign-off' task. Put the proposal on the task first (description or a comment), then call this with that task. The reviewer gets it in their daily decision digest, and it escalates if still open after 48h. Limits: one open ask per task, and at most 3 open asks per AI employee — beyond that you are refused and shown your open asks; add new material to one of them as a comment instead of asking again. Check list_approvals before asking: if the answer is already there, act on it. You can never approve your own ask, or anyone's.

params.name: task_id
params.description: The task holding the proposal.

params.name: summary
params.description: What you are asking the reviewer to decide, in one or two sentences, including what happens on approval (e.g. 'Approve the Verbal-stage investor sequence: 3 subject lines, sender Jordan Lee, 100 contacts. On approval I enroll them in AngelSend.'). Max 600 chars.

params.name: reviewer
params.description: Name or email of the workspace member who decides. Omit to ask the workspace owner.

tools.name: request_compliance_archiving_change
tools.description: Pass a member's or admin's compliance archiving preference to the workspace owner — for example "please turn archiving on", "keep records for 7 years", "use our new Smarsh address", or "turn it off". Only the owner can change archiving, so for anyone who is NOT the owner this is how their preference is heard: the owner gets an alert linking to the Archiving settings, and the request is recorded in the audit log. Nothing changes until the owner acts; say so. If the user IS the owner, use configure_compliance_archiving instead.

params.name: preference
params.description: What they would like, in their own words, plus any detail they gave (address, retention length, reason).

tools.name: rescan_stale_documents
tools.description: Re-audit a batch of this workspace's documents against its recent decisions and (re)raise stale flags. WRITES flags to the workspace. SLOW and token-costly: one LLM call per document, run sequentially, capped per call — a large workspace is scanned by re-calling with the returned next offset until there is no more. Use list_stale_documents afterwards to read the results.

params.name: offset
params.description: Document offset to start this batch at (default 0). Pass the offset returned by the previous call to continue.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max documents to scan this call (default and cap 25).

tools.name: research_contact
tools.description: Research ONE contact on the public web now and store only facts that pass the fact-check: the supporting quote must be verbatim on the source page, still there on a second independent read, about the right person (matched on firm plus title or location, rejected on any ambiguity), dated, and judged by a separate check to fully support the statement. Everything else is discarded, never softened. THIS SPENDS CREDITS: typically 25-40 per contact (search, reading up to four pages, model calls), billed to the person asking. LinkedIn is never scraped; if the asker has AngelSend connected, its LinkedIn enrichment is used only to confirm identity. Refused if the contact was researched in the last 24 hours. Separate from the automatic research a workspace can opt into for personalized cadence steps — this works whether or not that is on.

params.name: contact_id
params.description: Deal Room / network contact id.

params.name: contact_email
params.description: The contact's email, when you do not have the id.

tools.name: resend_invite
tools.description: Re-send a workspace invite. Rotates the token (so the old link stops working), extends the expiry, flips the status back to 'pending' if it was expired/declined, and emails the invitee. Fails if the invite was already accepted.

params.name: invite_id
params.description: Invite row id (UUID).

tools.name: resolve_waiting_on
tools.description: Close a waiting-on entry: status 'resolved' when the deliverable arrived, 'cancelled' when it's no longer needed. Add a short note saying how it closed.

params.name: status
params.description: Default: resolved.

params.name: note
params.description: How it closed (one line).

tools.name: restore_task_version
tools.description: Restore a task to an earlier version recorded in list_task_history. The current state is automatically saved as a 'Before restore' snapshot first, so a restore is itself reversible by restoring that newer snapshot. Identifies the snapshot by its numeric version row id (not the version_no — pass the id field from list_task_history).

params.name: version_id
params.description: The id of the version row to restore from (from list_task_history)

tools.name: restore_trash_item
tools.description: Restore a soft-deleted item back into the workspace by its trash id. The item leaves the Trash once restored. Any workspace member may restore.

params.name: trash_id
params.description: The trash item id to restore (from list_trash_items).

tools.name: retrieve_twin_context
tools.description: Search the digital twin's owner-grounded corpus (their profile bio, completed tasks they were assigned, and discussion posts they authored). Use this BEFORE answering any question about what the owner has done, decided, or thinks — it grounds the response in real artifacts. Returns the top-k most relevant text passages. Only available when the active persona is a digital twin.

params.name: query
params.description: The question or topic to ground on. A short natural-language description works best (e.g. 'how did I structure the auth migration?').

params.name: k
params.description: How many passages to return. Default 5, max 15.

tools.name: review_decision_suggestion
tools.description: Close one pending decision suggestion on the user's behalf. action='accept' creates the real decision record from it (optionally overriding title/context/what_we_chose before saving; the accepting USER is recorded as the reviewer — never the AI); action='dismiss' closes it without recording. ONLY call this when the user has explicitly said what to do with the suggestion — never accept or dismiss on your own judgment; the whole point of suggestions is that a human picks.

params.name: id
params.description: The suggestion id (from list_decision_suggestions).

params.name: action
params.description: 'accept' to record it as a decision, 'dismiss' to close it without recording.

params.name: title
params.description: Optional replacement title for the recorded decision (accept only).

params.name: what_we_chose
params.description: Optional replacement outcome text for the recorded decision (accept only).

params.name: context
params.description: Optional replacement context for the recorded decision (accept only).

tools.name: review_role_change_request
tools.description: Approve or reject a pending role-change request. Approving APPLIES the requested role change, altering what the target member can access. You cannot review your own request. Requires workspace owner/admin.

params.name: request_id
params.description: Id (UUID) of the role-change request to review.

params.name: decision
params.description: Whether to approve or reject the request.

params.name: review_note
params.description: Optional note explaining the decision.

tools.name: revoke_share_link
tools.description: Revoke a public share link by its id so its URL immediately 404s. Admin-only at the API layer. Use list_share_links to find the id. Irreversible — a new link must be minted to re-share.

params.name: link_id
params.description: The id of the share link to revoke (from list_share_links).

tools.name: revoke_time_bound_grant
tools.description: Revoke a time-bound role grant early, before its expiry. This removes the temporary access immediately. Requires workspace owner/admin.

params.name: grant_id
params.description: Id (UUID) of the time-bound grant to revoke.

tools.name: rollback_app_version
tools.description: Make an older version of an app this workspace owns the current one (what new installs get). Name the target by semver. For a private app the target is approved on the owner's say-so; for a public app only an already-approved version can be made current. Workspaces that already installed the app stay pinned to the version they consented to — including this one — so re-run install_app here if you want this workspace on the rolled-back version too.

params.name: slug
params.description: The app's slug.

params.name: version
params.description: The semver of the version to make current, e.g. '1.0.0'.

tools.name: run_exec_meeting
tools.description: Convene an exec meeting NOW, off-schedule — the execs report, discuss, and the chair files action items as tasks. Works whether or not the boardroom is armed, and does NOT arm it or disturb its cadence. THIS SPENDS: a meeting is 15-40 AI calls. Only call it when the user has clearly asked to run/hold/convene a meeting now — never as a way to answer a question you could answer with the read tools, and never on your own initiative. The meeting is queued and starts within about 5 minutes; it does not run while you wait, so tell the user to check back rather than claiming it is done. Admin only.

params.name: boardroom
params.description: The boardroom's id, or its exact name.

tools.name: run_report_schedule_now
tools.description: Trigger an off-cycle delivery of a schedule immediately (generates the report, emails the resolved recipients, and stamps last_sent_at). Useful for testing the recipient list or sending an ad-hoc copy without changing the cron. A large report can take a few minutes. If a call times out or seems to fail, do NOT call it again — check last_sent_at with list_report_schedules first: a repeat within 15 minutes of a delivery, or while one is still running, is refused so recipients are never mailed twice.

params.name: force
params.description: Send even though this schedule was delivered in the last 15 minutes. Only when the user explicitly asks for another copy.

tools.name: run_saved_view
tools.description: Execute a saved view and return the matching tasks. Returns a concise summary by default; pass detail='full' for every column. Use to answer questions like 'what tasks does the Sprint 4 view show?' without re-deriving the filter set.

params.name: detail
params.description: summary = id/title/status/assignees (default); full = every visible column.

params.name: limit
params.description: Cap returned rows (default 50, max 200).

tools.name: save_conversation_to_knowledge
tools.description: Save THIS conversation into the knowledge base as one structured document. The server condenses the transcript (context, key facts, decisions, next steps) with a single LLM call and creates the document — so PREFER this over hand-writing create_knowledge_document calls when the user asks to 'add this conversation / what we discussed to the knowledge base'. Optional title overrides the generated one; optional focus steers what to emphasize. SLOW (one LLM call). Undoable.

params.name: title
params.description: Optional document title. Omitted = a title is generated from the conversation.

params.name: focus
params.description: Optional steer for what to emphasize (e.g. 'the pricing decisions and open questions'). Max 300 chars.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Optional project ref to scope the document to. Omitted = workspace-shared.

params.name: parent_document_id
params.description: Optional existing knowledge document id to nest the saved document under.

tools.name: save_dashboard_widget
tools.description: Add a widget (a chart/card) to a saved dashboard. The dashboard must belong to this workspace. Returns the new widget's id.

params.name: dashboard_id
params.description: Id of the dashboard to add the widget to.

params.name: widget_type
params.description: Widget/chart kind (e.g. a report type like 'velocity', 'burndown', 'completion-rate'). Free-form string the UI understands.

params.name: title
params.description: Optional widget title. Defaults to widget_type.

params.name: config
params.description: Optional widget config (report filters/params such as projectRef, days). Free-form object.

params.name: position
params.description: Optional grid position (x/y/w/h). Usually set by the UI.

tools.name: save_report_dashboard
tools.description: Create a new saved report dashboard for the workspace. Returns the new dashboard's id — add charts to it with save_dashboard_widget.

params.name: name
params.description: Dashboard name (1-200 chars).

params.name: is_default
params.description: Mark this as the workspace's default dashboard. Defaults to false.

params.name: layout
params.description: Optional free-form layout object (grid positions etc.). Usually left empty and filled in by the UI.

tools.name: save_report_filter
tools.description: Save a reusable report filter preset for the workspace (a named report_type + filter config). Returns the new filter's id.

params.name: name
params.description: Filter preset name.

params.name: report_type
params.description: The report type this filter applies to (e.g. 'velocity', 'time-tracking').

params.name: filter_config
params.description: Free-form filter config saved with the preset (e.g. { projectRef, days, groupBy }).

tools.name: scaffold_app_code
tools.description: Generate the complete starter project for a Kavanah app: the HTTPS server that answers its signed tool calls (one stub handler per tool with the required fields checked), the async-operation and lifecycle-event endpoints if the manifest needs them, one page per declared screen wired to the Kavanah UI bridge, package.json, .env.example and a README with the deploy-and-connect steps. Deterministic and free — no model call. Give it the slug of an app this workspace owns (uses its current manifest) OR a manifest JSON string (a draft not yet created). Returns every file with its path; hand them to the user or write them into a task. It never contains the signing secret: that is read from an environment variable the user sets after minting it on the Apps page.

params.name: slug
params.description: Slug of an app this workspace owns. Either this or manifest_json.

params.name: manifest_json
params.description: A full manifest as a JSON string, for an app not created yet. Either this or slug.

params.name: framework
params.description: Server framework for the generated project. 'next' (default) is a Next.js App Router project that deploys to Vercel as-is; 'express' is a single Node server.

tools.name: scan_documents_for_decisions
tools.description: Scan a batch of this workspace's knowledge documents for DECISIONS that were never recorded in the decision log, filing each find as a pending suggestion for human review. WRITES suggestions (never decisions — a person accepts or dismisses every one). SLOW and token-costly: one LLM call per changed document, run sequentially, capped per call; unchanged documents are skipped free. Re-call with the returned offset until no more remain, then use list_decision_suggestions to read the results.

params.name: offset
params.description: Document offset to start this batch at (default 0). Pass the offset returned by the previous call to continue.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max documents to consider this call (default and cap 25).

tools.name: scan_workspace_readiness
tools.description: Read the workspace's setup gaps — the config that most limits how useful you can be, ranked by CONSEQUENCE (not a completion score). Use when the user asks how to set up / improve their workspace, when a new workspace is empty, or to decide what to offer to help with. Read-only. If it returns gaps, you can offer to run a setup interview (start_setup_interview) to fill one.

tools.name: schedule_email
tools.description: Schedule an email to be sent automatically at a future time, through the user's connected email provider. Use this when the user says 'send this tomorrow morning', 'email them next Monday', etc. The email is queued and delivered by a background worker at `scheduled_at`; nothing is sent now. To send immediately use gmail_send_email / angelsend_send_email; to just save a draft for manual review use gmail_create_draft. List or cancel queued emails with list_scheduled_emails / cancel_scheduled_email.

params.name: to
params.description: One or more recipient email addresses.

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line.

params.name: body
params.description: Message body (plain text by default; HTML if `is_html` is true).

params.name: scheduled_at
params.description: When to send. Preferred: a naked local timestamp `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]` (no `Z`, no offset) — the handler converts it from the user's timezone (shown in the system prompt) to UTC. Or send ISO 8601 with an explicit offset (e.g. `2026-05-28T09:00:00-07:00`). NEVER hand-compute a `Z`/UTC timestamp — DST math is error-prone. Must be in the future.

params.name: provider
params.description: Which connected provider to send through. `auto` (default) prefers the Gmail bridge, then native Gmail, then the AngelSend gateway. `gmail` forces Gmail; `angelsend` forces the AngelSend gateway.

params.name: cc
params.description: Optional CC addresses.

params.name: bcc
params.description: Optional BCC addresses.

params.name: is_html
params.description: Set to true if `body` is HTML rather than plain text. Defaults to false.

params.name: reply_to
params.description: Optional Reply-To address.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Optional Gmail thread id to send into (reply within a conversation).

params.name: in_reply_to
params.description: Optional RFC 5322 Message-ID of the message being replied to.

params.name: timezone
params.description: Optional IANA timezone, stored so the queued send is displayed in the right zone. Defaults to the calling user's timezone. You do NOT need to set this to make `scheduled_at` resolve correctly — a naked local `scheduled_at` is already interpreted in the user's timezone.

tools.name: schedule_message
tools.description: Schedule a message to send later. target_type: direct|group|channel; target_id: contact id, group uuid, or channel uuid.

params.name: scheduled_at
params.description: When to send. Preferred: a naked local timestamp `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]` (no `Z`, no offset) — the handler converts it from the user's timezone to UTC. Or ISO 8601 with an explicit offset. NEVER hand-compute a `Z`/UTC timestamp — DST math is error-prone. Must be in the future.

params.name: timezone
params.description: IANA timezone (default UTC)

tools.name: schedule_recurring_email
tools.description: Set up a RECURRING email that is re-sent automatically on a schedule (e.g. 'email the team a reminder every Monday at 9am', 'send this status note on the 1st of each month'). Unlike schedule_email (which fires once at a single timestamp), this fires again on every cron match until you disable or cancel it. The email goes out through the user's connected provider. LIVE-DATA PLACEHOLDERS: the subject and body may contain {{date}} (send date), {{tasks_due_today}}, {{tasks_overdue}}, {{tasks_due_within:N}} (next N days), and {{open_task_count}} — each is rendered against the workspace's live task data AT SEND TIME, so a deadline-reminder email lists the actual tasks instead of a static note. PER-PERSON placeholders {{my_tasks_due_today}}, {{my_tasks_overdue}}, {{my_tasks_due_within:N}} and {{my_open_tasks}} list only the tasks assigned to each recipient; a body using any of them is sent as a SEPARATE copy to each recipient (nobody sees anyone else's tasks), and a copy with nothing in it is skipped. Use them whenever a reminder goes to several people. {{tasks_completed_since_last_send}} lists tasks finished since the previous send, with who finished them — for a management completions summary. WEEKLY GOALS: {{my_weekly_goals}} (per person: their top 3 open tasks for the week, picked automatically by priority then due date and frozen for the week) and {{my_weekly_goals_status}} (per person: how each of THOSE goals stands — done / in progress / blocked / not started) make a Monday goals email and a Friday review; {{team_weekly_goals}} lists everyone's goals this week with status, for management. Prefer these placeholders for any task-reminder or status email. Use list_recurring_emails / update_recurring_email / cancel_recurring_email to manage it. For recurring REPORTS (auto-generated analytics attached as PDF/CSV), use create_report_schedule instead.

params.name: to
params.description: One or more recipient email addresses.

params.name: subject
params.description: Email subject line.

params.name: body
params.description: Message body (plain text by default; HTML if `is_html` is true).

params.name: cron_expression
params.description: Standard 5-field cron (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week), evaluated in the `timezone` field below — which defaults to UTC. Write the time the USER means in THEIR timezone and pass that timezone; do NOT convert to UTC yourself. Doing so is not just unnecessary, it is wrong twice over: if you also set `timezone`, your converted hour is then re-interpreted in that zone and the send lands hours off. Daylight saving is handled for you — `0 9 * * MON` in America/Chicago fires at 09:00 local in both summer and winter. The minute field must be specific minute(s) like `0` or `0,30` — not `*`, a range, or a step (otherwise it would send many times per hour). Examples, all local to `timezone`: `0 9 * * MON` weekly Monday 09:00; `0 9 * * MON-FRI` weekdays 09:00; `0 7 1 * *` first of each month 07:00; `0 17 * * FRI` every Friday 17:00.

params.name: provider
params.description: Which connected provider to send through. `auto` (default) prefers the Gmail bridge, then native Gmail, then the AngelSend gateway.

params.name: cc
params.description: Optional CC addresses.

params.name: bcc
params.description: Optional BCC addresses.

params.name: is_html
params.description: Set to true if `body` is HTML rather than plain text. Defaults to false.

params.name: reply_to
params.description: Optional Reply-To address.

params.name: enabled
params.description: Defaults to true. Set false to create it paused.

params.name: timezone
params.description: IANA timezone the `cron_expression` is EVALUATED in — not a display label. Defaults to UTC when omitted. Set it to the user's timezone (shown in the system prompt) and write the cron in their local time; the schedule then follows daylight saving automatically. Omitting it while writing a local-time cron schedules the send at that hour in UTC, which is wrong by the user's whole offset.

tools.name: scrappy_activate_source
tools.description: Activate a DRAFT Scrappy source so it can be scraped. Returns the updated source. No-op error if it's already active.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_captcha
tools.description: Check whether a captcha is blocking the page, and optionally attempt to solve it. Run `detect` first and treat it as diagnosis — it tells you a selector will never appear because the page is challenged, which is otherwise indistinguishable from a slow load. `solve` SPENDS the user's money on a third-party solving service per attempt, so only use it when they have asked you to get through a specific blocked page, and tell them it is being used. A cleared challenge is not a guarantee: these systems also score the session server-side.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: action
params.description: Default detect.

params.name: max_attempts
params.description: Solve attempts, 1-5. Each one bills.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_capture_profile
tools.description: Save a live session's signed-in state into a saved login, so later sessions start already authenticated. Only works on a session the user owns. Confirm with the user before calling — this persists their live login for reuse.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: profile_id
params.description: Saved login to write into.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_check_access
tools.description: Check that Scrappy is connected AND that the user's API key carries the browser scopes this toolkit needs. Cheap and read-only. Call it first if any other browser tool reports a permission problem — the fix is re-minting the Scrappy key with browser scopes, not retrying.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_click
tools.description: Click by CSS selector or coordinates. `click_count: 2` double-clicks, which is how many data grids enter cell-edit mode. `button: 'right'` opens a context menu. Set `pierce` when a selector cannot find something you can plainly see — querySelector does not cross shadow roots, so controls inside web components are invisible without it. `hold_ms` turns it into a press-and-hold, the only way past a 'Press & Hold to confirm you are human' widget (which starts a timer on pointerdown, so an ordinary click always fails). Clearing that gesture is not the same as clearing the challenge — those systems also score the session server-side. NEVER type passwords, credit-card numbers, one-time codes, or any other credential — if a page asks for one, stop and tell the user to sign in themselves on the Browser page.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: ref
params.description: Node handle from scrappy_browser_read_page. PREFER THIS over selector — it targets the element Chrome's accessibility tree resolved, so the visible label is what matched. A stale ref means the page re-rendered: call read_page again, do not fall back to guessing a selector.

params.name: selector
params.description: CSS selector to click.

params.name: x
params.description: X coordinate, when there is no selector.

params.name: y
params.description: Y coordinate, when there is no selector.

params.name: button
params.description: Default left.

params.name: click_count
params.description: 2 to double-click.

params.name: pierce
params.description: Also search open shadow roots.

params.name: hold_ms
params.description: Press-and-hold duration in ms.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_cookies
tools.description: Read, set, or delete the session's cookies. `action: 'delete'` with no name clears ALL of them, which signs the session out of everything — including a saved login it was started from. Cookies ARE the credential: report what you find in terms of names and domains, never by echoing values, and never copy them anywhere outside this session.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: action
params.description: Default get.

params.name: cookies
params.description: For 'set': objects with name, value, domain, and optionally path/secure/httpOnly/sameSite/expires.

params.name: name
params.description: For 'delete': the cookie name.

params.name: domain
params.description: For 'delete': the cookie domain.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_create_profile
tools.description: Create an EMPTY saved-login slot. It holds no login until one is captured from a live session. You cannot perform that capture: the user must sign in themselves on the Browser page and save it. Use this only when the user has asked you to set up a new saved login for them.

params.name: label
params.description: Human label, e.g. 'LinkedIn — Sales Nav'.

params.name: site_hint
params.description: Which site it is for.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_create_session
tools.description: Start a cloud browser session. Pass `profile_id` to reuse one of the user's saved logins, which starts the browser ALREADY SIGNED IN to that site — this is the normal way to act on a user's behalf. SPENDS the user's Scrappy credits up front and then meters per minute for as long as it lives, so release it when done. Capped at ~10 concurrent sessions.

params.name: profile_id
params.description: Saved login to start from (`scrappy_browser_list_profiles`). Omit for a clean, signed-out browser.

params.name: title
params.description: Short label so the user can recognise it.

params.name: screen_width
params.description: Window width. Default 1280.

params.name: screen_height
params.description: Window height. Default 720.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_delete_profile
tools.description: PERMANENTLY delete a saved login and the encrypted credential it holds. This is the revocation path — use it when the user disconnects an account or suspects a saved session is compromised. Not recoverable. Always confirm first and say exactly which login will be removed.

params.name: profile_id
params.description: Saved login to delete.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_drag_drop
tools.description: Drag one element onto another — slider filters, sortable lists, drag-and-drop upload zones. Moves through intermediate points so drag libraries register the motion.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: source_ref
params.description: Node handle for the element to drag (scrappy_browser_read_page). Prefer over source_selector.

params.name: target_ref
params.description: Node handle for the drop target. Prefer over target_selector. Each end is addressed independently, so it is normal to pass a ref for one and a selector for the other — a drag usually has one end read off the page and the other a known container.

params.name: source_selector
params.description: Element to drag.

params.name: target_selector
params.description: Where to drop it.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_element_info
tools.description: Describe one element — whether it exists, is visible, its position, size, attributes and text. This is the tool for 'my click did nothing': it distinguishes a selector that matches nothing from one that matches something hidden, disabled, or covered by an overlay, which look identical from a click that reports success. PROVE A WRITE ACTUALLY CHANGED SOMETHING: the response carries `contentDigest`, `rowCount` and `descendantCount` for whatever the selector matches. Read the container (a list, a table body) BEFORE the action and again after — an unchanged digest is positive proof the action was a no-op, which 'a matching row exists' can never tell you, because the row may have been there all along. For a create specifically, prefer `rowCount`: a page with a ticking timestamp changes its digest every second while the count stays honest. FIND OUT WHY A CONTROL IS DISABLED instead of retrying it: when the element is disabled the response carries `gating` — `disabledVia` ('property' or 'aria'), `emptyFields`, `emptyRequiredFields`, `invalidFields` and `formValid`. Read `emptyFields` and fill what it names. Do NOT check `emptyRequiredFields` alone and conclude nothing is missing: a field the form insists on can be absent from it while `emptyFields` names the field actually blocking the button, which is the usual reason a submit stays greyed out with no visible error.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: ref
params.description: Node handle from scrappy_browser_read_page. PREFER THIS over selector — it targets the element Chrome's accessibility tree resolved, so the visible label is what matched. A stale ref means the page re-rendered: call read_page again, do not fall back to guessing a selector.

params.name: selector
params.description: CSS selector to describe.

params.name: pierce
params.description: Also search open shadow roots.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_evaluate
tools.description: Run a JavaScript expression in the page and return its result. The escape hatch when no other tool fits — computing a value from many elements, reading a framework's in-memory state, or driving a control that responds to nothing else. Prefer a purpose-built tool when one exists: they report failure meaningfully and this returns whatever the expression happened to evaluate to. NEVER use it to read passwords, cookies, tokens or card numbers out of a page, and never send such values anywhere — the user signed in here on the understanding that their credentials stay in the browser.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: expression
params.description: JavaScript expression to evaluate.

params.name: timeout
params.description: Milliseconds. Default ~10000.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_get_console
tools.description: Read the page's console messages, for diagnosing a page that silently failed. NOTE this DRAINS the buffer: it returns what has accumulated since the last call and clears it, so read it once right after the action you are investigating rather than polling.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_get_dom
tools.description: Fetch the page's DOM structure. Use when you need the real element tree to build a selector — `scrappy_browser_scrape` with format 'skeleton' is usually better and much smaller, so try that first.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_get_network
tools.description: Read the requests the page has made — the way to find the JSON endpoint behind a table and fetch it directly instead of scraping rendered HTML. DRAINS the buffer like `scrappy_browser_get_console`. Capture starts when a tab is first touched, so to catch a page LOAD call this once before navigating and again after, rather than only afterwards. To BLOCK requests rather than observe them, use `scrappy_browser_intercept`.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_history
tools.description: Go back, go forward, or reload. Back is not the same as navigating to the previous URL — it restores the page's own history entry, which matters after a form post or inside a single-page app. Reload keeps the current URL, which you may not know.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: action
params.description: Which one.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_hover
tools.description: Hover the pointer over an element. Navigation menus that reveal a submenu on hover, and tooltips carrying the data you want, never appear for a click — the submenu is not in the DOM until the pointer is over its parent.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: ref
params.description: Node handle from scrappy_browser_read_page. PREFER THIS over selector — it targets the element Chrome's accessibility tree resolved, so the visible label is what matched. A stale ref means the page re-rendered: call read_page again, do not fall back to guessing a selector.

params.name: selector
params.description: CSS selector to hover.

params.name: x
params.description: X coordinate, when there is no selector.

params.name: y
params.description: Y coordinate, when there is no selector.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_iframe
tools.description: Read or act on content INSIDE a same-origin iframe. Ordinary click/type/scrape cannot cross a frame boundary — a CSS selector stops at the document — so payment fields, consent walls and embedded third-party forms are invisible to every other tool here. Use `html`/`text` to read the frame, or `click`/`type` with a selector INSIDE it. NEVER type passwords, credit-card numbers, one-time codes, or any other credential — if a page asks for one, stop and tell the user to sign in themselves on the Browser page.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: frame_selector
params.description: CSS selector of the <iframe> itself.

params.name: action
params.description: What to do inside the frame.

params.name: selector
params.description: Selector INSIDE the frame, for click/type.

params.name: text
params.description: Text to type. Never a credential.

params.name: expression
params.description: JavaScript, for action 'evaluate'.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_intercept
tools.description: Block requests by resource type or URL pattern so pages load faster and scrapes use less bandwidth. `action: 'stop'` clears all blocking. For a general scraping run prefer `scrappy_browser_scrape_mode`, which does this and more.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: action
params.description: Default start.

params.name: resource_types
params.description: e.g. image, media, font, stylesheet, script.

params.name: url_patterns
params.description: URL glob patterns to block.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_keep_awake
tools.description: Hold a session open while nobody is watching it, or stop holding it. This is the tool for 'keep my session alive', 'do not let it time out' and 'persist this session' — `scrappy_browser_keepalive` only buys a single ~30-minute idle window and will NOT survive the user closing the tab. Sets a deadline up to 4 hours out that a cron refreshes; re-run it to extend from now. Every minute held awake meters against the user's Scrappy account whether or not anyone comes back, so the 4-hour cap is deliberate and there is no forever option — say so rather than promising one. Pass enabled: false to stop early. Upstream also reaps at 12 hours absolute no matter what.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: enabled
params.description: true to hold the session open, false to stop holding it.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_keepalive
tools.description: Mark a session as still in use without acting on the page. Rarely needed from the agent — any action already counts as activity. Use it only when a human is doing something in the viewer (reading, completing MFA) and the session would otherwise look idle. This buys ONE idle window (~30 minutes); to hold a session open while nobody is watching it, use `scrappy_browser_keep_awake` instead.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_list_profiles
tools.description: List the user's saved logins — sites they have already signed in to, which a session can start from to act as them. Stored cookies are never returned, only labels. Read-only and free. These belong to the user who captured them and cannot be used for anyone else.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_list_sessions
tools.description: List the user's live browser sessions plus any shared with the workspace, with each one's id, status and whether it was started from a saved login. Call this first — every other browser tool needs a session id. Read-only and free.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_list_tabs
tools.description: List the session's open tabs with the tab id every tab operation needs. Call this before `scrappy_browser_manage_tab` — the id is an internal target id that appears in no other response, so there is no other way to name a tab. Also the way to notice that a click opened a popup you did not expect.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_manage_tab
tools.description: Close a tab, or make one the active tab with `action: 'activate'`. Activating brings the tab to the front AND makes it the tab every later action lands on (click, type, evaluate, screenshot) until it is closed — so after looking something up in a second tab, activate the first one before continuing there. Web apps open tabs constantly — OAuth consent, payment windows, target=_blank links — and without this they accumulate and keep consuming session resources.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: tab_id
params.description: Tab to act on.

params.name: action
params.description: Default close.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_navigate
tools.description: Navigate a session to an http/https URL. Private and internal hosts are blocked. After navigating, prefer `scrappy_browser_wait_for_network` before reading a single-page app, which often renders before its data arrives.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: url
params.description: Absolute http(s) URL.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_open_tab
tools.description: Open a new blank tab and return its id. Useful to keep a long form intact while you look something up, instead of navigating away and losing the filled fields. The new tab is blank, so your actions keep landing on the form until you navigate it; when you are done there, activate the form's tab with scrappy_browser_manage_tab before continuing.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_press_key
tools.description: Press a key — 'Enter' to submit a search or form, 'Escape' to dismiss a modal, 'Tab' to move focus, 'ArrowDown'/'ArrowUp' to walk an autocomplete list. Many search boxes have no submit button at all and only respond to Enter, so this is often the only way to run a query. NEVER type passwords, credit-card numbers, one-time codes, or any other credential — if a page asks for one, stop and tell the user to sign in themselves on the Browser page.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: ref
params.description: Node handle from scrappy_browser_read_page. PREFER THIS over selector — it targets the element Chrome's accessibility tree resolved, so the visible label is what matched. A stale ref means the page re-rendered: call read_page again, do not fall back to guessing a selector.

params.name: key
params.description: Key name, e.g. Enter, Escape, Tab, ArrowDown, Backspace.

params.name: modifiers
params.description: Bitmask: 1 Alt, 2 Ctrl, 4 Meta/Cmd, 8 Shift. Add them together.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_read_page
tools.description: Read the page as a list of interactive elements — each with its role, its visible name, its state, and a `ref` to act on. START HERE before clicking or typing on any page you have not already read. Pass a returned `ref` to click, type, hover, press_key, select_option, scroll, drag_drop or element_info instead of writing a CSS selector. This is Chrome's own accessibility computation, so the name a node comes back with is the one a person reads off the screen — aria-label, label[for], alt text and content are already folded in, none of which a selector can see. Guessing a selector from a screenshot is how a form gets filled wrong in a way that reports success: typing a person's NAME into the field that wanted their record id looks identical to a correct type. Reading the page first removes the guess. Refs are invalidated by anything that re-renders the page. If one comes back stale, call this again for fresh refs — do not fall back to inventing a selector.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: tab
params.description: Tab id, when the session has more than one.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_release_session
tools.description: Close a browser session, freeing capacity and STOPPING the per-minute meter. Always do this when finished — an abandoned session bills until it is reaped 30 minutes later.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_render_pdf
tools.description: Render the current page to a PDF, returned base64-encoded. Use for archiving a receipt, invoice, or report exactly as it appears.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_resolve_download
tools.description: Resolve the real file URL behind a link or button — CSV exports, PDFs, attachments — so it can be fetched directly instead of driving a download dialog.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: selector
params.description: The link or button to resolve.

params.name: timeout
params.description: Milliseconds to wait.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_scrape
tools.description: Read the current page. TRY `structured` FIRST — when a site publishes JSON-LD, microdata, OpenGraph or embedded framework state, reading its own data beats inferring it from markup. `markdown` strips boilerplate to the main content; `skeleton` collapses repeated components to one exemplar plus the CSS selector matching all of them (ideal for finding the selector to loop over); `text` and `html` are raw. All formats run server-side over the RENDERED DOM, so they see post-JavaScript state.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: format
params.description: Output shape. Default markdown.

params.name: selector
params.description: Limit to a subtree.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_scrape_mode
tools.description: Render pages for extraction instead of for humans: blocks images/media/fonts/trackers, removes cookie and consent walls, unsticks fixed headers that swallow clicks, finishes animations that stop waits settling, promotes lazy-loaded data-src images, and pauses media. By default it applies to the CURRENT page only; pass persist: true to keep it across navigations for a multi-page run. Call it before a scraping run — and TURN IT OFF again (action: off) as soon as you are done reading. A cloud browser session is SHARED with the human: leave this on and every page they open afterwards renders with no images and no fonts, looking broken, with nothing on screen explaining why.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: action
params.description: Turn extraction rendering on or off. Defaults to on when neither this nor `enabled` is given.

params.name: enabled
params.description: Alias for `action`. Prefer `action`; passing both is an error if they disagree.

params.name: persist
params.description: Apply to every later navigation in this session too. Default FALSE — the human shares this browser, and a persistent setting leaves every page they open afterwards stripped of images and fonts. Set true only for a multi-page scraping run, and turn it off (action: off) when you finish.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_screenshot
tools.description: Capture the page as a base64 image. Use when you need to SEE layout — for reading text or data, `scrappy_browser_scrape` is far cheaper and more accurate. Rate-limited to 30/min.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: full_page
params.description: Capture the whole scrollable page.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page — to an element, by a pixel offset, or straight to 'top'/'bottom'. Needed for infinite-scroll lists and anything lazy-loaded: content below the fold often has not been fetched at all yet, so scraping without scrolling returns a short list and looks like the real answer.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: ref
params.description: Node handle from scrappy_browser_read_page. PREFER THIS over selector — it targets the element Chrome's accessibility tree resolved, so the visible label is what matched. A stale ref means the page re-rendered: call read_page again, do not fall back to guessing a selector.

params.name: selector
params.description: Scroll this element into view.

params.name: x
params.description: Horizontal offset, with `y`.

params.name: y
params.description: Vertical offset in pixels.

params.name: position
params.description: Jump to an end.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_select_option
tools.description: Choose an option in a native <select> dropdown. Do NOT try to click one: the list a native select opens is drawn by the operating system, not the page, so there is no element to click and the click silently does nothing. Pass `values` for a multi-select.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: ref
params.description: Node handle from scrappy_browser_read_page. PREFER THIS over selector — it targets the element Chrome's accessibility tree resolved, so the visible label is what matched. A stale ref means the page re-rendered: call read_page again, do not fall back to guessing a selector.

params.name: selector
params.description: CSS selector of the <select>.

params.name: value
params.description: The option's value attribute.

params.name: values
params.description: Several values, for a multi-select.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_session_context
tools.description: Report how this session appears to sites: proxy, exit IP, timezone and the OS it presents. Use when a site is blocking or challenging the session — a browser clock that disagrees with its own IP's region reads as automation no matter how ordinary the rest looks.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_set_checkbox
tools.description: Tick or untick a checkbox or radio button. Prefer this over clicking one: a click TOGGLES, so if you are unsure of the current state — or you retry after an ambiguous failure — clicking flips it back. This sets the state you asked for and is safe to repeat.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: selector
params.description: CSS selector of the checkbox or radio.

params.name: checked
params.description: true to tick, false to untick.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_set_viewport
tools.description: Resize the page viewport, optionally emulating a mobile device. Use when a site serves a different layout by width — a responsive table that collapses to cards, or a mobile site that exposes data the desktop one hides behind a menu.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: width
params.description: Viewport width in pixels.

params.name: height
params.description: Viewport height in pixels.

params.name: device_scale_factor
params.description: Pixel density, e.g. 2 for retina.

params.name: mobile
params.description: Emulate a mobile device (touch, meta viewport).

tools.name: scrappy_browser_sleep_session
tools.description: Snapshot the session's signed-in state and open tabs, then shut the browser down — which STOPS the per-minute meter while keeping the login. Returns a snapshot id for `scrappy_browser_wake_session`. This is the right way to pause work that resumes later: keepalive keeps paying, and releasing throws the state away.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_storage
tools.description: Read, set, or delete localStorage / sessionStorage entries for the current page. Many single-page apps keep their auth token here, so the same rule as cookies applies: never echo a value that looks like a credential and never copy one out of the session. `action: 'delete'` with no key clears the whole store.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: action
params.description: Default get.

params.name: type
params.description: Which store. Default local.

params.name: key
params.description: Entry key. Omit on get to read everything.

params.name: value
params.description: For 'set'.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_suppress_dialogs
tools.description: Replace alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload with no-ops on the current page. Call this BEFORE any click that might open one: an open dialog blocks its tab, so a Save or Delete that fires confirm() makes every later command on that tab time out with no way to answer it. Per-document — re-apply after each navigation.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_type
tools.description: Type text into an input. NEVER type passwords, credit-card numbers, one-time codes, or any other credential — if a page asks for one, stop and tell the user to sign in themselves on the Browser page.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: ref
params.description: Node handle from scrappy_browser_read_page. PREFER THIS over selector — it targets the element Chrome's accessibility tree resolved, so the visible label is what matched. A stale ref means the page re-rendered: call read_page again, do not fall back to guessing a selector.

params.name: selector
params.description: CSS selector of the input.

params.name: text
params.description: Text to type. Never a credential.

params.name: clear
params.description: Clear the field first.

params.name: pierce
params.description: Also search open shadow roots.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_upload_file
tools.description: Attach a file to a file input. Give either `content` (base64, ~7MB ceiling from the request body limit) or `source_url` (fetched by Scrappy itself, up to 20MB — use this for real documents). `source_url` is SSRF-checked like navigate.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: selector
params.description: CSS selector of the file input.

params.name: content

params.name: source_url
params.description: Public URL for Scrappy to fetch.

params.name: file_name
params.description: Filename to present to the page.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_wait_for_network
tools.description: Block until the page stops issuing requests. Essential for single-page apps that render their shell before the data arrives — scraping too early returns an empty skeleton. Polls server-side (one request, not dozens). Returns idle:false on timeout rather than failing.

params.name: session_id
params.description: Kavanah browser session id, from `scrappy_browser_list_sessions`.

params.name: timeout
params.description: Milliseconds.

tools.name: scrappy_browser_wait_for_selector
tools.description: Block until an element is visible (default), present, hidden, or detached. Returns found:false on timeout rather than failing.

params.name: session_id

params.name: selector

params.name: state

params.name: timeout

params.name: pierce

params.name: snapshot_id
params.description: From `scrappy_browser_sleep_session`.

params.name: screen_width

params.name: screen_height

params.name: lead_ids
params.description: Lead ids to validate (1-1000).

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Search Apollo.io for companies — issuers, funds, broker-dealers — by employee count, revenue, funding, industry keywords and location. Uses the CALLER'S OWN Apollo key (Settings → Integrations; organization search is on paid Apollo plans only). COSTS ONE APOLLO CREDIT PER PAGE, whatever the page holds, so use per_page up to 100 and narrow filters rather than paging. What Apollo CANNOT do, and you must not claim it did: it has no filter for funding STAGE (Series C, pre-IPO) and no knowledge of a raise IN PROGRESS. For 'later-stage companies raising $100M+', the closest honest proxy is latest_funding_min_dollars=100000000 (the LATEST COMPLETED round was $100M or more) plus exclude_public=true (drops companies Apollo lists with a stock ticker — applied after the page is fetched, so it does not save the credit). Say that it is a proxy. Results are not saved; add the ones worth keeping with add_firm_from_search.

params.name: name
params.description: Company name (partial matches).

params.name: keywords
params.description: Industry keyword tags, e.g. ['fintech','defense'].

params.name: locations
params.description: Headquarters city, state or country.

params.name: latest_funding_min_dollars
params.description: Size of the latest COMPLETED round, in dollars.

params.name: latest_funding_after
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD — latest round on or after.

params.name: latest_funding_before
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD.

params.name: exclude_public
params.description: Drop companies with a public stock ticker (after fetching).

params.name: page
params.description: 1-based. Each page costs a credit.

params.name: per_page
params.description: 1-100, default 25. Same cost per page either way.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search Kavanah's official documentation (the /docs site: getting started, core features, dev & AI, integrations, and the full API reference) plus the Help Center FAQs. Returns the best-matching pages with excerpts and matching FAQs with their full answers. Use for conceptual and capability questions — 'how does the client portal work?', 'does Kavanah have an API for tasks?', 'what do automations do?', 'how is my data secured?' — anything answered by product documentation rather than workspace data. For WHERE a feature lives in the UI use find_ui_feature; for KVN methodology coaching use the course tools; for the user's own uploaded files use the knowledge-base tools.

params.name: query
params.description: What to look up, in free text — e.g. 'client portal permissions', 'tasks API create endpoint', 'time tracking reports', 'desktop app offline'.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return (1–15). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: search_engineering_notes
tools.description: Search Kavanah's internal engineering notes (docs/agent-notes/) — architecture decisions, invariants, gotchas, and the reasoning behind how subsystems were built. Use for questions about how Kavanah is IMPLEMENTED ('why does undo use a group id?', 'how does the KVN gate avoid rate limits?', 'what breaks if I add a task-creating tool?'). This is internal engineering context, NOT product documentation: for how to USE a feature, call search_docs instead. Returns the best-matching notes with the section each hit falls under; follow up with read_engineering_note for the full text.

params.name: query
params.description: What to look for, in free text — e.g. 'undo staleness guard', 'why is the charter cache 60s', 'safe mode tool stripping', 'gmail list vs detail format'.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max notes to return (1–10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: search_google
tools.description: Run a Google search and get the ranked result list back verbatim — titles, URLs, snippets, plus the answer box / knowledge panel when Google shows one. Use this instead of `web_search` when you need the RESULTS themselves rather than a written answer: finding a specific page, comparing what several sources say, checking who ranks for a term, or gathering URLs to then open with `read_web_page`. Read-only; it never changes workspace data.

params.name: query
params.description: The Google query. Google operators work (site:, filetype:, quoted phrases, -exclusions).

params.name: recency
params.description: Optional: only return results published within this window. Omit for no time filter.

params.name: num

params.name: country

tools.name: search_knowledge_documents
tools.description: Full-text search over knowledge documents (title AND body). Returns id + title + icon + a snippet around the match. Use to find a specific document to open, comment on, edit, or link; to answer a QUESTION from workspace knowledge prefer ask_knowledge_base.

params.name: limit
params.description: 1..50, default 12

tools.name: search_prospects
tools.description: Search millions of professional profiles for people matching a role, firm, sector or location — the discovery step for building an investor, issuer or partner list. FREE: this costs nothing and does not reveal email addresses. Results carry a record id you pass to unlock_prospect_email when you have decided who is worth paying for. Use this to build and rank a candidate list BEFORE spending anything.

params.name: query
params.description: Free text, e.g. 'family office defense tech'.

params.name: titles

params.name: page

params.name: limit

tools.name: search_tasks
tools.description: Search for tasks by keyword in title or description. Can also filter by project, status, assignee, priority, tag, or created/updated time (never infer recency from ids).

params.name: keyword

params.name: project_ref

params.name: status

params.name: assigned_to

params.name: priority

params.name: tag

params.name: created_after

params.name: updated_after
params.description: Updated at/after; same format

params.name: include_archived

params.name: limit
