params.name: cursor
params.description: Continue a search: pass the cursor the last call reported. When more pages exist the tool says so — keep paging before calling a list complete.

tools.name: send_progress_report
tools.description: Compose and deliver a project / team progress report to specific people via Kavanah's internal inbox AND/OR email — in a single call. Provide your own markdown `body` (preferred — you already know what to say), or omit it to auto-build one from this week's stats for the given project. Routing: `member_names` are workspace teammates (delivered as a Kavanah chat DM); `emails` are raw addresses (delivered via the user's connected email provider — Gmail bridge → native Gmail → AngelSend gateway, in that order). Set `channels` to control delivery: ['inbox'] = chat only, ['email'] = email only, ['inbox','email'] (default) = send to BOTH channels for member_names (DM + their email on file) and email for `emails`. Use this instead of chaining `post_chat_message` + `gmail_send_email` per recipient.

params.name: title
params.description: Short report title used as the email subject and the first line of the DM (e.g. 'Weekly status — Website Redesign').

params.name: body
params.description: Markdown body of the report. Omit to have the tool auto-generate one from this week's task stats for `project_ref`.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project reference scoping the auto-generated body and (when set) the subject. Optional.

params.name: member_names
params.description: Display names of workspace members to receive the report. Each member is matched against `assigned_to` / member directory (case-insensitive). Unknown names are reported back and skipped.

params.name: emails
params.description: Raw email addresses (clients, contractors, etc.) to receive the report via email.

params.name: cc
params.description: Optional CC list for the email channel.

params.name: channels
params.description: Which delivery channels to use. Defaults to ['inbox','email']. For workspace members on a both-channels send, the inbox DM is the source of truth and the email is a copy.

params.name: provider
params.description: Email provider for the email channel. Defaults to 'auto' (Gmail bridge → native Gmail → AngelSend gateway).

params.name: is_html
params.description: Treat `body` as HTML for the email channel. Defaults to false (plain markdown is sent as text).

tools.name: set_agent_token_limits
tools.description: Raise (or lower) how many AI-agent tokens each workspace member may use: the daily limit behind "You've reached today's agent limit", plus the hourly and per-minute burst caps. Admin-only. The limits apply to EVERY member of the workspace, not only the person asking, and take effect on the next message. Values below the floors (5,000,000 daily, 3,000,000 hourly, 1,000,000 per minute) are refused, because they would be ignored. Usage counts input, output and cache writes in full and cache reads at 10%, and the daily count resets at 00:00 UTC. Tell the user the new numbers and that the change affects everyone; they can also change it themselves in Settings → AI Agent.

params.name: max_tokens_per_user_per_day
params.description: New daily limit per member. Whole number, 5,000,000 to 2,147,483,647.

params.name: max_tokens_per_user_per_hour
params.description: New hourly burst limit per member. At least 3,000,000, and no more than the daily limit.

params.name: max_tokens_per_user_per_minute
params.description: New per-minute burst limit per member. At least 1,000,000, and no more than the hourly limit.

tools.name: set_client_health

tools.name: set_contact_runway_threshold

tools.name: set_custom_field

tools.name: set_deal_investment_profile
tools.description: Record what a deal IS, as read from its data-room materials, so investors can be ranked against it. Read the deal's data room first — get_deal_space lists its Drive folder, drive_read_file reads each document — this tool stores your reading, it does not do it for you. `themes` is the highest-value field: short phrases in the issuer's own language ("grid-scale storage", "nurse staffing"), because a firm's thesis is prose and prose matches on themes rather than on a taxonomy. Storing the profile makes the ranking REPRODUCIBLE: extraction happens once here, and every later ranking is arithmetic over it, so the same deal yields the same order and the next tranche is a stable cursor rather than a fresh opinion. Re-run it when the data room materially changes.

params.name: themes
params.description: Short phrases from the materials describing what this issuance is about. 3-8 is typical.

params.name: sectors
params.description: Sector tags. Falls back to the deal's own sector field when omitted.

params.name: stages

params.name: min_check_dollars
params.description: Smallest position the issuer will accept, if the materials state one.

params.name: summary
params.description: A few sentences an analyst could act on.

params.name: source_files
params.description: The Drive files this reading came from, so the profile can be audited against its sources.

tools.name: set_deal_sheet_mirror
tools.description: Turn the outbound mirror on or off for a pipeline's sheet link, and optionally rename the mirror tab. While enabled, Kavanah writes the pipeline out to that separate tab on every sync AND hourly in the background. The mirror tab may never be the source tab — that would overwrite the team's real data, and is rejected.

params.name: pipeline

params.name: enabled
params.description: True to arm the mirror, false to disable it.

params.name: mirror_tab_name
params.description: Optional tab to mirror into (default 'Kavanah Sync'). Must differ from the source tab.

tools.name: set_document_parent

The move is validated server-side: the parent must exist in this workspace, must not be a template, and the move must not create a circular hierarchy (a page can't become its own ancestor) — an invalid move returns an error and changes nothing.

params.name: document_id
params.description: Id of the document to move.

params.name: parent_id
params.description: Id of the new parent document, or null to move the document to the top level (root).

tools.name: set_energy_level

params.description: The energy level to set: 'deep', 'steady', or 'shallow'.

tools.name: set_entity_properties

tools.name: set_field_permission
tools.description: Set a field-level permission for a role: whether that role can view and/or edit a specific field of a resource. This changes what members with that role can see or change. Requires workspace owner/admin.

params.name: resource

params.name: field_name
params.description: Name of the field the rule governs.

params.name: can_view
params.description: Whether the role can view the field. Defaults to true.

params.name: can_edit
params.description: Whether the role can edit the field. Defaults to false.

tools.name: set_manager_agreement
tools.description: Create or update the caller's own Manager Mode agreement. ONLY the fields you pass are changed; everything else keeps its current value. Set enabled=true to have Kavanah start managing them (this is the opt-in — nothing happens until it is true). Use this when the user says something like 'be my manager', 'hold me accountable', 'check in on me daily', or asks to change their working hours or check-in time. Affects only the current user.

params.description: Turn Manager Mode on or off for the caller. Off means no check-ins are generated and no points are awarded.

params.name: style

params.name: objectives

params.name: work_days

params.name: day_end_hour

params.name: confidence

params.name: max_open_commitments

params.name: checkin_frequency
params.description: How often the manager checks in. Default 'weekdays'.

params.name: checkin_hour

params.name: checkin_day_of_week

params.name: timezone

tools.name: set_member_capacity

tools.name: set_member_profile

Resume upload is UI-only (People page member modal) — this tool cannot attach a resume.

params.name: experience_summary

tools.name: set_my_notepad

To edit a SPECIFIC note or add a new one, prefer create_my_note / update_my_note. Affects only the current user's personal data.

params.name: body

tools.name: set_network_sheet_mirror
tools.description: Turn the network mirror on or off, or rename its tab. The mirror refuses any tab a Kavanah sync reads from (this link's source tab or any other linked tab in the same file, ignoring case and spacing). Default mirror tab: 'Kavanah Network'.

params.name: mirror_tab_name

tools.name: set_north_star
tools.description: Set or update the North Star for the workspace or a project: the metric, how it is measured, the direction, the target and the date to hit it by. Advisory, never enforced — it does not refuse anything, it gives people and you a shared way to say whether work moves the company. Provide any subset of fields; omitted ones are unchanged. Admin-only at the API layer for the workspace scope. Setting one on a project overrides the inherited company metric for that project's work.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project to set it on. Omit to set the company-wide North Star.

params.name: metric
params.description: The metric's name, e.g. 'Weekly active teams'. Naming it is what creates the North Star.

params.name: definition
params.description: How it is measured / what counts. The half that stops two people reading the same name differently.

params.name: unit
params.description: Unit shown next to the number, e.g. '%', 'teams', '$'.

params.name: direction
params.description: Which way is good. Default 'increase'.

params.name: baseline
params.description: Where the metric stood when this was set. Powers the progress reading.

params.name: target
params.description: The number being aimed at.

params.name: horizon
params.description: Date to hit the target by, as YYYY-MM-DD.

params.name: source
params.description: Where the current value comes from. 'manual' means somebody records it with record_north_star_value. The task sources are measured automatically once a day from this workspace's own task data. 'deal_weighted_pipeline' (every open deal's value times its probability, falling back to its stage's default and then to zero) and 'deal_forecast_revenue' (the Deal Room revenue forecast's expected FEE, not deal size) are measured the same way from the Deal Room, in whole currency units — both are company-wide, so neither can be set with project_ref, and forecast revenue is unavailable while the workspace reports fee bands separately.

params.name: clear
params.description: Set true to REMOVE the North Star at this scope. A project reverts to inheriting the company's.

tools.name: set_notification_priority
tools.description: Set a notification's priority for the current user. Use 'action_needed' for items requiring follow-up, 'fyi' for informational items, or null to clear.

params.name: priority
params.description: action_needed | fyi | null (string 'null' clears).

tools.name: set_outbound_daily_cap
tools.description: Set the outbound daily cap for one mailbox, or the workspace default. ARMS higher unattended sending: the scheduled-email cron defers against this number every minute, so raising it immediately releases more mail. Admin-only, and it spends a shared, not individually recoverable, resource — the sending domain's reputation. Prefer adding a warm-up ramp (warmup_start + warmup_floor + warmup_step) over a straight raise on any identity that has not been sending at the new volume already: a domain that jumps to its cap on day one gets filtered, and the fix for that is a new domain, not a smaller number next week. Call plan_outbound_capacity first and repeat what it says about the provider ceiling.

params.name: daily_cap
params.description: Messages per day once any ramp completes.

params.name: user_id
params.description: The mailbox owner. Omit to set the WORKSPACE DEFAULT, which every mailbox without its own row inherits.

params.name: warmup_start
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD the ramp begins. Null clears the ramp, which sends at daily_cap immediately.

params.name: warmup_floor
params.description: Day-one ceiling. Default 50.

params.name: warmup_step
params.description: Added per day until daily_cap. Default 25.

tools.name: set_partner_status
tools.description: Record where a broker-dealer partnership stands: prospect, contacted, agreed, active, paused or declined. This is the gate on supply/demand matching — ONLY firms at 'agreed' or 'active' are matched against live deals and alerted on. A firm merely tagged broker_dealer is one we know of; mailing them a deal is cold outreach, which is a different act needing different consent. Set 'declined' rather than deleting, so we stop re-asking someone who already said no.

params.name: supply_offered
params.description: What they BRING us — retail distribution, family-office LPs, syndication capacity. Their demand (what they want) is the firm's sectors, stages, geographies and check size.

params.name: mandate_notes
params.description: Anything about their mandate that does not fit the structured fields.

tools.name: set_project_budget
tools.description: Create or update a project's planned budget (labor, external, total) and ROI projection. Upsert-style.

tools.name: set_project_department
tools.description: Link (or unlink) a whole project to a department. Pass project_ref and either a department to link, or empty to unlink. Independent of per-task department routing.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project ref (e.g. "1", "website-redesign")

params.name: department_id
params.description: Department UUID, or empty string to unlink

params.name: department_name
params.description: Department name (alternative to department_id)

tools.name: set_project_key_prefix
tools.description: Rename a project's issue-key prefix. Must be 2-10 uppercase letters/digits starting with a letter (e.g. ACME, FOO2).

params.name: key_prefix
params.description: 2-10 chars, uppercase, leading letter, A-Z/0-9 only.

tools.name: set_project_kvn
tools.description: Update one or more axes of a project's KVN charter. Provide any subset of know_how/vision/negation. Admin-only at the API layer.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project to update.

params.name: know_how
params.description: Replacement Know-how text. Omit to leave unchanged.

params.name: vision
params.description: Replacement Vision text. Omit to leave unchanged.

params.name: negation
params.description: Replacement Negation text. Omit to leave unchanged.

tools.name: set_project_outcome_target
tools.description: Tag a project with the customer-outcome it is meant to move (e.g. 'reduce support resolution time', 'lift ARR per seat', 'raise NPS'). Set while the project is active. Feeds the project-to-outcome conversion operating metric (course 6.4) once a result is later recorded with record_project_outcome.

params.name: outcome_target
params.description: The customer-side outcome this project is committed to moving.

tools.name: set_project_permission_override
tools.description: Set a per-project role override for a member: within one project they act with a different role than their workspace-wide one. This changes what the member can access in that project. Requires workspace owner/admin.

params.name: user_id
params.description: Member user id (UUID).

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project reference/id the override applies to.

params.name: role_id
params.description: Id (UUID) of the role to apply within that project.

tools.name: set_project_visibility
tools.description: Restrict a project's visibility to specific roles and/or teams. This changes who can see the project at all. Passing empty lists makes it visible to everyone again. Requires workspace owner/admin.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project reference/id to restrict.

params.name: allowed_role_ids
params.description: Role ids (UUIDs) allowed to see the project. Empty = no role restriction.

params.name: allowed_team_ids
params.description: Team ids allowed to see the project. Empty = no team restriction.

tools.name: set_recurring
tools.description: Configure a task to recur on a schedule. Sets up recurrence metadata on the task.

params.name: task_id
params.description: The task ID

params.name: frequency
params.description: How often the task repeats

params.name: interval
params.description: Repeat every N periods (default 1)

params.name: days_of_week
params.description: For weekly: days of week (0=Sun, 1=Mon, ..., 6=Sat)

params.name: end_date
params.description: Optional end date in YYYY-MM-DD format

tools.name: set_reminder
tools.description: Set or update a reminder on a task. Accepts a whole-day reminder or a specific time of day.

params.name: task_id
params.description: The task ID

params.name: reminder_date
params.description: When to fire. Accepts YYYY-MM-DD (whole-day) or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM (24-hour, specific time of day).

tools.name: set_request_field_visibility
tools.description: Set or clear the conditional show/hide rule on a single field of a request-intake page. With a rule, the target field only appears when the controlling field's answer matches. Pass clear=true (or omit op) to remove the rule and make the field always visible. The controlling field (when) must be another existing field on the same page.

params.name: request_page_id
params.description: Id of the request-intake page.

params.name: field_key
params.description: Key of the field whose visibility rule is being set/cleared.

params.name: when
params.description: Field key of the controlling field whose answer the rule reads. Required unless clearing.

params.name: op
params.description: Comparison operator. eq/neq/contains compare against `value`; empty/not_empty are presence checks (value ignored). Omit to clear the rule.

params.name: value
params.description: Operand the controlling answer is compared against for eq/neq/contains. Ignored for empty/not_empty.

params.name: clear
params.description: Set true to remove any existing visibility rule (field becomes always visible).

tools.name: set_task_access
tools.description: Set exactly who can see/edit a restricted task (replaces the current member list). Each member is an email + role (viewer = read-only, editor = can edit). Restricts the task if it wasn't already; pass restricted=false to also lift the restriction. Members must be active workspace users.

params.name: task_id
params.description: The task ID

params.name: members
params.description: The full desired member list (replace semantics).

params.name: restricted
params.description: Defaults true. Pass false to remove the restriction entirely.

tools.name: set_task_department
tools.description: Route a task to a department (the team queue that owns it). Pass null/empty department to clear. Does not change the per-person assignee.

params.name: task_id
params.description: The task id

params.name: department_id
params.description: Department UUID, or empty string to clear

params.name: department_name
params.description: Department name (alternative to department_id)

tools.name: set_task_estimate
tools.description: Set estimated_hours and/or story_points on a task.

tools.name: set_task_kvn
tools.description: Set or update the KVN axes on a single task. Provide any subset of know_how/vision/negation; omitted axes are unchanged. Use when delegating: every task should ideally have all three so the doer has unambiguous intent.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Task to update.

params.name: know_how
params.description: What the doer needs to know / use / verify. Omit to leave unchanged.

params.name: vision
params.description: End-state for this task in 1–2 sentences. Omit to leave unchanged.

params.name: negation
params.description: Hard nos for this task. Omit to leave unchanged.

params.name: north_star_contribution
params.description: One sentence naming how this task moves the North Star it inherits. Omit to leave unchanged; pass an empty string to clear it.

tools.name: set_task_location
tools.description: Pin a task to a geographic location for the Map view. Provide either explicit coordinates (lat AND lng) or a free-text address — when only an address is given it is forward-geocoded to coordinates via OpenStreetMap. The address label is stored alongside the coordinates. Replaces any existing pin on the task.

params.name: task_id
params.description: The numeric id of the task to locate.

params.name: address
params.description: Free-text address or place name. Required when lat/lng are not supplied (it will be geocoded). When coordinates are supplied this is used as the display label.

params.name: lat
params.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90..90). Provide together with lng to skip geocoding.

params.name: lng
params.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180..180). Provide together with lat to skip geocoding.

tools.name: set_task_projects
tools.description: Replace the full set of projects a task belongs to in one call. Specify primary_ref to control which project is primary (defaults to the first ref).

params.name: project_refs
params.description: Full list of project refs the task should belong to

params.name: primary_ref
params.description: Which ref is primary (must be in project_refs)

tools.name: set_task_restriction
tools.description: Restrict a single task so only workspace admins and its access members can see it — even people who can see its project — or lift the restriction. Use set_task_access to choose the members. When a non-admin restricts a task they are kept on it as an editor.

params.name: task_id
params.description: The task ID

params.name: restricted
params.description: true (default) to restrict the task; false to lift the restriction

tools.name: set_team_skills_context
tools.description: Replace the workspace-level team skills/experience context used for assignment decisions. Admin-facing workspace setting — keep it a concise brief (who owns what, ramp-up notes, routing conventions), max 8000 chars.

params.name: context
params.description: The full replacement context text. Empty string clears it.

tools.name: set_workspace_kvn
tools.description: Update one or more axes of the company's KVN charter. Admin-only at the API layer; non-admins will get a permission error. Provide any subset of know_how/vision/negation; omitted axes are unchanged.

params.name: know_how
params.description: Replacement Know-how text. Omit to leave unchanged.

params.name: vision
params.description: Replacement Vision text. Omit to leave unchanged.

params.name: negation
params.description: Replacement Negation text. Omit to leave unchanged.

tools.name: skip_detected_activity
tools.description: Skip (dismiss) one of the caller's own pending detected activities so it no longer appears in their review queue. Only the current user's own detected activities can be skipped.

params.name: activity_id
params.description: Id of the detected activity to skip (from list_detected_activities).

tools.name: slack_channel_history
tools.description: Read recent messages from a Slack channel the connected bot is a member of (Slack returns `not_in_channel` otherwise — the user must `/invite` the bot first). Returns newest-first message text with sender ids and thread markers. Use `slack_list_channels` to find the channel id, and pass the team_id it lists for a channel outside the default workspace.

params.name: channel
params.description: Channel id (e.g. C0123ABCD). Ids are safer than names here — Slack's history API does not resolve #names.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max messages to return. Default 20, capped at 100.

params.name: oldest_ts
params.description: Optional Slack message timestamp (e.g. 1712345678.000100); only messages newer than this are returned.

params.name: team_id
params.description: Optional Slack workspace id (T…) to act in, from slack_list_workspaces. Omit to use the default workspace (the one connected most recently). Also names the workspace inside an Enterprise Grid org-wide install.

tools.name: slack_create_channel
tools.description: Create a Slack channel through the connected bot and optionally invite workspace members to it by email. The name is normalized to Slack's rules (lowercase, dashes). Requires the Slack app to have the channels:manage scope (plus groups:write for private channels and users:read.email for email invites) — if Slack answers missing_scope, the user must re-install the Slack app with those scopes from its admin console; retrying will not help. The bot itself becomes a member automatically. For an Enterprise Grid org-wide install the workspace must be named with team_id; the tool lists the choices if it is missing.

params.name: name
params.description: Channel name or human title (e.g. 'Deal — Acme Series B'). Normalized to Slack's charset automatically; the created name is echoed back.

params.name: is_private
params.description: Create as a private channel. Default false (public).

params.name: invite_emails
params.description: Optional email addresses of Slack workspace members to invite. Each is resolved via Slack's directory; addresses with no Slack account in that workspace are reported back, not silently dropped.

params.name: team_id
params.description: Optional Slack workspace id (T…) to act in, from slack_list_workspaces. Omit to use the default workspace (the one connected most recently). Also names the workspace inside an Enterprise Grid org-wide install.

tools.name: slack_create_manager
tools.description: Put an AI employee in Slack to answer non-members (interns, students, a community) who @mention the Kavanah bot in its channels or DM it; it escalates what it can't answer. In Slack it has NO tools and NONE of this workspace's data — only its instructions and the playbook, its ONLY source of program facts: write it from what the user tells you, never invent a date, deadline or contact. YOU own it: it posts through your Slack connection and bills your credits. The result lists what still blocks it (e.g. a channel the bot must be invited to) — relay only that. Created OFF unless enabled — confirm first. No digital twins. Owners/admins only.

params.name: persona_id
params.description: AI employee id.

params.name: persona_name
params.description: Or its exact name.

params.name: team_id
params.description: Slack workspace id (T…). Default: your default Slack workspace.

params.name: channels
params.description: Channel ids or #names it answers @mentions in.

params.name: answer_all_channels
params.description: Answer in every channel the bot is in.

params.name: answer_dms
params.description: Answer direct messages to the bot.

params.name: playbook
params.description: The program facts it may state (max 30,000 chars).

params.name: escalate_to
params.description: Members (id, email or name) alerted on escalation. Default: the owner.

params.name: per_person_hourly_limit
params.description: Answers per person per hour (1–100, default 10).

params.name: hourly_reply_cap
params.description: Answers per hour overall (1–5000, default 200).

params.name: enabled
params.description: Answering on. Spends credits — only after the user says yes.

tools.name: slack_delete_manager
tools.description: Remove an AI Slack manager and its reply history; the AI employee is kept. To pause instead, update enabled false. Owners/admins only.

params.name: manager_id
params.description: From slack_list_managers.

tools.name: slack_invite_to_channel
tools.description: Invite Slack workspace members (by email) to an existing channel the connected bot is a member of. Requires the channels:manage (or groups:write for private channels) and users:read.email bot scopes. Use slack_list_channels to find the channel id first.

params.name: channel
params.description: Channel id (e.g. C0123ABCD).

params.name: emails
params.description: Email addresses of the Slack workspace members to invite.

params.name: team_id
params.description: Optional Slack workspace id (T…) to act in, from slack_list_workspaces. Omit to use the default workspace (the one connected most recently). Also names the workspace inside an Enterprise Grid org-wide install.

tools.name: slack_list_channels
tools.description: List Slack channels the connected bot can see (public + private channels the bot has been invited to). Returns channel id, name, visibility, and member count. Use this to find a channel id before posting with `slack_post_message`. Without team_id, channels from every connected Slack workspace are listed, each labelled with its workspace.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max channels to return. Default 50, capped at 200.

params.name: team_id
params.description: Optional Slack workspace id (T…) to act in, from slack_list_workspaces. Omit to use the default workspace (the one connected most recently). Also names the workspace inside an Enterprise Grid org-wide install.

tools.name: slack_list_managers
tools.description: List the workspace's AI Slack managers: employee, channels, DMs, on/off, owner (who pays), limits, last 7 days. Pass manager_id for one in full, with its playbook. Owners/admins only.

params.name: manager_id
params.description: From slack_list_managers.

tools.name: slack_list_workspaces
tools.description: List the Slack workspaces the user has connected to Kavanah — each one's name and team_id, and which is the default (the most recently connected, used when a Slack tool is not given a team_id). An Enterprise Grid org-wide install is listed with the workspaces inside it. Call this before acting in a workspace other than the default.

tools.name: slack_post_message
tools.description: Post a message to a Slack channel through the connected bot. The bot must already be a member of the target channel — if not, Slack returns `not_in_channel` and the user has to invite the bot via `/invite @<botname>`. Posts as the bot, not the user.

params.name: channel
params.description: Channel id (preferred — e.g. C0123ABCD) or name with `#` prefix.

params.name: text
params.description: Message text. Slack mrkdwn formatting is supported.

params.name: thread_ts
params.description: Optional parent message timestamp to reply in a thread instead of the channel.

params.name: team_id
params.description: Optional Slack workspace id (T…) to act in, from slack_list_workspaces. Omit to use the default workspace (the one connected most recently). Also names the workspace inside an Enterprise Grid org-wide install.

tools.name: slack_update_manager
tools.description: Change an AI Slack manager. Fields mean what they do on slack_create_manager; omitted ones stay. playbook REPLACES it, playbook_append adds to it. The owner never changes. Switching on spends credits — confirm first. Owners/admins only.

params.name: manager_id
params.description: From slack_list_managers.

tools.name: sms_send_alert
tools.description: Text a workspace member. COSTS MONEY per message and reaches a real phone, so use it only for things that genuinely warrant interrupting someone — an outage, a same-day deadline, an urgent approval — and prefer a notification or email otherwise. It reaches ONLY members who verified a number and consented; for anyone else it reports that and sends nothing, which is not an error to retry. Quiet hours are enforced. Keep the message under 140 characters: longer texts are split and billed per segment, and one emoji more than halves the limit.

params.name: member_email
params.description: Email of the workspace member to text.

params.name: message
params.description: The text to send. Plain language, no markdown — it renders raw on a phone. Say who it is from and what to do.

tools.name: snooze_detected_activity
tools.description: Snooze one of the caller's own tasks that is blocked (waiting on a review, an external party, a vendor, or a dependency), recording the blocker so it surfaces in their capture queue. The task must belong to the caller's workspace and the snooze is recorded under the CURRENT user only.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Id of the task to snooze. Must belong to the caller's workspace.

params.name: blocker_kind
params.description: What kind of blocker is holding the task. Defaults to 'other'.

params.name: blocked_by
params.description: Free-text note on who or what the task is blocked by.

params.name: unsnooze_when
params.description: Human-readable note on when the task should resume (e.g. 'after design review').

params.name: snoozed_until
params.description: Optional ISO 8601 timestamp to auto-mark the snooze ready.

tools.name: snooze_notification
tools.description: Snooze (or un-snooze) a notification for the current user.

tools.name: snooze_notification_until
tools.description: Snooze a notification until a specific ISO timestamp, or pass snooze_until=null to clear the snooze. Use this when the user says 'snooze until Friday 2pm' rather than the boolean toggle.

params.name: snooze_until
params.description: ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g. 2026-06-04T14:00:00Z). Pass null to clear.

tools.name: soundgen_clone_voice
tools.description: Clone a voice from 1–25 audio samples. Pass a human-readable `name` and an array of publicly reachable `audio_urls`. Returns a `voice_id` once training completes (2–5 minutes). DESTRUCTIVE: a cloned voice can be used to impersonate the source speaker — confirm consent before calling.

params.name: name
params.description: Display name for the cloned voice.

params.name: audio_urls
params.description: 1–25 publicly reachable audio sample URLs.

params.name: description
params.description: Optional description shown alongside the voice.

tools.name: soundgen_generate_music
tools.description: Start an AI music generation job from a text prompt. Returns a `generation_id` you can poll with `soundgen_get_generation`. Async — typical wall-clock is 10–30 seconds for short clips. The user pays per generation, so confirm the prompt before kicking off long durations.

params.name: prompt
params.description: Text description of the music to generate (min 3 chars). Example: 'upbeat electronic track with synth arpeggios'.

params.name: duration
params.description: Duration in seconds (5–300, default 30).

params.name: bpm
params.description: Beats per minute (40–240, default 120).

params.name: genre
params.description: Target genre — use `soundgen_list_genres` for valid slugs.

params.name: key
params.description: Musical key (e.g. C, Am, G). Default C.

params.name: model
params.description: AI model id. Default 'soundgen-v1'.

tools.name: soundgen_get_generation
tools.description: Check the status of one SoundGen generation. Returns `status` ('processing' | 'completed' | 'failed') and — once completed — a downloadable `result_url`. Poll this after `soundgen_generate_music` until status is terminal.

params.name: id
params.description: Generation id returned by `soundgen_generate_music`.

tools.name: soundgen_get_project
tools.description: Fetch details of one public SoundGen project: tracks, BPM, key, duration, tags, settings. Use after `soundgen_list_projects` to drill in.

params.name: id
params.description: SoundGen project UUID.

tools.name: soundgen_get_sound
tools.description: Fetch one SoundGen sound by id, including its file_url, waveform_url, BPM, key, duration, tags, and engagement counts. Use after `soundgen_list_sounds` to drill into a track.

params.name: id
params.description: SoundGen sound UUID.

tools.name: soundgen_get_stats
tools.description: Platform-level SoundGen stats: total sounds, total projects, top genres, API version. Use for 'how big is the library' style answers.

tools.name: soundgen_list_generations
tools.description: List the calling user's SoundGen generation history. Use to find a prior `generation_id` or surface 'my recent generations'.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max rows (1–100, default 20).

params.name: offset
params.description: Pagination offset (default 0).

tools.name: soundgen_list_genres
tools.description: List every genre slug SoundGen knows about (~6 today). Cheap and unauthenticated — use to validate a `genre` value before passing it to `soundgen_list_sounds` or `soundgen_generate_music`.

tools.name: soundgen_list_projects
tools.description: Browse public SoundGen projects — collections of tracks with metadata. Useful for 'show me example arrangements in genre X' workflows.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max projects (1–100, default 20).

params.name: offset
params.description: Pagination offset (default 0).

tools.name: soundgen_list_sounds
tools.description: Browse the SoundGen sound library. Supports genre filter, featured-only, free-text search across title/artist/description, and pagination. Use to surface tracks the user can drop into a project or reference in a brief.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max sounds to return (1–100, default 20).

params.name: offset
params.description: Pagination offset (default 0).

params.name: genre
params.description: Filter by genre slug (e.g. 'electronic', 'ambient').

params.name: featured
params.description: Return only featured sounds.

params.name: search
params.description: Free-text search across title, artist, description.

tools.name: soundgen_list_voices
tools.description: List voices available for text-to-speech, including SoundGen's built-in voices and any the user has cloned. Returns voice ids the user can pass to `soundgen_synthesize_speech`.

tools.name: soundgen_separate_stems
tools.description: Split an audio file into individual stems (vocals, drums, bass, etc.). Pass a publicly reachable `audio_url`. Returns a `separation_id` for tracking; SoundGen typically takes ~30 seconds. Async — the result URLs land on the row when status reaches 'completed' (poll via the generations surface or wait for a webhook).

params.name: audio_url
params.description: Publicly reachable URL of the audio file to process.

params.name: stems
params.description: Which stems to extract. Defaults to vocals/drums/bass/other when omitted.

tools.name: soundgen_synthesize_speech
tools.description: Convert text to speech using a SoundGen voice. Returns a `synthesis_id` that resolves to an audio file URL when done (~1s). Text is capped at 5000 chars.

params.name: text
params.description: Text to synthesize (max 5000 chars).

params.name: voice_id
params.description: Voice id from `soundgen_list_voices` (built-in or cloned).

params.name: output_format
params.description: Audio container. Default mp3.

tools.name: split_time_entry
tools.description: Break one recorded block into several billable lines — 'that 2 hours was 0.5 reviewing exhibits, 1.0 drafting, 0.5 on the call'. Each part gets its own task, narrative and rounded quantity, and replaces the original entry. Refuses an entry that is already invoiced or still running. Confirm the breakdown with the user first: the original entry is replaced.

params.name: entry_id
params.description: The time entry to split.

params.name: parts
params.description: Two or more parts. Their durations need not sum to the original — rounding each line up legitimately exceeds it.

tools.name: staff_deal_team
tools.description: Put the people the user confirmed onto a deal's team — ADDITIVE: adds each member (title 'Analyst' unless given) and sets the lead ONLY if the deal has no active lead; it never removes anyone and never replaces a lead (use update_deal_team for that). Each person is resolved against the workspace's ACTIVE members (email, exact name, then a unique name prefix) and all must resolve or nothing changes. The people added are emailed and pushed that they are on the deal, and — when the deal already has a Slack channel / Drive folder — invited to them through YOUR Slack and Google connections. Those invites and notices cannot be recalled; the undo takes back only the roster change. Run suggest_deal_team first, show the proposal, and only call this for the people the user agreed to. May park for approval.

params.name: deal_id
params.description: The deal's id, as list_deals prints it.

params.name: members
params.description: People to add (name, email or user id each) — usually the ones suggest_deal_team proposed and the user kept.

params.name: lead
params.description: Name, email or user id of the lead, used only when the deal has no active lead.

params.name: title
params.description: What the added members do on this deal. Default 'Analyst'. Up to 80 characters.

params.name: invite_to_space
params.description: Invite them to the deal's existing Slack channel / Drive folder. Default true.

tools.name: start_focus_session
tools.description: Start a Focus Mode session for the caller themselves. Any existing active session for the caller is closed first. Duration is clamped to 5–480 minutes. This only ever starts the CURRENT user's own session — you cannot start a session for anyone else.

params.name: duration_min
params.description: Session length in minutes (5–480). Defaults to 90.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Optional id of a task in this workspace to attach the session to. Must belong to the caller's workspace.

tools.name: start_investor_campaign
tools.description: Run the investor funnel for a deal in one call: ranks the workspace's investors against the deal's investment profile (if it has never been ranked), releases the next tranche of firms, picks the best person at each (warmest with an email first, then the most senior title), links them to the deal and enrolls them in a DEAL cadence. Refuses when the deal has no investment profile and says what to run (get_deal_space, drive_read_file, set_deal_investment_profile). Returns a SOURCING GAP list — released firms with no contact who has an email — so you can find people there with search_prospects and unlock_prospect_email and run this again: a re-run while a tranche is open releases nothing and only enrolls firms nobody has written to yet. A firm is marked approached automatically once a step has actually been SENT to someone there on this deal. auto_release (default false, stored on the deal) lets the 6-hourly scan release and enroll the next tranche once every released firm is approached or dismissed. This ARMS UNATTENDED OUTBOUND EMAIL to up to 200 investors per call through your mailbox — confirm the cadence, tranche size and auto_release with the user first.

params.name: cadence
params.description: Deal cadence id or exact name. Optional on a re-run: the campaign's stored cadence is reused.

params.name: batch_size
params.description: Firms per tranche, 1-200. Default 100 (or the campaign's stored size).

params.name: contacts_per_firm
params.description: People enrolled per firm, 1-3. Default 1.

params.name: auto_release
params.description: Release and enroll the next tranche automatically once this one is worked. Default false; omitted keeps the stored setting.

params.name: provider
params.description: Send provider. Defaults to auto.

tools.name: start_issuer_campaign
tools.description: Run the issuer funnel for a campaign in one call: ranks the workspace's issuers against the mandate (if never ranked), releases the next tranche of firms, picks the best person at each (warmest with an email first, then the most senior title), and enrolls them in a NETWORK cadence stamped with this campaign. Refuses without a mandate (themes/sectors) and says what to run. Returns a SOURCING GAP list — released firms with nobody who has an email — so you can find people there with search_prospects and unlock_prospect_email and run this again: a re-run while a tranche is open releases nothing and only enrolls firms nobody has written to yet. A firm is marked approached automatically once a step has actually been SENT to someone there, and ENGAGED once anyone there replies or takes a meeting. auto_release (default false, stored on the campaign) lets the 6-hourly scan release and enroll the next tranche once every released firm is approached, engaged or dismissed. This ARMS UNATTENDED OUTBOUND EMAIL to up to 200 prospects per call through your mailbox — confirm the cadence, tranche size and auto_release with the user first.

params.name: campaign
params.description: Campaign id or exact name.

params.name: cadence
params.description: NETWORK cadence id or exact name. Optional when the campaign already has one.

params.name: batch_size
params.description: Firms per tranche, 1-200. Default 100 (or the campaign's stored size).

params.name: contacts_per_firm
params.description: People enrolled per firm, 1-3. Default 1.

params.name: auto_release
params.description: Release and enroll the next tranche automatically once this one is worked. Default false; omitted keeps the stored setting.

params.name: provider
params.description: Send provider. Defaults to auto.

tools.name: start_runbook
tools.description: Begin executing a runbook. Returns a run id and the FIRST step to perform. Do the step's work with your other tools, then call advance_runbook to record it done and get the next step. Continue until the run completes.

params.name: runbook
params.description: Runbook id or exact name.

tools.name: start_setup_interview
tools.description: Begin an interview that asks the user a short series of questions to fill a piece of workspace config, then stages a draft for their review. Returns the interview id and the first question — ask it, then feed the user's reply to record_interview_answer. Only offer this; never start it unprompted mid-conversation. Topics: 'kvn_charter' (the company Know-how / Vision / Negation), 'team_context' (who's who, for assignment).

params.name: topic
params.description: Which config the interview fills.

tools.name: start_timer
tools.description: Start a running timer for a project (and optional task) for the current user (or a named actor).

params.name: actor_name
params.description: Override actor name (defaults to current user)

tools.name: stop_cadence_enrollment
tools.description: Stop a contact's active cadence on a deal. Future steps are cancelled; already-sent emails are unaffected.

tools.name: stop_investor_campaign
tools.description: Stop a deal's investor campaign: auto-release is turned off and the cadence detached, so nothing more is released or enrolled automatically. Pass stop_enrollments to also cancel every ACTIVE sequence to the deal's investor contacts (future steps and any already-queued send; mail already sent stays sent). The ranking and tranche state are kept.

params.name: stop_enrollments
params.description: Also stop the active investor sequences on this deal. Default false.

tools.name: stop_issuer_campaign
tools.description: Stop an issuer campaign: auto-release is turned off and the cadence detached, so nothing more is released or enrolled automatically. Pass stop_enrollments to also cancel every ACTIVE sequence this campaign started (future steps and any already-queued send; mail already sent stays sent). The mandate, ranking and tranche state are kept; pass archive to retire the campaign entirely.

params.name: campaign
params.description: Campaign id or exact name.

params.name: stop_enrollments
params.description: Also stop this campaign's active sequences. Default false.

params.name: archive
params.description: Archive the campaign after stopping it. Default false.

tools.name: stop_network_cadence_enrollment
tools.description: Stop a contact's active NETWORK cadence. Future steps are cancelled and any already-queued send is pulled back; already-sent emails are unaffected.

tools.name: stop_timer
tools.description: Stop a running timer. Provide entry_id, or actor_name to stop that user's most recent open entry.

tools.name: stripe_create_customer
tools.description: Create a customer record on the connected Stripe account. This creates NO charge and takes no money — it is the address-book entry a future invoice or subscription attaches to. For a customer in Kavanah's own CRM use `create_client` instead; the two are separate records.

params.name: name
params.description: Customer or company name.

params.name: email
params.description: Customer email address.

params.name: description
params.description: Optional internal note.

tools.name: stripe_create_invoice
tools.description: Create a DRAFT invoice on the connected Stripe account: one or more line items, then the invoice itself. Nobody is charged and nothing is emailed — the draft sits in Stripe until someone calls `stripe_send_invoice` or issues it from the dashboard. Every agent-created invoice is set to collect by EMAIL, never by automatically charging a saved card, so issuing one is always a request the customer must act on. Amounts are given in the MAJOR unit of the currency (20.50 means $20.50, not 2050). Use `stripe_list_customers` for the customer id.

params.name: customer_id
params.description: Stripe customer id (cus_…).

params.name: line_items
params.description: Line items. Give EITHER `amount` + `currency` for an ad-hoc charge, OR `price_id` for a catalog price — not both.

params.name: days_until_due
params.description: Payment terms in days. Default 30.

params.name: description
params.description: Optional memo on the invoice.

tools.name: stripe_create_payment_link
tools.description: Create a Stripe Payment Link — a reusable public URL that takes real money from anyone who opens it. Requires a `price_id` from stripe_list_products. ALWAYS confirm the exact price with the user before creating one, and quote the price back to them: the link cannot be edited afterwards, only deactivated in the Stripe dashboard, and anyone holding the URL can pay through it.

params.name: price_id
params.description: Stripe price id (price_…) to sell. Get one from stripe_list_products.

params.name: quantity
params.description: Quantity of that price per purchase. Default 1.

tools.name: stripe_create_refund
tools.description: Refund a Stripe charge — this MOVES REAL MONEY back to the customer and cannot be undone from Kavanah or from Stripe. Requires a charge id (ch_… or py_…) from stripe_list_charges. Omit `amount` for a full refund; pass it for a partial one, in the MAJOR unit of the charge's currency (20.50 means $20.50, not 2050). NEVER call this without the user explicitly confirming the charge id and the amount in the same turn. This tool is only available when a workspace admin has turned on Stripe money movement in Settings → AI Agent.

params.name: charge_id
params.description: Stripe charge id (ch_… / py_…) from stripe_list_charges.

params.name: amount
params.description: Partial refund amount in the charge's MAJOR currency unit (e.g. 20.50 for $20.50). Omit to refund the charge in full.

params.name: reason
params.description: Optional Stripe refund reason.

tools.name: stripe_create_subscription
tools.description: Start a recurring subscription for an existing Stripe customer. THIS BEGINS BILLING: Stripe charges the customer's stored payment method on the price's schedule, starting immediately unless you pass `trial_days`. Requires a `price_id` from stripe_list_products and a customer who already has a payment method on file. ALWAYS confirm the customer, the price and the amount with the user before calling. This tool is only available when a workspace admin has turned on Stripe money movement in Settings → AI Agent.

params.name: customer_id
params.description: Stripe customer id (cus_…).

params.name: price_id
params.description: Recurring Stripe price id (price_…) from stripe_list_products.

params.name: quantity
params.description: Quantity of that price. Default 1.

params.name: trial_days
params.description: Optional free-trial length in days before the first charge.

tools.name: stripe_get_account
tools.description: Show the connected Stripe account: business name, country, default currency, whether charges and payouts are enabled, and — importantly — whether the connected key is LIVE or TEST mode. Call this first when a Stripe number looks wrong or empty: a test-mode key reads a separate, usually near-empty dataset, so "no revenue" often means "test key", not "no sales".

tools.name: stripe_get_balance
tools.description: Current Stripe balance, split into available and pending, per currency. This is money Stripe is holding, NOT revenue and NOT the bank balance — funds sit pending until they settle and then leave on the payout schedule. Use stripe_revenue_summary for what the business earned.

tools.name: stripe_get_customer
tools.description: Fetch one Stripe customer by id (cus_…), with their active subscriptions. Get an id from stripe_list_customers.

params.name: customer_id
params.description: Stripe customer id (cus_…).

tools.name: stripe_get_invoice
tools.description: Fetch one Stripe invoice by id (in_…), including its totals, status, and the hosted invoice + PDF links you can give the customer.

params.name: invoice_id
params.description: Stripe invoice id (in_…).

tools.name: stripe_list_charges
tools.description: List payments (charges) on the connected account, newest first. Optionally filter to one customer or to charges created in the last N days. Amounts are reported in the charge's own currency; refunds are shown against the original charge.

params.name: customer_id
params.description: Optional Stripe customer id (cus_…).

params.name: days
params.description: Only charges created in the last N days. Default: no date filter.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: stripe_list_customers
tools.description: List customers on the connected Stripe account, newest first. `email` filters by EXACT address — Stripe's list endpoint has no substring or name search, so a partial email or a company name finds nothing. For Kavanah's own client records use `list_clients` instead.

params.name: email
params.description: Exact email address to filter by (not a partial match).

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: stripe_list_invoices
tools.description: List Stripe invoices, newest first. Filter by `status` (draft, open, paid, uncollectible, void) or by customer. "open" is the one to use for unpaid/outstanding invoices — a draft has not been sent to anyone and must not be described as owed.

params.name: status
params.description: Invoice status filter.

params.name: customer_id
params.description: Optional Stripe customer id (cus_…).

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: stripe_list_products
tools.description: List products in the Stripe catalog with their default price ids. Use this to find the `price_…` id that stripe_create_payment_link needs.

params.name: include_inactive
params.description: Include archived products. Default false (active only).

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: stripe_list_subscriptions
tools.description: List Stripe subscriptions with their status, price items and renewal date. Defaults to `active`; pass "all" to include cancelled and past-due ones. `cancel_at_period_end` is the churn signal — a subscription can be status "active" and already scheduled to end.

params.name: status
params.description: active | past_due | trialing | canceled | unpaid | all. Default: active.

params.name: customer_id
params.description: Optional Stripe customer id (cus_…).

params.name: limit
params.description: Max results to return. Default 25, capped at 100.

tools.name: stripe_revenue_summary
tools.description: The headline revenue picture: estimated monthly recurring revenue (MRR) from active subscriptions, net charge volume over a recent window, and current balance — each reported PER CURRENCY, never summed across currencies (there is no exchange rate here and inventing one would invent revenue). MRR is an ESTIMATE from list prices: it normalises every interval to a month and ignores discounts, coupons, taxes, proration and trials. It also CANNOT price metered (usage-based) or tiered subscriptions, so those are counted and reported separately — if that count is non-zero, say so when quoting the figure rather than presenting the total as complete.

params.name: days
params.description: Window in days for the charge-volume half of the summary. Default 30, capped at 365.

tools.name: stripe_send_invoice
tools.description: Finalize a DRAFT Stripe invoice and EMAIL it to the customer. This is the moment the invoice becomes a real demand for payment and leaves the building — it cannot be un-sent, and finalizing also locks the amounts. Confirm the invoice id and its total with the user before calling. Nobody is charged by this; the customer receives a payment link and chooses to pay.

params.name: invoice_id
params.description: Stripe invoice id (in_…) from stripe_create_invoice or stripe_list_invoices.

tools.name: submit_app_for_review
tools.description: Submit a version of an owned app for platform review, the first step toward PUBLIC marketplace listing. Only a draft or previously-rejected version can be submitted; approval and listing are a Kavanah operator decision, not something this call grants. Defaults to the latest version. A private app that only this workspace uses never needs this.

params.name: slug
params.description: The app's slug.

params.name: version
params.description: Optional semver of the version to submit. Defaults to the latest.

tools.name: submit_availability
tools.description: Submit (or update) the current user's availability. Pass request_id to respond to a specific ask, or omit it for a 'standing' entry that captures ongoing availability. Latest submission wins.

params.name: request_id
params.description: Optional. Omit for standing entry.

params.name: period_start
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD; required for standing entry.

params.name: period_end
params.description: YYYY-MM-DD; required for standing entry.

tools.name: submit_feature_request
tools.description: Submit a new feature request on behalf of the caller. Any workspace member may submit; the submission is attributed to the caller. Use this when the user wants a capability, integration, or improvement Kavanah doesn't have today — including when YOU had to tell them you can't do something. ALWAYS ask first ("Want me to file that as a feature request?") and call this only after they agree. Requests land on the public board at Settings → Feature Requests where others can upvote them. Not for bugs — something broken is record_bug_report.

params.name: title
params.description: Short title (max 140 chars).

params.name: description
params.description: Full description of the request (max 4000 chars).

params.name: category
params.description: Category. Defaults to 'general'.

tools.name: suggest_cadence_variants
tools.description: Evidence for writing subject lines and choosing sender names for a NEW cadence, from this workspace's past campaigns: the automatic winner decisions on record (with the arms they beat), first-touch subject arms ranked by reply rate with their contact counts, which subject traits went with higher reply rates (question, uses the name, names the deal, a number, five words or fewer), and sender names by reply rate. Use it before create_deal_cadence, then propose 2–4 subject_variants that CITE the evidence (e.g. 'questions replied 6.1% vs 3.4% over 420 contacts'). Arms from linked cadences with a sender pool are flagged as confounded. Reports nothing as a pattern below 20 contacts per arm.

tools.name: suggest_deal_team
tools.description: Propose who should staff a deal — read-only, changes nothing, costs no AI usage. Ranks the workspace's active members for the ANALYST seat (and for the LEAD seat when the deal has no active lead) on their job title (Analyst/Associate fits the analyst seat; Director/VP/MD/Partner the lead), their skill profile (finance, analytics, research, data; biz-dev and strategy for a lead), their experience against the deal's sector / category / stage / geography, their own reported availability (unavailable people are listed but never proposed), and how many open deals and task hours they already carry. Says how many members the team needs to reach the workspace's minimum size (default 5) and proposes up to its maximum (default 10), each with the reasons. Show the proposal and let the user choose; staff_deal_team writes it.

params.name: deal_id
params.description: The deal's id, as list_deals prints it.

tools.name: suggest_task_eta
tools.description: Suggest a data-backed due date + confidence for a planned task, computed from the workspace's historical completion times (optionally filtered by tag and/or assignee). Use this instead of guessing a due date. Read-only, no LLM.

params.name: tag
params.description: Optional tag to match a cohort of similar past tasks.

params.name: assignee
params.description: Optional assignee name to match that person's velocity.

params.name: start_date
params.description: Optional start date (YYYY-MM-DD) the ETA is measured from. Defaults to today.

tools.name: suggest_task_split
tools.description: Check whether an existing task actually bundles two+ independent deliverables that should be tracked separately, and if so suggest standalone titles. Different from decompose_task (which expands ONE deliverable into subtasks) — this SPLITS a task into peers. Returns a preview; commit with create_task.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Id of the task in this workspace to evaluate for splitting.

params.name: force
params.description: Skip the cheap pre-filter and always run the LLM check. Default false.

tools.name: surface_false_friend
tools.description: Append a false-friend to a project's KVN charter — an approach that looks correct but sits in the negation space. Use when reviewing a proposed approach, when the user explicitly names a pattern that should be refused, or when a task you almost recommended would have crossed a boundary. The agent will check every subsequent task in this project against this list.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project to add the false friend to.

params.name: approach
params.description: Short label for the approach being refused.

params.name: why_wrong
params.description: Why this approach sits in the negation space (1–2 sentences).

tools.name: sweep_project_for_false_friends
tools.description: Audit every open task in a project against its KVN charter and report which ones have drifted — tasks that resemble the Vision but serve a proxy for it, or that sit in the Negation space. This is the charter-drift review: use it when the user asks whether a project is still on-mission, during a quarterly/charter review, or when a project 'feels busy but not productive'. Bounded to the most recent open tasks. Costs one model call per task, so do not call it casually on a large project.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: Project to sweep.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max open tasks to check, newest first. Default 40, capped at 100.

tools.name: sync_angelsend_audience
tools.description: Reconcile the Deal Room's contacts and opt-outs with AngelSend's, so the two are one audience rather than two lists that drift. `direction` picks what runs: - 'optouts_in' (the default, and the safe one) — pull AngelSend's do-not-email list into this workspace's suppression list. Run this before any campaign. Until it has run, a person who unsubscribed from an AngelSend campaign still receives Kavanah cadence steps, because the two lists never met. - 'optouts_out' — push this workspace's own opt-outs to AngelSend. - 'contacts_in' — pull an AngelSend segment (or the whole lead list) into the Deal Room as contacts. GAP-FILLING: it never overwrites a field a person curated here. - 'contacts_out' — push Deal Room contacts into an AngelSend project as leads. Note this direction OVERWRITES the whole AngelSend row, because import-leads has no partial form: a field Kavanah does not hold is blanked there. Opted-out addresses are excluded, since importing one is how an opt-out gets quietly undone. Each direction runs on its own. Do not describe running one as having synced the audience.

params.name: direction
params.description: Which reconciliation to run. Defaults to optouts_in.

params.name: project_id
params.description: AngelSend project. Required for contacts_out.

params.name: segment_id
params.description: Segment to pull for contacts_in. Omit for the whole lead list.

params.name: limit
params.description: Rows to pull for contacts_in. Default 200, capped at 500.

tools.name: sync_angelsend_campaign_mirror
tools.description: Run the AngelSend campaign mirror now instead of waiting for the 10-minute sweep: removes stopped/suppressed recipients from AngelSend, reads sends/replies/unsubscribes back, re-verifies the archive copy, and hands new enrollments to AngelSend (which then emails them). Admin only.

params.name: deal_id
params.description: For a deal cadence: which deal's campaign.

tools.name: sync_client_sheet
tools.description: Run a two-way sync between the workspace's client list and its linked Google Sheet, using the saved column mapping. Pulls the source tab in (matching clients by company), then — only if the mirror is enabled — writes Kavanah's client directory out to a SEPARATE mirror tab. The original tab is never written to.

tools.name: sync_deal_sheet
tools.description: Run a two-way sync between a pipeline and its linked Google Sheet, using the column mapping saved by the original import. Pulls the source tab in (creating/updating deals and contacts), then — only if the mirror is enabled — writes Kavanah's canonical state out to a SEPARATE mirror tab. The team's original tab is never written to. Requires an existing link (see get_deal_sheet_link); establishing one needs the /deals/import wizard.

params.name: pipeline
params.description: Pipeline id or slug. Defaults to the workspace default pipeline.

tools.name: sync_network_sheet
tools.description: Run the network sheet sync now instead of waiting for the hourly job: re-import (gap-filling) and, when the mirror is on, rewrite the mirror tab with Kavanah's whole network. WRITES TO THE CUSTOMER'S SPREADSHEET when the mirror is armed. Pass link_id when more than one sheet is linked; omit it to sync every linked sheet.

params.name: link_id
params.description: One link; omit for all.

tools.name: teams_list_channel_messages
tools.description: List recent messages in a Microsoft Teams channel. Returns sender, text, and time. Read-only. Reading channel messages requires the workspace admin to have granted the ChannelMessage.Read.All scope.

params.name: team_id
params.description: The team id from `teams_list_teams`.

params.name: channel_id
params.description: The channel id from `teams_list_channels`.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max messages to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 50.

tools.name: teams_list_channels
tools.description: List the channels in a Microsoft Teams team. Returns channel id, name, and type. Call this to get a channel id before reading or posting messages.

params.name: team_id
params.description: The team id from `teams_list_teams`.

tools.name: teams_list_chats
tools.description: List the user's Microsoft Teams 1:1 and group chats (most recent first), with their id, topic, and members. Call this to get a chat id before sending a chat message. Read-only.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max chats to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 50.

tools.name: teams_list_teams
tools.description: List the Microsoft Teams the user is a member of, with their id + display name. Call this first to get a team id before listing channels.

tools.name: teams_send_channel_message
tools.description: Post a message to a Microsoft Teams channel as the user. Confirm the destination channel with the user before posting to an unfamiliar channel.

params.name: team_id
params.description: The team id from `teams_list_teams`.

params.name: channel_id
params.description: The channel id from `teams_list_channels`.

params.name: text
params.description: Message text to send.

tools.name: teams_send_chat_message
tools.description: Send a message to a Microsoft Teams 1:1 or group chat as the user. Confirm the destination chat with the user before sending to an unfamiliar chat.

params.name: chat_id
params.description: The chat id from `teams_list_chats`.

params.name: text
params.description: Message text to send.

tools.name: telegram_bot_link_hint
tools.description: Return the workspace bot's @username and the canonical https://t.me/<bot> URL without rotating any tokens. Useful when the user just wants to know how to reach the bot.

tools.name: telegram_get_me
tools.description: Confirm the workspace's Telegram bot is reachable and return its identity (username + id). Use this before suggesting a Telegram action to verify the integration is wired up.

tools.name: telegram_link_status
tools.description: Report whether the calling user is linked to a Telegram chat through the workspace's bot. Returns the chat id / Telegram username when connected, or hints at the binding flow when not. Use as a first step in any 'ping me on Telegram' conversation.

tools.name: telegram_request_link
tools.description: Issue (or re-issue) a Telegram deep link the calling user can click to bind their Kavanah account to a Telegram chat. Returns a `https://t.me/<bot>?start=<token>` URL plus the raw `/start <token>` paste fallback. If the user is already connected, returns the existing chat instead of rotating it.

tools.name: telegram_send_message
tools.description: Send a Telegram message via the workspace's bot. Defaults to the calling user's own linked chat (so 'ping me on Telegram' works), or pass `chat_id` to target a specific chat. Requires the user to have linked their Telegram account via Settings → Integrations.

params.name: text
params.description: Message body. Plain text. Telegram caps this at ~4096 chars.

params.name: chat_id
params.description: Optional Telegram chat id. Omit to send to the calling user's own linked chat.

tools.name: telegram_unlink
tools.description: Revoke the calling user's Telegram link. Future messages from that chat will be rejected with a /start prompt. Confirm with the user before calling — they will need to re-bind via telegram_request_link.

tools.name: telegram_webhook_info
tools.description: Show the workspace bot's webhook configuration: delivery URL, pending update count, last error (if any). Useful for debugging 'why aren't my Telegram messages arriving?' incidents.

tools.name: test_app_tool
tools.description: Send ONE signed test call to an owned app's tool endpoint and return exactly what it answered: HTTP status, latency, body, whether the call was signed, and whether the input matched the tool's schema. The payload is the same shape a real agent call sends, plus test:true and an X-Kavanah-Test header, so the app's real handler RUNS — do not test a tool whose side effect the user would not want. Requires the app to be installed here with a signing secret minted (in production an install without one is refused rather than called unsigned). Read the answer literally: 401 means the secret on the user's server does not match, 404 means their server has no handler for that tool name, a network error means the endpoint is down or private.

params.name: slug
params.description: The app's slug.

params.name: tool_name
params.description: The tool's LOCAL name as declared in the manifest (e.g. 'create_deal', not 'app__acme__create_deal').

params.name: input_json
params.description: The tool input as a JSON object string. Defaults to {}.

tools.name: toggle_automation
tools.description: Enable or disable an automation rule without changing its config.

tools.name: toggle_discussion_star
tools.description: Star or unstar a discussion thread.

tools.name: toggle_subtask
tools.description: Toggle (or set) the completed state of a single subtask on a task.

params.name: completed
params.description: Optional explicit value; toggles if omitted

tools.name: track_waiting_on
tools.description: Record that someone owes a deliverable or answer, so the agent chases it later. Call this whenever you delegate work, assign a task that needs a response, or ask a person for input you'll need. One entry per obligation.

params.name: waiting_on
params.description: Who owes it — a workspace member's display name (preferred) or an email address.

params.name: description
params.description: What they owe, self-contained (e.g. 'Security review of the auth PR, promised in standup').

params.name: due_date
params.description: When it's due (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit if no deadline was agreed.

params.name: related_task_id
params.description: Optional Kavanah task id this obligation is attached to.

tools.name: triage_task_candidate
tools.description: Resolve one candidate. action='accept' creates the real task from it (optionally edit title/description/project/assignee/subtasks first). action='dismiss' closes it with a reason: 'out_of_scope' (crosses a Negation — pass matched_negation with the charter line so it records a negation hit), 'no_checkable_outcome' (a topic, not a task), 'duplicate', 'premature' (needs an owner/spec first), or 'other'. Only do this when the user asks you to triage; otherwise propose_task_candidate and let a human decide.

params.name: candidate_id
params.description: The candidate's id (from list_task_candidates).

params.name: title
params.description: accept: override the title.

params.name: description
params.description: accept: override the description.

params.name: project_ref
params.description: accept: place the task in this project.

params.name: assigned_to
params.description: accept: assign to this member name.

params.name: subtasks
params.description: accept: checkable sub-steps.

params.name: reason
params.description: dismiss: why. Required when action='dismiss'.

params.name: matched_negation
params.description: dismiss + out_of_scope: the exact Negation charter line the candidate crosses.

params.name: note
params.description: dismiss: optional free-text note.

tools.name: twin_brief_meeting
tools.description: Before a meeting the twin's owner cannot attend: what they would want raised, asked and protected, grounded in their own indexed work and the deal context. Use this to prepare whoever IS attending. This is the around-the-meeting route; sending the owner's twin INTO a Kavanah call is a separate thing the owner does from the call controls.

params.name: topic
params.description: What the meeting is about.

params.name: deal_id
params.description: Optional deal, to ground on its history and contacts.

params.name: attendees
params.description: Who will be there.

tools.name: twin_respond_to_meeting
tools.description: After a meeting the twin's owner missed: read the transcript and give their response — what they would have said, where they would disagree, what they want followed up, and a draft reply to the participants. Grounded in their indexed work, and explicit about anything it cannot judge on their behalf. Requires a recorded meeting with a finished transcript.

params.name: meeting_id
params.description: The recorded meeting to read.

params.name: focus
params.description: Optional: what the owner most cares about.

tools.name: unbill_time_entries
tools.description: Clear the invoiced stamp (invoice reference + invoiced-at) from every time entry billed under a given ClearBooks invoice reference, making that time billable again — the local inverse for a voided or deleted draft. Does NOT touch ClearBooks itself; void or delete the invoice there separately (clearbooks_void_invoice / clearbooks_delete_invoice). Admin only.

params.name: invoice_ref
params.description: The ClearBooks invoice id the entries were stamped with.

tools.name: undo_last_action
tools.description: Pop the top undoable action off the calling user's stack and run its inverse. Only supports trash-style mutations on clients, projects, and tasks (the same set the Cmd+Z UI handles). The matching redo entry is pushed onto the redo stack, so the action can be re-applied with redo_last_action. Destructive in the sense that it changes data — confirm with the user before calling it for anything non-obvious.

tools.name: uninstall_app
tools.description: Uninstall a community app from this workspace. This revokes every API key the app holds and destroys its signing secret immediately, so the app can no longer call Kavanah or verify calls from it; re-installing later means minting a new secret and redeploying the app with it. The app's definition (for an app this workspace built) is kept. Confirm with the user before calling.

params.name: slug
params.description: The installed app's slug.

tools.name: unlink_network_sheet
tools.description: Stop syncing a sheet with the network: the hourly import and mirror stop for it. Nothing already imported is removed, and the sheet itself is not touched. Relinking the same tab later picks up where it left off. Undoable.

params.name: link_id
params.description: Required when more than one sheet is linked.

tools.name: unlock_prospect_email
tools.description: Obtain a verified email address for ONE person. THIS SPENDS MONEY — roughly $0.02 per contact on ppl.contact, or a plan credit on Apollo or Hunter. Providers are tried cheapest-first and the first real address wins. Pass the record id from search_prospects when you have one; otherwise a name plus a company domain. Confirm with the user before unlocking in bulk, and tell them the expected cost. A record that comes back with no address still may have cost a credit.

params.name: external_id
params.description: Record id from search_prospects. The cheapest and most accurate route.

params.name: company_domain
params.description: Required when there is no external_id — Hunter cannot work without it.

params.name: save_contact
params.description: Write the result into the workspace as a deal contact, linked to its firm. Default true — an unlocked address you did not save is money spent for nothing.

tools.name: unpublish_document
tools.description: Remove a document's publication. The public token is invalidated immediately.

tools.name: update_agent_cost_settings
tools.description: Admin-only. Cost settings for unattended runs (schedules, AI-employee runs, automations, meetings). background_model: 'auto' (router picks the cheapest fit per run), a model id, or 'default'. auto_optimize_for: what auto optimizes for (chat + unattended). headless_daily_token_budget: daily token ceiling, null = none, 0 refused. PROPOSE first; apply only once the user agrees. Undoable.

params.name: background_model
params.description: 'auto', a model id, or 'default' (use the workspace model).

params.name: headless_daily_token_budget
params.description: Cost-weighted tokens per UTC day, or null for no ceiling.

tools.name: update_agent_schedule
tools.description: Change a scheduled autonomous run. Pass only the fields you want to change (name, prompt, frequency, hour_utc, minute_utc, day_of_week, day_of_month, autonomy_level, enabled, persona_id, model, only_when_tasks_for, task_gate, tasks_due_within_days). model 'auto' cuts a simple schedule's cost. To stop a reminder emailing when there's nothing for its person, set only_when_tasks_for to that person. Set enabled:false to pause without deleting. Set persona_id to make an existing schedule run as an AI Employee (e.g. one created before that employee existed), or to an empty string to run as the default agent again. Changing any timing field reschedules the next run. No undo: re-apply the reply's previous to revert.

params.name: schedule_id
params.description: The schedule id (from list_agent_schedules).

params.name: persona_id
